commonMistakes: Jerking the weight off the floor before building full lat tension.
Rounding the spine during the initial pull.
safetyNotes: Never allow your spinal column to round aggressively under maximal pulling loads.
contraindications: Acute lumbar disc herniation or untreated severe lower back pain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: back lever
steps: Lie back securely on the bench and grasp the bodyweight with hands slightly wider than shoulders.
Pull your shoulder blades together and plant both feet flat on the floor.
Lower the weight smoothly with elbows angled at roughly forty-five degrees.
Descend until the weight touches or hovers just above your chest.
Press the load back up powerfully until your arms reach full extension.
tips: Retract and depress your shoulder blades into the bench for solid shoulder stability.
Tuck your elbows at roughly forty-five degrees rather than flaring wide.
commonMistakes: Bouncing the weight off your sternum at the bottom.
Flaring your elbows wide at ninety degrees, placing high stress on the rotator cuff.
safetyNotes: Maintain a firm grip and verify bar collars are tightly clamped.
contraindications: Severe active rotator cuff impingement or acute AC joint sprain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: back pec stretch
steps: Assume a stable position holding the bodyweight with your spine kept neutral.
Retract your shoulder blades and brace your abdominal wall firmly.
Drive your elbows straight back to pull the weight smoothly toward your torso.
Pause for one second at peak contraction while squeezing your back muscles.
Lower the weight with deliberate control back to the starting stretch.
tips: Initiate the pull by retracting your shoulder blade before bending your elbow.
Think about driving your elbows straight back toward your hip pockets.
commonMistakes: Using aggressive torso momentum to fling the weight upward.
Shrugging your shoulders upward toward your ears during the pull.
safetyNotes: Keep your lower back flat and braced when rowing in bent-over postures.
contraindications: Acute lumbar radiculopathy aggravated by unsupported flexion.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Backstroke Lap Swimming
steps: Push off pool wall supine in horizontal streamline.
Flutter kick continuously with relaxed pointed toes.
Rotate torso to sweep arm straight out of water thumb first.
Catch water with pinky finger and drive down toward thigh.
Breathe continuously with one breath per arm stroke cycle.
tips: Keep hips high near water surface by looking up.
Rotate shoulders with each arm entry.
commonMistakes: Sitting in the water and letting hips sink low.
Bending knees excessively during kick.
safetyNotes: Count strokes to anticipate pool wall turn.
contraindications: Shoulder impingement.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Backward Drag
steps: Set up with your feet shoulder-width apart holding the bodyweight securely in position.
Brace your core and inhale deeply to build intra-abdominal pressure.
Hinge your hips back and bend your knees to lower under control.
Descend until your thighs reach parallel to the floor with knees tracking over toes.
Drive firmly through your midfoot and heels to return to standing lockout.
tips: Keep your chest proud and drive your knees outward in line with your toes.
Maintain full midfoot balance throughout the descent and ascent.
commonMistakes: Letting knees cave inward during the upward drive.
Allowing your lower back to round into pelvic wink at bottom depth.
safetyNotes: Always set safety spotter arms just below your target depth before loading heavy weights.
contraindications: Avoid heavy spinal loading during acute lumbar disc flare-ups or acute knee meniscus tears.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: backward jump
steps: Set up with your feet shoulder-width apart holding the bodyweight securely in position.
Brace your core and inhale deeply to build intra-abdominal pressure.
Hinge your hips back and bend your knees to lower under control.
Descend until your thighs reach parallel to the floor with knees tracking over toes.
Drive firmly through your midfoot and heels to return to standing lockout.
tips: Keep your chest proud and drive your knees outward in line with your toes.
Maintain full midfoot balance throughout the descent and ascent.
commonMistakes: Letting knees cave inward during the upward drive.
Allowing your lower back to round into pelvic wink at bottom depth.
safetyNotes: Always set safety spotter arms just below your target depth before loading heavy weights.
contraindications: Avoid heavy spinal loading during acute lumbar disc flare-ups or acute knee meniscus tears.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Fire Log Pose (Double Pigeon)
steps: Sit on your mat and bend your left knee, placing shin parallel to front of mat.
Stack your right shin directly on top of your left shin with right ankle over left knee.
Flex both feet intensely to protect your knee joints.
Sit tall with an erect spine and place fingertips on the floor beside hips.
Hinge forward gently from hips if extra stretch is desired in outer glutes.
Hold for forty-five seconds, then unwind legs and repeat with left shin on top.
tips: Flex both feet firmly to keep knee ligaments stable.
Place a yoga block under the top knee if it hovers high off the bottom foot.
commonMistakes: Sickling the ankles and twisting knee joints.
Rounding lower back to force torso down.
safetyNotes: Do not force top knee down; support with a block.
contraindications: Acute meniscus tear or knee osteoarthritis.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Happy Baby Pose
steps: Lie on your back on your mat and draw both knees toward your armpits.
Flex your feet and grip the outside edges of your feet with your hands.
Open your knees slightly wider than your torso and stack ankles over knees.
Gently pull downward with hands to draw knees toward the floor.
Keep your tailbone and entire spine grounded flat against the mat.
Hold the restorative hip opener for forty-five seconds with slow breaths.
tips: Keep the back of your neck long by tucking your chin slightly.
Gently rock side to side if comfortable for lower back massage.
commonMistakes: Peeling the tailbone and lower back high off the mat.
Tensing shoulders and neck up toward ears.
safetyNotes: Hold shins or back of thighs if feet are out of reach.
contraindications: Late-term pregnancy or acute neck injury.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Half Moon Pose
steps: Begin in Triangle pose with your right leg forward.
Bend your right knee slightly and place right fingertips on the floor six inches ahead of toes.
Shift your weight into your right foot and float your left leg up parallel to the floor.
Straighten your standing right leg without locking the knee joint.
Stack your left hip and shoulder directly over your right side.
Extend your left arm toward the ceiling and gaze up if balance allows.
Hold for thirty seconds, then lower down and repeat on your left side.
tips: Flex your lifted foot intensely and push out through the heel.
Place a yoga block beneath your lower hand to keep torso elongated.
commonMistakes: Letting the lifted leg drop below hip level.
Collapsing the chest toward the mat.
safetyNotes: Use wall support behind your back to build hip stacking confidence.
contraindications: Severe vertigo or inner ear infection.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Half Lord of the Fishes Pose
aliases: Bound Half Lord of the Fishes Pose
steps: Sit with legs extended, bend right knee, and place right foot outside left thigh.
Bend left knee and fold left foot close to right outer hip.
Place right hand on floor behind your sacrum like a kickstand.
Inhale, raise left arm tall, then exhale and hook left elbow outside right knee.
Rotate torso to the right with each exhale, gazing over right shoulder.
Hold for forty-five seconds, untwist, and repeat on opposite side.
tips: Lengthen spine tall on every inhale before deepening twist on exhale.
Keep both sitting bones grounded flat on mat.
commonMistakes: Slouching back onto the rear hand and rounding spine.
Craning the neck aggressively instead of twisting from thoracic spine.
safetyNotes: Twist from the upper back, not the lower back.
contraindications: Acute spinal disc prolapse or severe sacroiliac irritation.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Eight-Angle Pose
steps: Sit on mat, bend right knee, and hook right leg high over right shoulder.
Place palms flat on floor beside hips with fingers spread wide.
Cross left ankle over right ankle and squeeze thighs against right arm.
Press through hands to lift hips and legs off the mat.
Bend elbows to ninety degrees, extend legs out to right, and lower chest parallel to floor.
Hold for thirty seconds, release, and repeat on opposite side.
tips: Squeeze thighs firmly together like a vise around your arm.
Keep shoulders level and gaze forward.
commonMistakes: Failing to clamp legs, causing them to slide down arm.
Collapsing chest onto the floor.
safetyNotes: Warm up wrists and hips thoroughly before practicing.
contraindications: Acute wrist injury or shoulder impingement.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Bound Angle Pose (Cobbler)
steps: Sit upright on your mat and bend both knees.
Bring the soles of your feet together and draw heels toward your pelvis.
Clasp your hands around your feet or ankles and sit tall with shoulders back.
Let your knees drop naturally outward toward the floor without forcing them.
Inhale to lengthen your spine, then hinge forward gently from your hips.
Hold the posture for sixty seconds with calm, steady breathing.
tips: Open the soles of your feet toward the ceiling like pages of a book.
Never push down forcefully on your knees with your hands.
commonMistakes: Pushing knees down aggressively with arm force.
Hunching shoulders forward into ears.
safetyNotes: Support knees with blocks if groin feels strained.
contraindications: Acute knee ligament tears or severe groin pull.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Crow Pose
steps: Squat down on your mat with feet together and hands shoulder-width on floor.
Spread fingers wide and press firmly through knuckle pads.
Lift hips, bend elbows slightly, and rest knees on backs of upper triceps.
Shift bodyweight forward until feet become light.
Lift one foot, then the other, balancing entirely on your hands.
Hold for thirty seconds while drawing navel toward spine, then lower feet.
tips: Look slightly forward rather than down to keep momentum balanced.
Round your upper back and push floor away.
commonMistakes: Looking down at your feet, causing you to tip forward.
Letting elbows flare wide out to the sides.
safetyNotes: Place a cushion in front of your head while learning balance.
contraindications: Carpal tunnel syndrome or acute wrist sprains.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Child's Pose
steps: Kneel on mat with big toes touching and knees wide apart.
Lower hips to rest back on heels and fold torso forward over thighs.
Extend arms forward along mat or rest them alongside body, palms up.
Rest forehead softly on yoga mat.
Release all muscular tension and breathe into back ribcage.
Hold for sixty seconds in calm surrender.
tips: Rest forehead on a block if head does not reach floor.
Place a rolled blanket behind knees if hips do not meet heels.
commonMistakes: Holding tension in shoulders or neck.
Holding breath during resting posture.
safetyNotes: Restorative pose; adjust knee width for comfort.
contraindications: Recent knee surgery or acute diarrhea.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Wild Thing
steps: From Downward-Facing Dog, lift your right leg high into Three-Legged Dog.
Bend your right knee and flip your dog by stepping right foot to floor behind you.
Ground through your left hand and left outer foot.
Inhale, lift your hips high, and extend your right arm overhead toward front of mat.
Curl your upper back into an expressive, joyful backbend.
Hold for thirty seconds, flip back to downward dog, and repeat on opposite side.
tips: Press down through your supporting left hand and engage the left lat.
Keep hips elevated through glute contraction.
commonMistakes: Collapsing into the supporting shoulder joint.
Letting hips sag toward the ground.
safetyNotes: Maintain active shoulder blade engagement on base arm.
contraindications: Rotator cuff tears or carpal tunnel syndrome.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Cobra Pose
steps: Lie prone on your stomach with the tops of your feet flat on the mat.
Place your hands beneath your shoulders with fingers pointing forward.
Hug your elbows lightly against your ribcage.
Press your pubic bone into the mat and inhale as you peel your chest upward.
Engage your back extensors to lift your sternum without pressing heavily through hands.
Hold the gentle backbend while breathing evenly through your nose.
tips: Keep the back of your neck long by directing your gaze forward and slightly down.
Press the tops of your feet into the mat to stabilize your pelvis.
commonMistakes: Pushing with full arm force into a crunching compression of the lumbar spine.
Shrugging your shoulders tightly up around your ears.
safetyNotes: Distribute spinal extension evenly across the thoracic spine rather than hinging only in lower back.
contraindications: Pregnancy, carpal tunnel syndrome, or acute spinal disc herniation.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Corpse Pose
steps: Lie completely flat on your back along the center of your yoga mat.
Allow your feet to fall open naturally wider than hip-width apart.
Rest your arms comfortably alongside your body with palms turned upward.
Close your eyes softly and release all intentional muscular control.
Allow your breathing to settle into a natural, quiet rhythm.
Remain completely still and present for the entire allotted relaxation period.
tips: Place a rolled blanket under your knees if your lower back feels strained.
Scan your body from crown to toes to systematically soften residual tension.
commonMistakes: Holding physical tension in the jaw, brow, or shoulders.
Leaving the session abruptly without gentle preliminary movements.
safetyNotes: Keep warm with a blanket if your body temperature drops during stillness.
contraindications: Third-trimester pregnancy (modify by lying on the left side with bolster).

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Bow Pose
steps: Lie flat on your stomach and bend both knees, bringing heels toward buttocks.
Reach back with both hands and clasp your outer ankles.
Keep knees hip-width apart throughout the movement.
Inhale and kick your shins and feet strongly backward away from your body.
Allow the kick of your legs to lift your chest and thighs off the floor.
Balance on your abdomen and hold for thirty seconds with rhythmic breath.
tips: The lift comes from kicking your legs backward into your hands.
Do not let knees splay out wider than your hips.
commonMistakes: Letting knees splay very wide, jamming sacroiliac joints.
Holding breath while balancing on the belly.
safetyNotes: Kick legs back smoothly without sudden jerking.
contraindications: High blood pressure, hernia, or pregnancy.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Downward-Facing Dog
steps: Begin on your hands and knees in a tabletop position on your mat.
Spread your fingers wide and press firmly through all ten knuckles.
Tuck your toes under and lift your knees away from the floor.
Send your sitting bones up and back toward the ceiling to lengthen your spine.
Ground your heels gently toward the mat while keeping your ears between your upper arms.
Hold the posture steady while taking slow, measured nasal breaths.
tips: Bend your knees slightly if tight hamstrings cause your lower back to round.
Externally rotate your upper arms to broaden your upper back.
commonMistakes: Dumping bodyweight into the wrists instead of pressing through finger knuckles.
Rounding the spine and pushing the chest forward rather than back.
safetyNotes: Distribute weight evenly across the entire surface of both hands to avoid wrist strain.
contraindications: Severe carpal tunnel syndrome, late-term pregnancy, or uncontrolled hypertension.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Eagle Pose
steps: Stand in mountain pose, bend both knees slightly, and shift weight to your right foot.
Cross your left thigh over your right thigh and hook left toes behind right calf if able.
Cross your right elbow over your left elbow, bending arms and pressing palms together.
Lift your elbows to shoulder height while pulling your hands away from your face.
Sink your hips deeper into the squat while keeping your spine erect.
Hold for thirty seconds, then unwind arms and legs and repeat on the opposite side.
tips: Squeeze your inner thighs tightly together to maintain balance on your standing leg.
Draw your navel in and lengthen your tailbone toward the ground.
commonMistakes: Hunching forward and collapsing your chest over your thighs.
Letting your knees splay unevenly.
safetyNotes: Unwrap toes from calf if knee twist or ankle torque occurs.
contraindications: Acute knee ligament tears or shoulder impingement.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Cow Face Pose
steps: Sit with knees bent, sliding left foot under right hip and right knee over left knee.
Stack your knees directly on top of each other in the centerline.
Reach your right arm overhead, bend elbow, and place palm between shoulder blades.
Reach your left arm behind your back, bend elbow, and reach fingers up toward right hand.
Clasp fingers together or hold a yoga strap between both hands.
Hold with tall spine for forty-five seconds, then switch legs and arms and repeat.
tips: Keep both sit bones grounded evenly on the floor.
Use a strap between hands if shoulders are tight.
commonMistakes: Arching lower back into hyper-lordosis to connect hands.
Sitting unevenly on one hip.
safetyNotes: Use a strap to prevent shoulder joint strain.
contraindications: Rotator cuff impingement or acute knee meniscus tear.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Plow Pose
steps: Lie on back, engage core, and lift legs up and overhead.
Lower toes to the floor behind your head with legs straight.
Support lower back with hands or interlace fingers on mat.
Press through toes to lift sit bones toward ceiling.
Keep neck stationary and breathe into back of ribcage.
Hold for forty-five seconds, then roll down vertebra by vertebra.
tips: Rest toes on a chair or block behind head if feet do not reach floor.
Keep neck long and gaze upward toward belly.
commonMistakes: Turning head while neck is loaded under flexion.
Forcing feet down while rounding and compressing spine.
safetyNotes: Do not turn head while in plow pose.
contraindications: Cervical disc herniation or severe hypertension.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Head-to-Knee Forward Bend
steps: Sit with your right leg extended straight and left knee bent.
Place the sole of your left foot against your right inner thigh.
Turn your torso slightly to align your sternum over your right extended leg.
Inhale to lengthen your spine, then exhale and fold forward over right thigh.
Hold your right shin, ankle, or foot with both hands.
Hold for forty-five seconds, then sit up, switch legs, and repeat on left side.
tips: Keep your extended foot flexed and kneecap pointing straight up.
Rotate your torso from the navel to square over the extended leg.
commonMistakes: Rounding the upper back aggressively and yanking with the neck.
Letting the extended leg roll outward.
safetyNotes: Use a strap to maintain spinal length.
contraindications: Acute groin strain or lumbar disc herniation.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Angle Pose (Cobbler)
steps: Sit upright on your mat and bend both knees.
Bring the soles of your feet together and draw heels toward your pelvis.
Clasp your hands around your feet or ankles and sit tall with shoulders back.
Let your knees drop naturally outward toward the floor without forcing them.
Inhale to lengthen your spine, then hinge forward gently from your hips.
Hold the posture for sixty seconds with calm, steady breathing.
tips: Open the soles of your feet toward the ceiling like pages of a book.
Never push down forcefully on your knees with your hands.
commonMistakes: Pushing knees down aggressively with arm force.
Hunching shoulders forward into ears.
safetyNotes: Support knees with blocks if groin feels strained.
contraindications: Acute knee ligament tears or severe groin pull.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Garland Pose (Yogi Squat)
steps: Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width with toes angled forty-five degrees outward.
Bend your knees deeply and lower your hips down into a deep squat.
Bring your palms together at your heart center in prayer position.
Press your elbows outward against your inner knees to gently open your hips.
Lengthen your spine upward from your tailbone through the crown of your head.
Hold the deep squat while breathing into your pelvic floor.
tips: Place a rolled blanket or block under your heels if they lift off the mat.
Broaden across your chest and keep your spine tall.
commonMistakes: Rounding the spine into a hunched turtle posture.
Letting knees collapse inward over arches.
safetyNotes: Use block beneath hips if deep knee flexion causes discomfort.
contraindications: Severe meniscus tears or advanced knee osteoarthritis.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Frog Pose
steps: Begin on all fours on a padded mat or blanket.
Widen your knees as far apart as comfortably possible while keeping them in line with hips.
Bend your ankles at ninety degrees with inside edges of feet resting on the floor.
Lower down onto your forearms and keep your spine flat and neutral.
Gently shift your hips back toward your heels to deepen the inner groin stretch.
Hold the posture for forty-five seconds while breathing steadily into your pelvis.
tips: Double-pad your knees with folded blankets for joint comfort.
Keep your belly gently braced to support your lower back.
commonMistakes: Arching lower back into severe swayback collapse.
Pushing hips back aggressively into sharp groin pain.
safetyNotes: Stop immediately if sharp pinching occurs in hip capsule.
contraindications: Groin adductor tear or severe hip impingement.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Sage Marichi Pose C
steps: Sit with both legs straight; bend right knee and place foot flat near sit bone.
Leave one hand-width space between right foot and left inner thigh.
Place right fingertips on floor behind your spine.
Inhale, extend left arm high, then exhale and hook left elbow outside right thigh.
Press arm against thigh to deepen thoracic twist to the right.
Hold for forty-five seconds, then release and repeat on opposite side.
tips: Keep left extended leg active and foot flexed throughout.
Sit tall and avoid slouching back.
commonMistakes: Collapsing into the rear hand with a curved spine.
Letting extended leg go limp and roll outward.
safetyNotes: Maintain upright spine throughout rotation.
contraindications: Acute spinal disc injuries or pregnancy.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Fish Pose
steps: Lie on your back with legs extended together.
Slide your hands under your buttocks, palms down, with elbows tucked close to sides.
Press firmly down through your forearms and elbows to arch your chest upward.
Lift your sternum high and gently release the crown of your head to the mat.
Keep ninety percent of your bodyweight on your forearms, not your head.
Hold for thirty seconds while breathing deeply into your chest.
tips: Keep weight anchored on your forearms to avoid compressing cervical spine.
Expand your ribcage fully with every deep inhale.
commonMistakes: Resting full head weight onto the neck vertebrae.
Spreading elbows wide and collapsing forearm base.
safetyNotes: Do not bear heavy weight on crown of head.
contraindications: Severe cervical spine injury or migraine.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Peacock Pose
steps: Kneel on mat, place palms flat with fingers pointing backward toward knees.
Press elbows together and bury them into your upper abdomen near navel.
Extend legs back one at a time into a plank shape.
Shift bodyweight forward and elevate legs horizontally off the mat.
Balance entirely on your hands with body horizontal like a peacock.
Hold for twenty seconds, then lower feet softly to the mat.
tips: Keep elbows tight together under belly without separating.
Lean weight forward to counterbalance lifted legs.
commonMistakes: Separating elbows and losing abdominal lever.
Dropping chest down while legs stay heavy.
safetyNotes: Requires intense wrist flexibility and abdominal pressure.
contraindications: Pregnancy, ulcers, hernia, or wrist injury.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Dancer Pose
steps: Stand balanced on your right leg and bend your left knee behind you.
Reach back with your left hand and grasp the inside edge of your left foot or ankle.
Inhale and raise your right arm straight up toward the ceiling.
Hinge slightly forward at your hips and kick your left foot back and up into your hand.
Open your chest forward and lift your back thigh parallel to the mat.
Hold the backbend balance steadily, then release and repeat on your left leg.
tips: Kick your foot actively into your hand to open the shoulder and chest.
Square your hips toward the front rather than opening the pelvis sideways.
commonMistakes: Bending the standing knee excessively and losing vertical lift.
Cranching into the lumbar spine without engaging upper back.
safetyNotes: Engage core firmly to support lower back during backbend.
contraindications: Severe lower back injury or knee instability.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Hands Under Feet Pose
steps: From a forward fold, bend your knees enough to slide your hands under your feet.
Place palms facing up so your toes rest comfortably against your wrist creases.
Inhale to look forward with a flat back and straight arms.
Exhale and fold deeply, bending your elbows wide to the sides.
Drop the crown of your head and gently press your balls of feet into palms.
Hold the deep fold for forty-five seconds while breathing steadily.
tips: Distribute weight forward so your toes give your palms a gentle massage.
Keep your neck relaxed without clenching your jaw.
commonMistakes: Tensing the neck and pulling with violent upper-body force.
Rocking back into heels.
safetyNotes: Micro-bend knees to protect hamstring attachments.
contraindications: Severe lumbar disc prolapse or carpal tunnel flare-up.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Big Toe Pose
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hinge forward at your hips into a fold.
Hook your big toes with your index and middle fingers, securing with thumbs.
Inhale, straighten your arms, lift your chest, and flatten your back.
Exhale, bend your elbows out to the sides, and draw your torso toward your thighs.
Keep your neck completely relaxed and shoulder blades pulled away from ears.
Hold for forty-five seconds while taking slow, deep breaths.
tips: Lift your sit bones high and engage your quadriceps to release hamstrings.
Keep elbows pulling outward to broaden upper back.
commonMistakes: Yanking with arm strength rather than hinging from hips.
Collapsing shoulders into the neck.
safetyNotes: Bend knees as needed to maintain contact between fingers and toes.
contraindications: Acute sciatica or hamstring tendonitis.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Lotus Pose
steps: Sit on mat with legs extended in staff pose.
Bend right knee and place right foot high on left upper thigh, sole facing up.
Bend left knee and carefully cross left foot over right shin onto right upper thigh.
Rest hands on knees in mudra with elbows softly straight.
Lengthen spine tall and soften shoulders.
Hold meditative seat with calm nasal breath for sixty seconds.
tips: Requires open hips; never force feet onto thighs if knees twist.
Keep feet flexed to protect knee joint ligaments.
commonMistakes: Yanking feet onto thighs when hips are tight, twisting knees.
Arching lower back aggressively.
safetyNotes: Never force knees down; practice half lotus if hips are tight.
contraindications: Knee meniscus tears, ligament injuries, or ankle sprains.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Gate Pose
steps: Kneel upright on your mat with knees under hips.
Extend your right leg straight out to your right side with toes pointing forward.
Inhale and extend both arms out to shoulder height parallel to the floor.
Exhale and side-bend your torso to the right, resting right hand on your right shin.
Sweep your left arm overhead past your ear, spiraling your chest open to the ceiling.
Hold for thirty seconds, then rise and repeat the stretch on your left side.
tips: Keep your kneeling hip stacked directly over your kneeling knee.
Do not press hand heavily against the side of the extended knee.
commonMistakes: Collapsing forward through the chest and dropping top shoulder.
Dumping weight onto the knee joint.
safetyNotes: Place folded blanket under kneeling knee for joint comfort.
contraindications: Acute knee bursitis on kneeling leg.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Reverse Warrior
steps: Establish Warrior II with your right knee bent directly over your right ankle.
Turn your front right palm to face the ceiling.
Inhale and sweep your right arm up and back over your head in an arching side bend.
Rest your rear left hand lightly on your back thigh or calf.
Maintain the deep ninety-degree bend in your front right knee.
Hold with chest open, then rise, switch legs, and repeat on your left side.
tips: Maintain depth in your front knee even as your torso reaches backward.
Keep length in both sides of your waist.
commonMistakes: Straightening the front knee when reaching back.
Resting heavy bodyweight onto the back kneecap.
safetyNotes: Do not press hand directly against rear knee joint.
contraindications: Severe spinal stenosis or cervical disc pain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Feathered Peacock Pose (Forearm Stand)
steps: Set forearms on mat parallel to each other, shoulder-width apart.
Tuck toes, lift knees, and walk feet toward elbows in dolphin pose.
Gaze slightly forward between forearms.
Float one leg up and kick gently to bring second leg up into balance.
Press floor away aggressively through forearms to avoid collapsing shoulders.
Hold vertical balance for thirty seconds, then lower under control.
tips: Use a strap around upper arms to prevent elbows from splaying wide.
Engage glutes and core into a hollow body shape.
commonMistakes: Allowing elbows to flare wide and dumping into shoulders.
Banana-arching spine instead of maintaining core brace.
safetyNotes: Practice against a wall to master balance and shoulder strength.
contraindications: Rotator cuff tears or untreated hypertension.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Wide-Legged Forward Fold A
steps: Step your feet four to five feet apart with outer edges parallel to mat edges.
Place your hands on your hips, inhale, and lift your chest high.
Exhale and hinge forward from your hip joints with a flat, elongated spine.
Place your palms flat on the floor directly beneath your shoulders.
Walk hands back until fingers align with toes, letting crown of head drop toward floor.
Hold for forty-five seconds while drawing your quadriceps upward.
tips: Shift your bodyweight slightly forward into the balls of your feet.
Hinge purely from hip joints rather than rounding the lumbar spine.
commonMistakes: Locking knees backward into hyperextension.
Keeping all weight back into heels and curling spine.
safetyNotes: Micro-bend knees if hamstrings are excessively tight.
contraindications: Severe lower back disc herniation or hamstring tear.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Locust Pose A
steps: Lie flat on your stomach with arms resting alongside your body, palms down.
Inhale deeply and lift your chest, head, arms, and legs simultaneously off the floor.
Reach back vigorously through your toes and fingers.
Rest your weight centered comfortably on your lower ribs, belly, and pelvis.
Keep the back of your neck long by gazing slightly downward.
Hold for thirty seconds while breathing into your abdomen.
tips: Squeeze your inner thighs toward each other to stabilize pelvis.
Think about lengthening from head to toes rather than just arching high.
commonMistakes: Holding the breath during the prone lift.
Craning the chin up and hyper-extending the cervical spine.
safetyNotes: Maintain gentle glute engagement to protect lumbar spine.
contraindications: Pregnancy or acute abdominal surgery.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Supported Shoulderstand
steps: Lie on your back with arms alongside your body.
Bend knees, press hands down, and sweep legs overhead into plow pose.
Bend elbows and place palms flat against your mid-back for firm support.
Walk hands down toward shoulder blades and extend legs vertically toward ceiling.
Align hips over shoulders and feet over hips.
Hold for forty-five seconds with chin tucked, then lower down smoothly.
tips: Place folded blankets under shoulders to allow neck to hang free without compression.
Never turn your head sideways while in shoulderstand.
commonMistakes: Turning head sideways while neck is loaded.
Flaring elbows wide apart and losing spinal support.
safetyNotes: Keep head strictly stationary to protect cervical vertebrae.
contraindications: Neck injury, high blood pressure, glaucoma, or menstruation.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Seated Forward Bend
steps: Sit on your mat with legs extended straight in front of you.
Flex your ankles and pull your toes back toward your shins.
Inhale deeply to raise both arms overhead and lengthen your spine.
Exhale and hinge forward from your hips over your thighs.
Reach for your shins, ankles, or the outer edges of your feet.
Hold the forward fold while breathing into the back of your ribcage.
tips: Prioritize lengthening the front of your torso over touching your forehead to knees.
Use a yoga strap looped around the soles of your feet if hamstrings are tight.
commonMistakes: Rounding aggressively through the upper spine and pulling with the neck.
Locking your knees into painful hyperextension.
safetyNotes: Hinge strictly from your pelvic hip joints rather than flexing the lumbar spine.
contraindications: Acute posterior lumbar disc herniation or acute hamstring tear.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Bridge Pose
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on mat, hip-width apart.
Slide your heels close enough so your fingertips can lightly touch them.
Press through your heels and inhale to lift your hips toward the ceiling.
Interlace your fingers beneath your back and roll onto the outer tops of shoulders.
Engage your glutes and keep thighs parallel to each other.
Hold for forty-five seconds, then release hands and roll down vertebra by vertebra.
tips: Press down through your big toe mounds to keep inner thighs active.
Do not turn your head from side to side while in the bridge.
commonMistakes: Letting knees flare wide apart under hip elevation.
Turning the neck while supporting weight on upper shoulders.
safetyNotes: Keep head still throughout to protect cervical spine.
contraindications: Recent neck injury without physician clearance.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Side Lunge Pose
steps: Begin in a wide-legged forward fold with feet parallel.
Bend your right knee deeply and sink into a half-squat on your right leg.
Keep your left leg completely straight, flexing your left foot with toes pointing up.
Bring your hands to prayer at your chest or place fingertips on the floor for support.
Keep your chest lifted and spine elongated.
Hold for thirty seconds, then shift hips across and repeat on your left side.
tips: Ground the heel of your bent leg if possible, or rest on a block for balance.
Engage the quadricep of your straight extended leg.
commonMistakes: Collapsing heavily into the ankle arch of the straight leg.
Rounding lower back excessively.
safetyNotes: Keep hands on the floor to support balance if needed.
contraindications: Acute groin strain or knee meniscus pathology.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Easy Pose
steps: Sit on mat and cross legs at shins, sliding feet beneath opposite knees.
Rest hands on knees with palms facing down or up in mudra.
Lengthen spine tall and align ears over shoulders and shoulders over hips.
Soften facial muscles, drop shoulders away from ears, and close eyes.
Breathe naturally through nose, focusing on breath awareness.
Hold for sixty seconds, then switch cross of legs.
tips: Sit on folded blanket to elevate hips if knees rise higher than pelvis.
Keep spine erect without leaning forward or backward.
commonMistakes: Slouching into lower back and hunching shoulders.
Tensing knees upward.
safetyNotes: Use elevation beneath pelvis for comfortable hip opening.
contraindications: Severe knee arthritis or recent hip surgery.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Supported Headstand
steps: Kneel on your mat and interlace your fingers to create a sturdy triangular base.
Place your forearms on the floor with elbows kept shoulder-width apart.
Nestle the crown of your head softly into the cradle of your clasped hands.
Straighten your legs, lift your hips, and walk your feet in toward your face.
Engage your shoulders and core to float both legs up vertically into the inversion.
Press strongly down through your forearms to alleviate compression on your cervical spine.
Hold with steady breath, then lower down smoothly into child pose.
tips: Eighty percent of bodyweight should be held by your forearms, not your head.
Keep your shoulder blades pulled actively away from your ears.
commonMistakes: Allowing your elbows to splay wide, collapsing forearm support.
Kicking up with wild uncontrolled momentum and arching the spine.
safetyNotes: Never compress your cervical vertebrae; bail immediately if you experience neck pain.
contraindications: Cervical spine injury, glaucoma, detached retina, severe high blood pressure, or migraine.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Supine Spinal Twist
steps: Lie flat on back and hug right knee into chest.
Extend right arm out to right side in a T-shape, palm facing up.
Guide right knee across body toward floor on left with left hand.
Turn head gently to gaze over right shoulder toward right hand.
Keep right shoulder blade pinned flat against mat.
Hold for forty-five seconds, bring knee to center, and repeat on left side.
tips: Keep both shoulder blades grounded flat against mat.
Place a block under the descending knee if it hovers in air.
commonMistakes: Lifting the right shoulder blade off mat to force knee to floor.
Holding tension in belly.
safetyNotes: Keep shoulders relaxed on the mat.
contraindications: Acute sacroiliac joint flare-up or disc herniation.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Reclining Leg Open to Side
aliases: Bound Reclining Leg Open to Side
steps: Lie on your back holding your right foot with a strap or hand in vertical stretch.
Anchor your left hand firmly on top of your left hip bone.
Exhale and slowly lower your right leg out to the right side toward the floor.
Keep your left hip and shoulder pinned flat against the mat.
Gaze over your left shoulder and hold for forty-five seconds.
Bring leg back to center, release, and repeat on your left leg.
tips: Do not let the opposite hip lift off the mat; keep pelvis level.
Rest right leg on a block if inner groin feels tight.
commonMistakes: Letting the body roll completely to the right side.
Tensing shoulders and neck.
safetyNotes: Use a block under the descending leg to support hip.
contraindications: Severe groin pull or sacroiliac instability.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Sun Salutation A Flow
steps: Begin in mountain pose at the front of your mat with hands at your heart center.
Inhale and sweep both arms overhead into upward salute, looking toward your thumbs.
Exhale and hinge forward from your hips into standing forward fold.
Inhale to a halfway lift with flat back and hands on your shins.
Exhale, step or hop back, and lower through four-limbed staff pose.
Inhale into upward-facing dog with chest open and thighs lifted off the floor.
Exhale, push hips up and back into downward-facing dog for five steady breaths.
Step forward to flat back, fold on exhale, and rise tall on inhale to complete the cycle.
tips: Link every individual movement smoothly with an inhale or exhale breath.
Bend your knees during the forward folds if your hamstrings feel tight.
commonMistakes: Rushing through transitions without coordinating with the breath.
Collapsing into the lower back in upward dog rather than lifting the chest.
safetyNotes: Modify chaturanga by lowering knees first if shoulder stability is compromised.
contraindications: Late-term pregnancy or acute carpal tunnel inflammation.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Mountain Pose
steps: Stand with your big toes touching and heels slightly apart.
Distribute your bodyweight evenly across the four corners of both feet.
Engage your quadriceps and lift your kneecaps gently upward.
Draw your belly button in slightly and lengthen your tailbone toward the floor.
Broaden across your collarbones and let your arms rest naturally by your sides.
Gaze forward steadily while breathing slowly and deeply through your nose.
tips: Stack your ears, shoulders, hips, and ankles in one vertical plum line.
Ground into your heels while lengthening the crown of your head.
commonMistakes: Locking knees aggressively into backward hyperextension.
Arching the lower back excessively instead of maintaining neutral pelvis.
safetyNotes: Maintain a micro-bend in knees if you are hypermobile.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Tree Pose
steps: Stand tall in mountain pose with your feet rooted firmly beneath your hips.
Shift your weight into your left foot and lift your right knee.
Place the sole of your right foot against your left inner calf or inner thigh.
Never place your foot directly against the side of your standing knee joint.
Bring your palms together in front of your chest at prayer position.
Fix your gaze on a stable unmoving point ahead to sustain balance.
Hold for thirty seconds, then release and repeat with equal duration on your left foot.
tips: Press your standing thigh and foot sole firmly into each other.
Engage your standing glute to keep your pelvis level.
commonMistakes: Resting the foot sole directly against the inner knee joint.
Letting the standing hip jut out sideways.
safetyNotes: Position hands near a wall if balance feels unsteady.
contraindications: Acute ankle sprain or inner ear balance pathology.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Wide-Angle Seated Forward Bend
steps: Sit on your mat and open your legs wide apart into a comfortable V-shape.
Flex both feet with toes pointing straight up toward the ceiling.
Place hands on the floor in front of you and sit tall on your sit bones.
Inhale, then exhale and walk your hands forward along the floor.
Lower your chest toward the floor while maintaining a flat, long spine.
Hold for forty-five seconds while breathing into your inner thighs.
tips: Sit on a folded blanket to tilt your pelvis forward if lower back rounds.
Keep kneecaps and toes pointing upward throughout.
commonMistakes: Allowing thighs and feet to roll inward as you fold.
Slouching through the lower back instead of hinging.
safetyNotes: Stop folding if sharp pain occurs in inner groin.
contraindications: Groin adductor tear or hamstring avulsion.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Wheel Pose (Upward Bow)
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet planted flat hip-width apart.
Place your palms flat on the floor beside your ears with fingers pointing toward shoulders.
Press through feet and hands simultaneously to lift your hips and chest off the mat.
Pause on the crown of your head to adjust elbows in, then push arms straight.
Open your chest toward the wall behind you while pressing firmly through big toes.
Hold the full backbend for thirty seconds, then tuck chin and lower slowly.
tips: Distribute the arc evenly through shoulders and upper back.
Keep thighs parallel and avoid letting feet turn outward.
commonMistakes: Letting feet splay out wide, compressing lumbar spine.
Pushing purely from lower back without opening shoulders.
safetyNotes: Tuck chin to chest before lowering down to protect neck.
contraindications: Carpal tunnel, high blood pressure, detached retina, or pregnancy.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Upward Salute
steps: Begin standing tall in mountain pose with your core gently engaged.
Inhale and sweep both arms out and overhead in a wide circular arc.
Turn your palms to face each other or press them gently together overhead.
Keep your shoulders drawn down away from your ears as you reach up.
Gaze toward your thumbs without compressing the back of your cervical spine.
Hold for thirty seconds while lengthening through both sides of your ribcage.
tips: Anchor firmly through your feet as you reach vertically through your fingertips.
Keep your ribs drawn downward rather than flaring your ribcage out.
commonMistakes: Shrugging shoulders up toward the ears, pinching the neck.
Leaning backward and compressing the lumbar vertebrae.
safetyNotes: Avoid severe neck hyperextension if cervical pain occurs.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Upward-Facing Dog
steps: Lie prone and place hands beside lower ribs with elbows stacked over wrists.
Press tops of feet and palms firmly into the yoga mat.
Inhale, straighten arms fully, and lift torso and thighs completely off the floor.
Roll shoulders back and draw chest forward through the window of your arms.
Keep thighs engaged and off the mat with knees lifted.
Hold for thirty seconds, then lower down or transition to downward dog.
tips: Keep thighs and knees elevated off the mat throughout.
Broaden across your collarbones and draw shoulder blades down.
commonMistakes: Sagging hips onto the mat and jamming into lower back.
Locking shoulders up into the ears.
safetyNotes: Ensure wrist joints are stacked comfortably under shoulders.
contraindications: Carpal tunnel syndrome or late-term pregnancy.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Camel Pose
steps: Kneel upright with your knees hip-width apart and thighs vertical.
Place your hands on your lower back with fingers pointing down for support.
Press your hips gently forward and lift your sternum toward the ceiling.
Reach back one hand at a time to grasp your heels or keep hands on lower back.
Open your chest fully while keeping thighs perpendicular to the floor.
Hold with steady breath for thirty seconds, then carefully sit back onto heels.
tips: Keep hips pressed forward over your knees rather than sagging backward.
Lift upward through the sternum to avoid crunching lower back.
commonMistakes: Dropping hips backward over heels.
Dropping the head backward violently and pinching cervical vertebrae.
safetyNotes: Keep hands on sacrum if reaching heels strains lower back.
contraindications: Severe lower back disc disease or cervical injury.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Goddess Pose
steps: Step feet wide apart on your mat with toes turned outward at forty-five degrees.
Bend your knees deeply, lowering hips until thighs are parallel to the floor.
Ensure your knees track directly over your middle toes.
Bring arms into cactus shape with elbows at shoulder height and palms facing forward.
Tuck your tailbone slightly and keep your torso completely vertical.
Hold the wide squat steadily while taking slow, deep diaphragmatic breaths.
tips: Press knees outward away from centerline to activate outer hips and glutes.
Stack your shoulders directly over your hips.
commonMistakes: Leaning forward and collapsing chest toward thighs.
Allowing knees to cave inward past ankles.
safetyNotes: Align knees over second toes to avoid joint torque.
contraindications: Recent groin pull or knee ligament strain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Chair Pose
steps: Stand with feet together or hip-width apart with arms by your sides.
Inhale and sweep your arms overhead with palms facing inward.
Exhale and bend your knees deeply, shifting your hips back as if sitting in a low chair.
Keep your weight centered over your heels and midfoot so toes can wiggle.
Lift your chest high and draw your belly button toward your spine.
Hold the squat with steady breath for the prescribed duration.
tips: Shift your knees back so you can see your toes in front of your kneecaps.
Keep your lower back long without excessive lumbar sway.
commonMistakes: Letting knees travel far forward over the toes, overloading patella.
Arching lower back into a deep swayback curve.
safetyNotes: Keep weight back into heels to protect kneecaps.
contraindications: Acute patellofemoral pain syndrome or severe arthritis.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Standing Forward Fold
steps: Stand in mountain pose with feet hip-width apart and hands on hips.
Inhale deeply to lengthen your spine toward the ceiling.
Exhale and hinge forward from your hip creases with an extended flat back.
Place your fingertips on the floor or rest hands on your shins or blocks.
Release your neck and let the crown of your head hang heavy toward the floor.
Hold for forty-five seconds while lifting your sitting bones toward the ceiling.
tips: Bend your knees softly if tight hamstrings cause your lower back to round.
Shift your weight forward slightly over the balls of your feet.
commonMistakes: Rounding aggressively through the lumbar spine to reach the floor.
Locking the knees into backward hyperextension.
safetyNotes: Hinge strictly from hips to avoid lumbar strain.
contraindications: Acute lumbar disc herniation or hamstring tear.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Extended Side Angle Pose
steps: Set up in Warrior II with your right knee bent directly over your ankle.
Rest your right forearm gently on your right thigh just above the knee.
Reach your left arm up and overhead creating a straight diagonal line from foot to fingers.
Spiral your chest upward toward the ceiling and gaze toward your left palm.
Press firmly into the outer blade of your back left foot.
Hold for thirty seconds, then rise, switch sides, and repeat with left leg forward.
tips: Keep your front thigh parallel to the mat and maintain deep hip flexion.
Avoid dumping your torso weight passively onto the resting forearm.
commonMistakes: Letting your top shoulder roll downward toward the floor.
Collapsing the arch of your rear foot.
safetyNotes: Maintain active core lift to protect resting shoulder joint.
contraindications: Recent knee injury or severe cervical disc issue.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Extended Triangle Pose
steps: Step feet wide apart with right foot pointing forward and left foot angled slightly inward.
Extend your arms out to shoulder height with palms facing down.
Inhale and reach your right arm forward directly over your right thigh.
Hinge at the right hip and bring your right hand to your shin, ankle, or a yoga block.
Extend your left arm straight up toward the ceiling and gaze toward your top thumb.
Hold with open chest, then reverse feet and repeat the posture on your left side.
tips: Prioritize lengthening both sides of your waist over touching the floor.
Imagine leaning the back of your body flat against an invisible wall.
commonMistakes: Resting heavy bodyweight onto the front shin or knee joint.
Collapsing your chest forward toward the ground.
safetyNotes: Use a yoga block under the lower hand to keep spine long.
contraindications: Severe hamstring strain or acute neck pain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Thunderbolt Pose
steps: Kneel on mat with knees and big toes touching.
Lower buttocks to rest comfortably on tops of heels.
Place palms flat on thighs with fingers pointing forward.
Sit tall with crown of head lifting toward ceiling.
Relax shoulders and breathe calmly into abdomen.
Hold for sixty seconds for post-meal digestive benefit.
tips: Place a blanket between calves and thighs if knees feel tight.
Keep spine vertically stacked.
commonMistakes: Slouching forward over thighs.
Letting ankles roll outward.
safetyNotes: Place cushion under ankles if tops of feet ache.
contraindications: Recent knee surgery or severe ankle sprains.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Legs-Up-the-Wall Pose
steps: Sit sideways with one hip against a sturdy wall.
Pivot on buttocks and swing legs up the wall as you lie back.
Rest back and head flat on mat with legs resting vertically.
Open arms out to sides with palms facing upward.
Close eyes and let gravitational drainage soothe legs.
Hold for sixty seconds while breathing naturally.
tips: Place a bolster under hips for elevated pelvic relaxation.
Allow all leg musculature to soften completely.
commonMistakes: Scooting too far from the wall so legs slide down.
Straining neck or shoulders.
safetyNotes: Maintain comfortable position for passive restorative blood flow.
contraindications: Glaucoma or late-term pregnancy.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Warrior I
steps: From standing, step your left foot back roughly four feet along your mat.
Angle your back left foot forty-five degrees outward with your heel grounded firmly.
Square your hips forward toward the front edge of your yoga mat.
Bend your front right knee until it stacks directly over your front ankle.
Inhale and raise both arms overhead with palms facing inward toward each other.
Hold with a tall spine, then switch sides and repeat with left leg leading.
tips: Press deeply into the outer heel of your back foot to stabilize your pelvis.
Sink hips lower while keeping your front knee tracking over middle toes.
commonMistakes: Letting the back heel peel off the mat during the posture.
Twisting through the lower back to force hips forward.
safetyNotes: Keep the back heel anchored to maintain knee alignment.
contraindications: Severe high blood pressure or acute knee injury.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Warrior III
steps: Stand balanced on your right foot with hands on your hips.
Hinge forward at your right hip as you extend your left leg straight behind you.
Bring your torso and left leg into a single horizontal line parallel to the ground.
Reach your arms forward past your ears or extend them back alongside your hips.
Flex your left foot and point all five toes straight down toward the mat.
Hold for thirty seconds with level hips, then switch and repeat on left leg.
tips: Keep both hip bones pointing evenly toward the floor like headlights.
Micro-bend your standing knee to avoid hyperextension.
commonMistakes: Opening the lifted hip upward and twisting the pelvis out of alignment.
Rounding the upper back and dropping the chest toward the floor.
safetyNotes: Engage core firmly to support lumbar spine during horizontal hold.
contraindications: Severe vertigo or uncontrolled balance disorders.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Hero Pose
steps: Kneel on mat with knees together and feet separated wider than hips.
Tops of feet rest flat on mat with toes pointing straight back.
Lower buttocks to sit on floor or block between heels.
Rest hands on thighs and lengthen spine tall.
Hold for sixty seconds with steady, measured breaths.
tips: Sit on a block between feet to eliminate knee strain.
Do not allow feet to roll inward.
commonMistakes: Sitting between feet when knees feel pinching pain.
Slumping lower back.
safetyNotes: Use block under sitting bones if knees feel torque.
contraindications: Knee ligament tear or meniscus pathology.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Bound Warrior II
steps: Step your feet four feet apart along the length of your yoga mat.
Turn your right foot out ninety degrees and angle your left foot slightly inward.
Inhale and raise both arms parallel to the floor with palms facing down.
Exhale and bend your right knee until it stacks directly over your right ankle.
Gaze steadily over your right front middle finger and hold the pose.
Straighten your leg, reverse your foot positions, and repeat on your left side.
tips: Press firmly into the outer blade of your back foot to stabilize your pelvis.
Stack your shoulders directly above your hips rather than leaning forward.
commonMistakes: Allowing the front knee to collapse inward past the big toe.
Lifting the back arm lazily lower than shoulder height.
safetyNotes: Ensure the front knee stays aligned with the second toe to prevent knee torque.
contraindications: Recent knee ligament tear or severe hip bursitis.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Crow Pose
steps: Squat down on your mat with feet together and hands shoulder-width on floor.
Spread fingers wide and press firmly through knuckle pads.
Lift hips, bend elbows slightly, and rest knees on backs of upper triceps.
Shift bodyweight forward until feet become light.
Lift one foot, then the other, balancing entirely on your hands.
Hold for thirty seconds while drawing navel toward spine, then lower feet.
tips: Look slightly forward rather than down to keep momentum balanced.
Round your upper back and push floor away.
commonMistakes: Looking down at your feet, causing you to tip forward.
Letting elbows flare wide out to the sides.
safetyNotes: Place a cushion in front of your head while learning balance.
contraindications: Carpal tunnel syndrome or acute wrist sprains.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Balance Board
steps: Position the balls of your feet on the platform holding or supporting the bodyweight.
Lower your heels below platform level to achieve a deep calf stretch.
Drive powerfully up onto the balls of your big toes into full plantarflexion.
Hold the top contraction for two seconds with knees kept straight or soft.
Descend slowly under control back into the full bottom stretch.
tips: Pause for two seconds at the peak contraction on the balls of your big toes.
Descend into a full, controlled calf stretch on each repetition.
commonMistakes: Bouncing rapidly through repetitions without controlling the stretch.
Rolling onto the outer edges of your feet rather than pressing through your big toe.
safetyNotes: Avoid bouncing at the bottom of the stretch to protect your Achilles tendon.
contraindications: Acute Achilles tendinitis or plantar fasciitis flare-up.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Child's Pose
steps: Kneel on mat with big toes touching and knees wide apart.
Lower hips to rest back on heels and fold torso forward over thighs.
Extend arms forward along mat or rest them alongside body, palms up.
Rest forehead softly on yoga mat.
Release all muscular tension and breathe into back ribcage.
Hold for sixty seconds in calm surrender.
tips: Rest forehead on a block if head does not reach floor.
Place a rolled blanket behind knees if hips do not meet heels.
commonMistakes: Holding tension in shoulders or neck.
Holding breath during resting posture.
safetyNotes: Restorative pose; adjust knee width for comfort.
contraindications: Recent knee surgery or acute diarrhea.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Ball Leg Curl
steps: Position yourself securely in the machine with the stabilityBall pad against your lower legs.
Align your knee joint directly with the rotational axis of the machine.
Flex or extend your knees smoothly against the resistance through full range.
Pause for one second at peak contraction while keeping your hips planted.
Lower the weight stack under steady control without letting the plates slam.
tips: Control the eccentric return smoothly over three full seconds.
Keep your hips firmly pressed into the pad throughout the contraction.
commonMistakes: Lifting your hips off the bench to assist the curl using lower back momentum.
Letting the weight stack slam together at the bottom of the movement.
safetyNotes: Align the machine pivot axis precisely with your knee joint.
contraindications: Recent ACL or PCL reconstruction without physical therapy clearance.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: band alternating biceps curl
steps: Stand or sit upright holding the resistanceBand with arms fully extended.
Pin your elbows securely against your sides and keep your chest lifted.
Curl the weight upward by flexing your biceps while keeping upper arms still.
Contract your biceps forcefully at the top of the movement.
Complete the target reps, then switch sides and repeat the movement.
tips: Pin your elbows lightly against your sides to eliminate momentum.
Squeeze your biceps hard at the peak for one full second.
commonMistakes: Swinging your hips and lower back to heave the weight up.
Letting your elbows drift forward excessively during the curl.
safetyNotes: Do not hyperextend your elbows violently at the bottom of the curl.
contraindications: Acute distal biceps tendinopathy or medial epicondylitis.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: band alternating v-up
steps: Set up in position with the resistanceBand and brace your core firmly.
Initiate the movement by contracting your target muscles through a full active range.
Exhale smoothly as you reach peak muscular contraction.
Pause for one second to maximize tension before returning under control.
Complete the target reps, then switch sides and repeat the movement.
tips: Draw your belly button toward your spine to engage the transverse abdominis.
Exhale completely at peak contraction to deepen abdominal recruitment.
commonMistakes: Hyperextending the lower back when fatigued during core drills.
Pulling with your neck instead of flexing from your abdominal muscles.
safetyNotes: Do not pull on the back of your neck with your hands during core flexions.
contraindications: Acute lumbar disc herniation aggravated by spinal flexion or twisting.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Band-Assisted Cat-Cow Dynamic Stretch
steps: Set up on hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
Inhale into cow pose by dropping your belly and lifting your chest and tailbone.
Exhale into cat pose by tucking your tailbone and rounding your spine up.
Press firmly through your palms to spread your shoulder blades apart.
Flow continuously between extension and flexion in rhythm with your breath.
tips: Articulate the movement vertebra by vertebra starting from your pelvis.
Keep your elbows unlocked throughout the transition.
commonMistakes: Cramming into cervical hyperextension by jerking the chin up too far.
Moving with rapid uncontrolled pace rather than smooth segmental articulation.
safetyNotes: Stay within a comfortable pain-free range of motion without forcing end ranges.
contraindications: Severe acute disc prolapse aggravated by flexion.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Backward Retreat Step
steps: Start in orthodox stance with hands held high in guard.
Step backward three to five inches with your rear back foot.
Push off the ball of your lead front foot to propel yourself backward.
Slide your lead foot back the exact same distance to reset stance.
Keep your chin tucked and guard solid as you retreat out of range.
tips: Step first with the back foot when moving backward.
Keep your center of gravity centered between both legs.
commonMistakes: Stepping backward with front foot first, crossing feet.
Leaning torso backward away from feet.
safetyNotes: Never run backward flat-footed.
contraindications: Achilles tendon strain.

name: Bob and Weave
steps: Assume your boxing stance as a horizontal hook is launched.
Drop beneath the punch by bending both knees into a quarter-squat.
Trace a smooth U-shape with your head moving under and across the arc.
Rise up on the opposite side of the hook with hips loaded to counter.
Keep your hands firmly protecting your chin throughout the weave.
tips: Weave using your legs and hips in a smooth continuous U-pattern.
Stay in punching range as you come up on the opposite side.
commonMistakes: Bending at the waist and bending neck down into danger.
Standing straight up in the middle of the opponent punch.
safetyNotes: Maintain continuous visual contact with opponent.
contraindications: Meniscus knee strain or lower back pain.

name: Defensive Check Hook (3)
steps: Begin in orthodox stance as an opponent steps forward aggressively.
Pivot sharply on the ball of your lead left foot, swinging your rear leg back.
Turn your body ninety degrees away from the opponent charging line.
Whip punch 3 (lead hook) across as you pivot your hips out of range.
Exit on the safe outside angle with hands returned to guard.
Complete the drill, then repeat on the opposite side.
tips: The check hook uses the opponent forward momentum against them.
Pivot your rear leg like opening a door on a hinge.
commonMistakes: Throwing the hook without pivoting the feet, getting tackled forward.
Dropping the rear defensive hand.
safetyNotes: Maintain stable foot pivot to avoid slipping.
contraindications: Acute ankle sprain or knee torsion.

name: Boxing Combination: Four-Punch Straight Flurry (1-2-1-2)

Drive punch 2 (cross) immediately following the jab line.
Fire a second punch 1 (jab) through the open centerline.
Finish with a powerful punch 2 (cross) to complete the flurry.
Snap both hands back to defensive cheek guard.
tips: Reference the numbered punches 1-6 smoothly without pauses.
Keep your chin tucked and non-punching hand in guard.
commonMistakes: Dropping the rear hand during combinations.
Over-committing balance forward.
safetyNotes: Maintain wrist alignment and wrap hands properly.
contraindications: Wrist fracture or carpal instability.

Whip another punch 3 (lead hook) to finish the sequence.

Snap back into defensive stance.
tips: Reference the numbered punches 1-6 smoothly without pauses.

name: Double Jab - Cross (1-1-2)
steps: Step forward lightly and fire punch 1 (lead jab).
Step forward again immediately and fire a second punch 1 to blind opponent.
Pivot on rear foot and drive punch 2 (rear cross) hard into the opening.
Keep your rear hand glued to your jaw during both lead jabs.
Snap punch 2 back to your cheek and reset in balanced stance.

The cross follows instantly behind the second jab.

name: One-Two Combination (1-2)
steps: Fire punch 1 (lead jab) straight down the pipe from your guard.
Retract the jab quickly while pivoting on your rear foot.
Drive punch 2 (rear cross) immediately following the returning jab path.
Turn your rear hip completely forward to transfer power into the cross.
Recoil punch 2 back to your cheek and reset in your balanced stance.
tips: The 1-2 should sound like a rhythmic double-tap: pop-pop.
Do not pause between punch 1 and punch 2.
commonMistakes: Dropping the lead hand while throwing punch 2.

safetyNotes: Maintain continuous defensive guard with non-punching hand.

name: Jab - Cross - Lead Uppercut - Cross (1-2-5-2)
steps: Fire punch 1 (jab) to distract opponent guard.
Pivot and drive punch 2 (rear cross) to back opponent up.
Dip lead shoulder and drive punch 5 (lead uppercut) under opponent chin.
Rotate rear hip and finish with a devastating punch 2 (cross).
Snap back into guard and circle away smoothly.

Keep uppercut compact and close to your chest.

name: Jab - Cross - Hook - Cross (1-2-3-2)
steps: Fire punch 1 (jab) followed instantly by punch 2 (rear cross).
Pivot weight forward to whip punch 3 (lead hook) across target.
Pivot rear foot again to drive final punch 2 (rear cross) down the middle.
Keep non-punching hand glued to jawline throughout each transition.
Retract all punches cleanly along their launch paths.
tips: Maintain a fast 1-2-3-2 rhythm: left-right-left-right.
Every punch sets up the hip rotation for the subsequent punch.
commonMistakes: Rushing the combo and smothering your own extension.
Dropping hands as fatigue sets in.

name: Boxing Combination: Slip Left - Cross - Hook - Cross (slip-2-3-2)
steps: Slip outside an incoming jab by shifting weight to rear leg.
Fire counter punch 2 (cross) directly over opponent arm.
Pivot to whip punch 3 (lead hook) to temple.
Finish with powerful punch 2 (cross) down the middle.
Snap both hands back to defensive cheekbones.
tips: Reference the numbered punches 1-6 smoothly without pauses.
Keep your chin tucked and non-punching hand in guard.
commonMistakes: Dropping the rear hand during combinations.
Over-committing balance forward.
safetyNotes: Maintain wrist alignment and wrap hands properly.

name: Cross - Lead Hook - Cross (2-3-2)
steps: Initiate with a powerful counter punch 2 (rear cross).
Pivot on your lead foot to whip punch 3 (lead hook) to the temple.
Pivot back on your rear foot and drive punch 2 (cross) straight down middle.
Keep your balance centered between both legs throughout.
Recoil back into your tight defensive guard.
tips: This power combo uses alternating hip torque: right-left-right.
Keep your lead shoulder high to protect your jaw.
commonMistakes: Over-committing on punch 2 and falling forward into opponent.
Dropping the non-punching hand.
safetyNotes: Maintain full foot contact with the floor on pivots.

name: Duck Defense
steps: Begin in your boxing stance with your hands held tightly in guard.
Bend at both knees, lowering your body straight down four to six inches.
Allow incoming horizontal hooks to pass safely over your head.
Keep your eyes fixed straight ahead on your opponent torso.
Drive through your heels to return immediately to your tall guard.
tips: Bend at your knees like an athletic squat, not at your lower back.
Keep your chin tucked and elbows tight to your ribs.
commonMistakes: Bending forward at the waist and looking down at the floor.
Duck-walking too deep and getting trapped underneath.
safetyNotes: Never take your eyes off your opponent while ducking.
contraindications: Patellofemoral knee overload.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: 45-Degree Lead Pivot
steps: Stand in orthodox stance with sixty percent weight on lead left foot.
Pivot on the ball of your lead foot while swinging rear leg forty-five degrees to right.
Create a fresh dominant angle outside the opponent front shoulder.
Plant your rear foot firmly to re-establish your balanced base.
Keep your hands in full defensive guard during the entire pivot.
tips: Pivot like a compass with your lead foot acting as the needle.
Turn your hips with the pivot to align punches on the new angle.
commonMistakes: Lifting the lead heel and stumbling off balance.
Dropping hands while pivoting.
safetyNotes: Keep core braced throughout the rotational pivot.
contraindications: Ankle sprain or knee meniscus twist.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Forward Shuffle Step
steps: Begin in your balanced boxing stance with weight on balls of feet.
Step forward two to four inches with your lead front foot.
Push off the ball of your rear foot to drive the forward movement.
Slide your rear foot forward the exact same distance to restore your stance.
Maintain your standard shoulder-width base without crossing feet.
tips: Always step with the foot closest to the direction you want to travel.
Stay light on the balls of your feet with heels lightly floating.
commonMistakes: Dragging the back foot lazily and narrowing your stance base.
Crossing your feet while stepping forward.
safetyNotes: Maintain athletic knee bend to absorb movement.
contraindications: Acute ankle instability.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Lead Body Jab (1b)
steps: Begin in your standard boxing stance with elbows tucked in guard.
Change levels by bending your knees and dropping your hips downward.
Step forward with your lead foot and drive punch 1 directly toward opponent solar plexus.
Keep your rear hand glued to your cheek to protect against counter-punches.
Push off your lead foot to snap back into tall guard position.
tips: Bend your knees to change levels rather than bending only at your waist.
Keep your eyes locked on the opponent chest and eyes.
commonMistakes: Bending at the waist and looking down at the floor.
Leaving the rear defensive hand low during the body shot.
safetyNotes: Keep rear guard high to protect against overhand counters.
contraindications: Acute lumbar facet strain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Lead Jab (1)
steps: Begin in your orthodox boxing stance with your hands held up in guard.
Step forward lightly with your lead left foot as you fire your left fist forward.
Rotate your fist over so your palm faces down at the moment of impact.
Shrug your lead shoulder upward to guard your chin against incoming counters.
Snap your left fist back along the exact same path to your defensive guard position.
tips: The 1 jab is a crisp whip: throw it relaxed and clench your fist on contact.
Keep your rear right hand glued to your cheekbone while throwing the jab.
commonMistakes: Dropping your left hand to your chest before extending the punch.
Over-committing your weight forward and falling off balance.
safetyNotes: Wrap your hands properly and keep your wrist straight to prevent sprains.
contraindications: Acute scaphoid wrist fracture or carpal instability.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Lead Shovel Hook to Liver (3b)
steps: Assume an orthodox stance within inside fighting distance.
Dip your torso slightly to the left by bending your knees.
Drive upward and inward at a forty-five-degree angle with punch 3.
Target the opponent right floating rib where the liver sits.
Snap the punch back immediately to your protective left cheek guard.
tips: The shovel hook is half-hook, half-uppercut driven by the legs.
Keep your elbow tucked close to your ribs until release.
commonMistakes: Telegraphing the punch by winding your arm backward.
Dropping your rear hand during the inside attack.
safetyNotes: Maintain compact elbow angle to avoid hyperextension.
contraindications: Acute shoulder labral strain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Orthodox Lead Hook (3)
steps: Begin in your orthodox guard position with hands protecting your jaw.
Shift bodyweight slightly toward your lead left foot.
Pivot sharply on the ball of your lead foot like squashing a bug.
Whip your left arm horizontally into punch 3 with elbow bent ninety degrees.
Align your wrist, elbow, and shoulder in one horizontal plane on impact.
Recoil your left fist immediately back to your cheek in guard.
tips: Power comes from the lead foot pivot and torso rotation, not arm swinging.
Keep your rear right hand glued to your cheek to absorb counters.
commonMistakes: Looping the hook too wide and exposing your chest to counters.
Dropping the rear hand while throwing the lead hook.
safetyNotes: Keep your wrist stiff and forearm horizontal to prevent sprains.
contraindications: Acute rotator cuff tear or wrist TFCC tear.

name: Orthodox Lead Uppercut (5)
steps: Begin in your orthodox guard with knees softly flexed.
Dip your left shoulder slightly and drop your left hand three inches.
Drive upward through your legs and rotate your left hip inward.
Thrust punch 5 vertically upward with palm facing your chest.
Target the opponent chin or solar plexus along the centerline.
Retract your left fist back to your defensive cheek guard.
tips: Power comes from leg drive and hip rotation, not lifting with your arm.
Keep the punch compact and close to your body.
commonMistakes: Dropping the hand down to the waist before punching, telegraphing.

safetyNotes: Keep the trajectory compact along the centerline.
contraindications: Acute bicep tendonitis or wrist sprain.
