Catch the weight securely in a strong rack or overhead receiving position.
Stand up to complete extension, then lower the weight under control to the floor.
tips: Achieve explosive triple extension through your ankles, knees, and hips.
Keep the bar path close to your body throughout the entire pull and catch.
commonMistakes: Banging the bar outward off the hips and looping it wide.
Pulling early with bent arms before full hip extension is reached.
safetyNotes: Always perform Olympic lifts on a dedicated lifting platform with bumper plates.
contraindications: Acute wrist TFCC injury or spinal disc herniation.

name: Power Stairs
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart holding the bodyweight with a secure grip.
Engage your lats, pull your shoulders back, and brace your midsection firmly.
Hinge back at your hips while keeping a slight soft bend in your knees.
Lower the weight along your shins until you feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes tightly to stand tall.
tips: Keep the bar or weight in light contact with your legs throughout the pull.
Lock out by squeezing your glutes rather than leaning back from your lower back.
commonMistakes: Jerking the weight off the floor before building full lat tension.
Rounding the spine during the initial pull.
safetyNotes: Never allow your spinal column to round aggressively under maximal pulling loads.

name: Wide-Legged Forward Fold A
steps: Step your feet four to five feet apart with outer edges parallel to mat edges.
Place your hands on your hips, inhale, and lift your chest high.
Exhale and hinge forward from your hip joints with a flat, elongated spine.
Place your palms flat on the floor directly beneath your shoulders.
Walk hands back until fingers align with toes, letting crown of head drop toward floor.
Hold for forty-five seconds while drawing your quadriceps upward.
tips: Shift your bodyweight slightly forward into the balls of your feet.
Hinge purely from hip joints rather than rounding the lumbar spine.
commonMistakes: Locking knees backward into hyperextension.
Keeping all weight back into heels and curling spine.
safetyNotes: Micro-bend knees if hamstrings are excessively tight.
contraindications: Severe lower back disc herniation or hamstring tear.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Preacher Curl
steps: Stand or sit upright holding the barbell with arms fully extended.
Pin your elbows securely against your sides and keep your chest lifted.
Curl the weight upward by flexing your biceps while keeping upper arms still.
Contract your biceps forcefully at the top of the movement.
Lower the weight back down slowly under control to full elbow extension.
tips: Pin your elbows lightly against your sides to eliminate momentum.
Squeeze your biceps hard at the peak for one full second.
commonMistakes: Swinging your hips and lower back to heave the weight up.
Letting your elbows drift forward excessively during the curl.
safetyNotes: Do not hyperextend your elbows violently at the bottom of the curl.
contraindications: Acute distal biceps tendinopathy or medial epicondylitis.

steps: Stand or sit upright holding the dumbbell with arms fully extended.

name: Precision Powerhouse The Roll Over
steps: Lie on back with arms by sides and legs extended together.
Inhale and lift legs to ninety degrees perpendicular to floor.
Exhale and peel spine off mat to carry legs overhead parallel to floor.
Open legs shoulder-width, flex feet, and articulate down vertebra by vertebra.
Bring legs together at forty-five degrees and repeat.
tips: Roll through spine with deep abdominal scooping.
Never turn your head sideways during the roll-over.
commonMistakes: Throwing legs back with violent momentum.
Turning head sideways while neck is bearing weight.
safetyNotes: Do not turn head while inverted on upper back.
contraindications: Cervical spine disc injury.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Precision Powerhouse The Roll Up
steps: Lie supine with arms reaching overhead and legs glued together.
Inhale and lift arms toward ceiling, tucking chin to chest.
Exhale and roll up smoothly off mat vertebra by vertebra.
Reach forward over toes in a continuous C-curve spine.
Roll down vertebra by vertebra back to the mat.
tips: Articulate through each spinal segment without momentum.
Keep feet flexed and thighs squeezed together.
commonMistakes: Flinging arms forward to heave body up.
Collapsing lower back onto mat abruptly.
safetyNotes: Control the descent to protect lumbar vertebrae.
contraindications: Acute lumbar disc herniation.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Precision Powerhouse The Saw
steps: Sit tall with legs opened slightly wider than your shoulders.
Extend arms out to sides at shoulder height with palms down.
Inhale and rotate torso to right with tall erect spine.
Exhale and reach left pinky finger past right pinky toe.
Complete the target reps, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Anchor both sit bones firmly to the mat throughout the reach.
Rotate from the waist, not just the arms.
commonMistakes: Lifting opposite hip off the floor while reaching.
Slumping into rounded lower back.
safetyNotes: Maintain spinal elongation during rotation.
contraindications: Acute sciatica.

name: Precision Powerhouse The Seal
steps: Sit on mat, bend knees, and thread arms through inner thighs to grip outer ankles.
Lift feet off mat and balance on sitting bones.
Clap feet together three times like a seal.
Roll back onto shoulder blades, clap feet three times, and roll up to balance.
Repeat the rolling sequence smoothly for target repetitions.
tips: Roll only onto upper shoulder blades; never roll onto neck.
Use deep core scoop to control balance at top.
commonMistakes: Rolling back onto cervical vertebrae.
Unclasping ankles and losing body shape.
safetyNotes: Never roll onto the neck.
contraindications: Cervical disc injury.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Precision Powerhouse Single Leg Stretch
steps: Lie on your back on your mat and bring both knees into your chest.
Curl your head and shoulder blades off the mat into an abdominal curl.
Extend your left leg forward at a forty-five-degree angle while drawing right knee in.
Place your left hand on your right knee and right hand on your right ankle.
Switch legs smoothly, extending your right leg and pulling left knee into chest.
Complete the target reps, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your torso completely stable and quiet as your legs alternate.
Keep your outside hand near your ankle and inside hand near your knee.
commonMistakes: Rocking your hips and torso side to side as your legs switch.
Dropping your shoulder blades down onto the mat between repetitions.
safetyNotes: Rest your head on the mat if your neck extensors become fatigued.
contraindications: Acute cervical strain or unhealed abdominal surgery.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Precision Powerhouse Swan Dive
steps: Lie prone with palms flat beside shoulders and legs together.
Inhale and press through hands, lifting chest into long extension.
Rock forward onto ribs, lifting legs up behind you as arms reach forward.
Rock back onto thighs, catching yourself lightly on hands.
Maintain continuous rocking arc for prescribed repetitions.
tips: Keep abdominal wall scooped to protect lumbar spine.
Maintain a uniform arc from crown to toes.
commonMistakes: Collapsing into lumbar hyperextension.
Throwing head back aggressively.
safetyNotes: Do not force extension if lower back pinches.
contraindications: Spondylolysis or acute spinal stenosis.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Precision Powerhouse The Hundred
steps: Lie on your back on a mat and bring both knees into your chest.
Curl your head, neck, and shoulder blades smoothly off the mat.
Extend your legs forward to a forty-five-degree angle in Pilates stance.
Reach your arms long by your sides hovering two inches off the floor.
Pump your arms briskly up and down from the shoulders in a six-inch range.
Inhale deeply for five arm pumps, then exhale completely for five arm pumps.
Complete ten breath cycles for a total of one hundred arm pumps.
tips: Pump your arms from the back of your shoulders with firm straight elbows.
Anchor your lower back into the mat by drawing your navel deeply to your spine.
commonMistakes: Pumping from the wrists or elbows instead of moving from the shoulder joint.
Letting your lower back peel up off the mat as legs extend.
safetyNotes: If your neck strains or lower back arches, bend your knees into tabletop.
contraindications: Acute cervical spine disc herniation or active diastasis recti.

name: Precision Powerhouse The Teaser
steps: Lie flat on your mat with arms reaching overhead and legs extended together.
Inhale and lift your arms and head to begin rolling forward off the mat.
Simultaneously lift your legs straight to a forty-five-degree angle.
Roll up into a balanced V-sit position on your sacrum with arms parallel to legs.
Pause for two seconds at the apex, lifting through your chest with open collarbones.
Articulate your spine smoothly back down onto the mat vertebra by vertebra.
tips: Roll through the spine with articulation rather than snapping up with momentum.
Keep your inner thighs firmly squeezed together throughout the movement.
commonMistakes: Flinging arms forward and using sudden jerking momentum to sit up.
Collapsing chest and slouching at the top of the V-position.
safetyNotes: Control the descent vertebra by vertebra to protect lumbar spine integrity.
contraindications: Severe osteoporosis or acute lumbar spinal disc herniation.

name: Precision Powerhouse Reformer Elephant

Place hands flat on footbar and round spine into a deep C-curve.

Draw carriage home by scooping abdominals deeply without moving shoulders.
Maintain rounded back and head hanging heavy between arms.
tips: Keep heels anchored into carriage throughout.
Draw carriage in using deep lower abdominals.

safetyNotes: Maintain secure grip on footbar.
contraindications: Acute hamstring tendonitis.

name: Precision Powerhouse Reformer Footwork - Toes

Place the balls of both feet onto the footbar with heels together in Pilates V.
Maintain a neutral pelvis with your spine resting long and flat on the carriage.
Inhale and press the carriage away by extending your knees smoothly.
Reach full leg extension without hyperextending or locking out your knee joints.
Exhale and resist the springs as you bend your knees to return the carriage home.
tips: Keep your heels glued together and elevated at a steady height throughout.
Resist the carriage springs with control on the return stroke.

Allowing the carriage to crash loudly into the stoppers on the return.
safetyNotes: Confirm that reformer spring tension is properly configured before lying down.

name: Precision Powerhouse Reformer Long Stretch
steps: Place hands on footbar and balls of feet against headrest in high plank.
Establish a long, rigid, continuous plank line.
Inhale and push carriage away by opening shoulder angle.
Exhale and pull carriage home by closing shoulders over footbar.
Maintain rigid core without sagging hips throughout.
tips: Keep shoulders depressed and long line from heels to crown.
Push and pull carriage purely from shoulder joints.
commonMistakes: Sagging hips toward springs.
Piking hips up into the air.
safetyNotes: Verify reformer springs are securely attached.
contraindications: Shoulder impingement.

name: Precision Powerhouse Reformer Short Box Round

steps: Place the short box crosswise over the reformer carriage and secure the safety foot strap.
Sit on the box facing the footbar and slip both feet securely under the safety strap.
Flex your ankles firmly against the strap and round your spine into a deep C-curve.
Wrap your arms around your midsection and draw your navel toward your spine.
Roll back over your sit bones, maintaining the rounded C-curve until arms reach horizontal.
Use your deep abdominals to curl back up over your pelvis without releasing the curve.

steps: Set up on hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
Inhale into cow pose by dropping your belly and lifting your chest and tailbone.
Exhale into cat pose by tucking your tailbone and rounding your spine up.
Press firmly through your palms to spread your shoulder blades apart.
Flow continuously between extension and flexion in rhythm with your breath.
tips: Articulate the movement vertebra by vertebra starting from your pelvis.

commonMistakes: Cramming into cervical hyperextension by jerking the chin up too far.

steps: Stand in an open doorway and place forearms flat against doorframe.
Position elbows at ninety degrees at shoulder height.
Step forward with one foot until you feel a gentle chest stretch.
Keep your neck relaxed and chest broad.
Hold the stretch for thirty seconds with steady breathing.
tips: Step gently forward to regulate stretch intensity.
Keep ribs pulled down.

Shrugging shoulders into ears.

Extend your right arm straight along the floor overhead.
Roll slowly along the outer ribcage and latissimus dorsi.
Pause on tight spots and take slow deep breaths.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Roll only along muscular tissue, avoiding lower ribs.

commonMistakes: Rolling directly onto floating lower ribs.

safetyNotes: Keep roller on muscular lat belly.

name: Prone Quadriceps Foam Rolling
steps: Lie prone on your mat with a foam roller under your thighs.
Support your upper body on your forearms in a low plank.
Roll slowly from the top of your hips down to just above knees.

Relax quadricep tissue.
commonMistakes: Rolling directly over the kneecap bone.

name: Prone Standing Hamstring Stretch
steps: Stand tall and place your right heel on a low bench or step.
Flex your right foot with toes pointing upward.
Hinge forward from your hips with a flat back.
Feel a gentle stretch through the back of your right thigh.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Hinge from the hips rather than rounding the lower back.
Keep your standing leg stable.
commonMistakes: Rounding the spine to force head toward knee.

Brace your core and lift your right knee toward your chest.

Rotate hip internally and drive heel toward ceiling.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Isolate the hip capsule without moving lower back.

commonMistakes: Arching or twisting your spine to compensate.
Rushing through sticky ranges.
safetyNotes: Move slowly with total joint control.
contraindications: Hip labral tear or severe impingement.

name: Prone Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
steps: Kneel on your left knee and step your right foot forward in a half-kneeling stance.
Maintain ninety-degree angles at both front and back knee joints.
Posteriorly tilt your pelvis by tucking your tailbone and squeezing your left glute.
Shift your hips forward slightly until you feel a deep stretch in front of your left hip.
Keep your torso completely vertical and hold the position for thirty seconds.

name: Prone Manual Hamstring
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart holding the bodyweight with a secure grip.
Engage your lats, pull your shoulders back, and brace your midsection firmly.
Hinge back at your hips while keeping a slight soft bend in your knees.
Lower the weight along your shins until you feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes tightly to stand tall.
tips: Keep the bar or weight in light contact with your legs throughout the pull.
Lock out by squeezing your glutes rather than leaning back from your lower back.
commonMistakes: Jerking the weight off the floor before building full lat tension.

safetyNotes: Never allow your spinal column to round aggressively under maximal pulling loads.

name: Prone 90-90 Hip Switch
steps: Sit on the floor with your front right leg bent at ninety degrees.
Position your trailing left leg bent at ninety degrees to your side.
Sit tall with your spine erect, using your hands behind you for support if needed.
Lift your knees and pivot on your heels to sweep your legs across to the left.
Finish in the mirror ninety-ninety position with your left leg leading in front.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.

Strive to perform the rotation without placing your hands on the ground as you progress.

name: Prone Quadruped Thoracic Rotation
steps: Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Place your right hand behind your head with elbow wide.
Rotate your right elbow down toward your left forearm on inhale.
Exhale and rotate your chest up toward ceiling, pointing elbow high.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.

Move smoothly with breath.
commonMistakes: Shifting hips sideways to cheat through rotation.

safetyNotes: Keep movement comfortable within joint range.
contraindications: Thoracic facet joint irritation.

name: Prone Standing Shoulder CARs
steps: Stand tall with a rigid braced core and fists clenched.
Raise your right straight arm forward and up past your ear.

Continue the circle backward, rotating arm internally as it reaches behind.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.

Move slowly through the entire circumference.
commonMistakes: Arching lower back when arm passes overhead.

name: Prone Resistance Band Shoulder Pass-Through
steps: Stand tall holding a light resistance band with a wide overhand grip.
Lock your elbows straight and hold the band across your front thighs.
Raise your arms up overhead in a wide smooth arc without bending elbows.
Continue the arc behind your back until the band lightly touches your glutes.
Reverse the arc smoothly to bring the band back overhead to the front.
Repeat for ten continuous fluid repetitions.

Keep your ribs pulled down and glutes squeezed to prevent lower back arching.

contraindications: Active anterior shoulder dislocation history or acute rotator cuff tear.

name: Prone Standing Quadriceps Stretch
steps: Stand tall on your left foot using a wall for balance if needed.
Bend your right knee and grasp your right ankle with right hand.
Gently pull your heel toward your glute while keeping knees aligned.
Tuck your pelvis under to increase the stretch along front thigh.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your knees together rather than letting working knee flare out.
Maintain tall posture.
commonMistakes: Arching lower back excessively.
Pulling ankle out to the side.
safetyNotes: Keep knees close together to protect ligaments.
contraindications: Patellofemoral pain syndrome.

name: Prone Thoracic Spine Foam Rolling
steps: Sit on your mat and position a foam roller horizontally across your mid-back.
Interlace your fingers behind your head to support the weight of your neck.
Lift your hips slightly and roll slowly between your mid-back and upper shoulders.
Pause at tight segments, lower your hips, and gently arch back over the roller.
Exhale smoothly as you extend your upper back over the roller.
Continue working your upper thoracic spine for the allotted sixty seconds.

name: prone twist on stability ball

name: Prone World's Greatest Stretch

Rotate your torso to the right and reach your right arm toward the ceiling.

Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.

Rotate from your upper back rather than twisting through your lumbar spine.

safetyNotes: Move smoothly between positions without snapping into end ranges.

name: push and pull bodyweight
steps: Lie back securely on the bench and grasp the bodyweight with hands slightly wider than shoulders.
Pull your shoulder blades together and plant both feet flat on the floor.
Lower the weight smoothly with elbows angled at roughly forty-five degrees.
Descend until the weight touches or hovers just above your chest.
Press the load back up powerfully until your arms reach full extension.
tips: Retract and depress your shoulder blades into the bench for solid shoulder stability.
Tuck your elbows at roughly forty-five degrees rather than flaring wide.
commonMistakes: Bouncing the weight off your sternum at the bottom.
Flaring your elbows wide at ninety degrees, placing high stress on the rotator cuff.
safetyNotes: Maintain a firm grip and verify bar collars are tightly clamped.
contraindications: Severe active rotator cuff impingement or acute AC joint sprain.

name: Push Press
steps: Hold the barbell at shoulder height with your wrists stacked directly over your elbows.
Tighten your glutes and brace your core to create a rigid foundation.

Lock out overhead with your arms straight and shoulders fully engaged.
Lower the weight under steady control back to the starting shoulder position.
tips: Squeeze your glutes and brace your core tightly to lock your pelvis in place.
Keep your forearms vertical beneath the load at the start of each rep.
commonMistakes: Leaning back excessively, turning the overhead press into an incline press.
Pressing the weight far out in front of your center of mass.
safetyNotes: Avoid excessive lumbar hyperextension under overhead pressing loads.
contraindications: Acute subacromial shoulder impingement or symptomatic cervical disc pathology.

name: Pyramid Interval 500m Rowing Ergometer Sprint
steps: Strap feet firmly into footrests and set damper to medium.
Drive hard with legs off the catch with locked core.
Swing torso back and accelerate handle into lower ribs.
Take quick, snappy recovery strokes with high stroke rate.
Sprint maximal effort until completing five hundred meters.
tips: Legs initiate ninety percent of sprint power.
Keep back straight and avoid slouching under fatigue.
commonMistakes: Shooting the seat back before driving the handle.
Rounding lower back into slumped posture.
safetyNotes: Keep core braced to protect lumbar spine at high stroke rates.

name: Pyramid Interval Backstroke Lap Swimming
steps: Push off pool wall supine in horizontal streamline.
Flutter kick continuously with relaxed pointed toes.
Rotate torso to sweep arm straight out of water thumb first.
Catch water with pinky finger and drive down toward thigh.
Breathe continuously with one breath per arm stroke cycle.
tips: Keep hips high near water surface by looking up.
Rotate shoulders with each arm entry.
commonMistakes: Sitting in the water and letting hips sink low.
Bending knees excessively during kick.
safetyNotes: Count strokes to anticipate pool wall turn.
contraindications: Shoulder impingement.

name: Pyramid Interval Breaststroke Lap Swimming
steps: Glide forward in streamline beneath the surface.
Pull hands out and sweep inward toward chest.
Lift head to breathe naturally as hands sweep in.
Whip feet in a circular frog kick to drive forward.
Glide long in streamline before beginning next stroke cycle.
tips: Emphasize the streamline glide phase between kicks.
Kick from knees and ankles without splaying hips too wide.
commonMistakes: Kicking with asymmetrical legs.
Lifting head too high out of the water.
safetyNotes: Avoid kicking if medial knee pain occurs.
contraindications: Swimmer knee MCL strain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Pyramid Interval Outdoor Brisk Walking
steps: Stand tall with shoulders relaxed and chest proud.
Walk forward at a purposeful pace of roughly four miles per hour.
Push actively off your trailing big toe on each stride.
Swing arms rhythmically at ninety-degree angles.
Maintain continuous brisk cadence throughout target distance.
tips: Walk with purpose: brisk enough to raise breathing rate.
Land softly heel to toe.
commonMistakes: Shuffling flat-footed without pushing off toes.
Slouching forward.
safetyNotes: Wear supportive walking shoes.
contraindications: Severe plantar heel spurs.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Pyramid Interval Elliptical Trainer Intervals
steps: Step onto elliptical pedals and grasp moving handlebars firmly.
Select interval resistance profile on machine console.
Drive pedals in smooth elliptical circles while pumping arms.
Push pace to maximal effort during high-intensity intervals.
Recover with steady aerobic gliding during rest intervals.
tips: Push and pull actively with arms to engage upper body.
Keep whole foot in contact with footplate.
commonMistakes: Slouching over the console.
Letting heels peel high off footplates.
safetyNotes: Maintain upright spinal posture throughout.
contraindications: Plantar fasciitis.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Pyramid Interval Freestyle Lap Swimming
steps: Push off the pool wall in a streamlined horizontal position beneath the surface.
Flutter kick from your hips with relaxed pointed ankles.
Enter the water with your hand fingertip-first and extend forward into the catch.
Pull your hand and forearm backward through the water toward your hip.
Rotate your torso to breathe naturally in the pocket created by your bow wave.
Recover your arm high over the water surface to initiate the next stroke entry.
tips: Keep your head neutral with eyes looking straight at the bottom of the pool.
Rotate your hips and torso as a single connected unit with every stroke.
commonMistakes: Lifting the head high out of the water to breathe, causing hips to sink downward.
Bending the knees excessively while kicking, creating heavy drag.
safetyNotes: Always swim in designated lanes with certified lifeguard coverage present.
contraindications: Tympanic membrane perforation without custom earplugs, or acute swimmer shoulder.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Pyramid Interval Indoor Rowing Ergometer
steps: Strap your feet into the footrests and grip the handle with an overhand grip.
Begin at the catch with shins vertical, arms straight, and torso leaning slightly forward.
Initiate the drive by pushing aggressively through your legs until knees are almost straight.
Swing your torso back to eleven o'clock and pull the handle into your lower ribs.
Reverse the motion on the recovery: extend arms, hinge torso forward, then slide knees forward.
tips: Power breakdown on the drive is sixty percent legs, twenty core, twenty arms.
Do not bend your knees on the recovery slide until the handle clears your knees.
commonMistakes: Shooting the slide by pushing legs without transferring force through a braced core.
Bending the knees too early on the return and clipping the handle over kneecaps.
safetyNotes: Keep your spine neutral on the catch; never slouch into rounded lumbar flexion.
contraindications: Acute lumbar disc herniation aggravated by combined seated compression and flexion.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Pyramid Interval Outdoor Road Running
steps: Establish an upright posture with a slight forward lean originating from your ankles.
Run forward with a steady cadence of roughly one hundred seventy steps per minute.
Land with your foot landing softly underneath your center of mass.
Drive your elbows backward in rhythm with your opposite leg strides.
Maintain relaxed shoulders and breathe rhythmically through nose and mouth.
tips: Avoid overstriding with a harsh braking heel strike ahead of your body.
Keep your hands relaxed as if holding a potato chip without crushing it.
commonMistakes: Overstriding and landing heavily on a stiff heel out in front.
Hunching shoulders upward toward your ears under fatigue.
safetyNotes: Wear cushioned, properly fitted footwear and build weekly mileage progressively.
contraindications: Severe medial tibial stress syndrome (shin splints) or acute stress fracture.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Pyramid Interval Indoor Spin Bike Sprints
aliases: Pyramid Interval Indoor Spin Bike Sprints
steps: Mount spin bike with balls of feet strapped securely into pedals.
Increase flywheel resistance to match sprint torque.
Stand out of saddle and drive pedals with explosive downward force.
Sprint at maximal cadence of over one hundred ten rpm.
Sit back down into saddle as interval expires.
tips: Keep resistance high enough to prevent flywheel bouncing.
Keep hips back over the saddle when standing.
commonMistakes: Sprinting with zero resistance, spinning out hips.
Leaning all bodyweight onto handlebars.
safetyNotes: Ensure flywheel resistance is engaged before standing sprint.
contraindications: Knee chondromalacia.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Pyramid Interval Stair Climber Intervals
steps: Step onto the revolving stairs and select your target interval climbing speed.
Stand tall with your chest lifted and avoid leaning heavily on the side handrails.
Place your entire foot flat on each moving step as you climb.
Push through your heel and midfoot to activate glutes on every upward step.
Maintain a steady rhythmic climbing cadence without skipping steps.
Safely press the stop button and wait for steps to lock before dismounting.
tips: Rest your fingertips on handrails for balance only; do not support your weight on arms.
Keep your torso upright with a slight natural forward lean from the hips.
commonMistakes: Slouching forward and locking arms out to support bodyweight on the rails.
Stepping only on the balls of your feet, placing excessive strain on calves.
safetyNotes: Keep your gaze on the revolving stairs to avoid mistiming steps and tripping.
contraindications: Severe patellofemoral knee arthritis or acute Achilles tendonitis.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Pyramid Interval Stationary Cycling
steps: Adjust the saddle height so your knee has a slight bend at the bottom pedal stroke.
Mount the bike and secure the balls of your feet over the pedal axles.
Grip the handlebars lightly and establish a steady pedaling cadence of eighty to ninety rpm.
Push smoothly down on each downstroke and scrape back across the bottom stroke.
Maintain an upright or athletic forward posture without collapsing your chest.
Breathe steadily and consistently through your designated training interval.
tips: Pedal in smooth circles rather than merely stomping downward on the pedals.
Keep your knees tracking straight forward rather than flaring out.
commonMistakes: Setting the saddle too low, causing excessive compressive knee joint stress.
Gripping the handlebars with excessive white-knuckle forearm tension.
safetyNotes: Verify the saddle and handlebar clamping pins are tightly secured before riding.
contraindications: Severe ischial tuberosity bursitis or acute knee effusion.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Pyramid Interval Tempo Road Running
steps: Settle into your threshold tempo pace with an upright posture.
Maintain a cadence of one hundred seventy to one hundred eighty steps per minute.
Land midfoot beneath your center of mass with quiet steps.
Keep breathing rhythmic with two steps inhale and two steps exhale.
Maintain steady pace throughout the designated tempo distance.
tips: Run comfortably hard: sustainable for roughly one hour.
Keep shoulders relaxed and arms swinging compactly.
commonMistakes: Starting too fast and falling off pace midway.
Overstriding with heel strike braking.
safetyNotes: Progress training volume by at most ten percent weekly.
contraindications: Tibial stress fracture.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Quadruped Mobility Flow Cat-Cow Dynamic Stretch
aliases: Quadruped Mobility Flow Cat-Cow Dynamic Stretch
steps: Set up on hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
Inhale into cow pose by dropping your belly and lifting your chest and tailbone.
Exhale into cat pose by tucking your tailbone and rounding your spine up.
Press firmly through your palms to spread your shoulder blades apart.
Flow continuously between extension and flexion in rhythm with your breath.
tips: Articulate the movement vertebra by vertebra starting from your pelvis.
Keep your elbows unlocked throughout the transition.
commonMistakes: Cramming into cervical hyperextension by jerking the chin up too far.
Moving with rapid uncontrolled pace rather than smooth segmental articulation.
safetyNotes: Stay within a comfortable pain-free range of motion without forcing end ranges.
contraindications: Severe acute disc prolapse aggravated by flexion.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Quadruped Mobility Flow Doorway Pectoral Stretch
aliases: Quadruped Mobility Flow Doorway Pectoral Stretch
steps: Stand in an open doorway and place forearms flat against doorframe.
Position elbows at ninety degrees at shoulder height.
Step forward with one foot until you feel a gentle chest stretch.
Keep your neck relaxed and chest broad.
Hold the stretch for thirty seconds with steady breathing.
tips: Step gently forward to regulate stretch intensity.
Keep ribs pulled down.
commonMistakes: Pressing forward with aggressive sudden force.
Shrugging shoulders into ears.
safetyNotes: Do not over-stretch anterior shoulder capsule.
contraindications: Anterior shoulder instability.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Quadruped Mobility Flow Latissimus Dorsi Foam Rolling
aliases: Quadruped Mobility Flow Latissimus Dorsi Foam Rolling
steps: Lie on your right side with a foam roller beneath your armpit.
Extend your right arm straight along the floor overhead.
Roll slowly along the outer ribcage and latissimus dorsi.
Pause on tight spots and take slow deep breaths.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Roll only along muscular tissue, avoiding lower ribs.
Regulate pressure using your feet.
commonMistakes: Rolling directly onto floating lower ribs.
Tensing up and holding breath.
safetyNotes: Keep roller on muscular lat belly.
contraindications: Osteoporosis or rib fracture.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Quadruped Mobility Flow Quadriceps Foam Rolling
aliases: Quadruped Mobility Flow Quadriceps Foam Rolling
steps: Lie prone on your mat with a foam roller under your thighs.
Support your upper body on your forearms in a low plank.
Roll slowly from the top of your hips down to just above knees.
Pause and breathe on tender trigger points for twenty seconds.
Continue rolling along the muscle belly for sixty seconds.
tips: Keep your core gently braced to prevent lower back sagging.
Relax quadricep tissue.
commonMistakes: Rolling directly over the kneecap bone.
Holding your breath while rolling tender areas.
safetyNotes: Never roll directly onto bone or joint capsules.
contraindications: Acute thigh hematoma.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Quadruped Mobility Flow Standing Hamstring Stretch
aliases: Quadruped Mobility Flow Standing Hamstring Stretch
steps: Stand tall and place your right heel on a low bench or step.
Flex your right foot with toes pointing upward.
Hinge forward from your hips with a flat back.
Feel a gentle stretch through the back of your right thigh.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Hinge from the hips rather than rounding the lower back.
Keep your standing leg stable.
commonMistakes: Rounding the spine to force head toward knee.
Locking knee into painful hyperextension.
safetyNotes: Avoid aggressive stretching into sharp pain.
contraindications: Acute hamstring tear.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Quadruped Mobility Flow Quadruped Hip CARs
aliases: Quadruped Mobility Flow Quadruped Hip CARs
steps: Assume a quadruped tabletop position on your hands and knees.
Brace your core and lift your right knee toward your chest.
Open your right knee out to the side in abduction.
Rotate hip internally and drive heel toward ceiling.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Isolate the hip capsule without moving lower back.
Imagine tracing the biggest circle possible.
commonMistakes: Arching or twisting your spine to compensate.
Rushing through sticky ranges.
safetyNotes: Move slowly with total joint control.
contraindications: Hip labral tear or severe impingement.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Quadruped Mobility Flow Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
aliases: Quadruped Mobility Flow Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
steps: Kneel on your left knee and step your right foot forward in a half-kneeling stance.
Maintain ninety-degree angles at both front and back knee joints.
Posteriorly tilt your pelvis by tucking your tailbone and squeezing your left glute.
Shift your hips forward slightly until you feel a deep stretch in front of your left hip.
Keep your torso completely vertical and hold the position for thirty seconds.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: The posterior pelvic tilt is what isolates the psoas; do not arch your lower back.
Raise your left arm overhead to intensify the stretch through the entire fascial line.
commonMistakes: Hyperextending the lumbar spine and dumping all forward travel into the lower back.
Failing to contract the trailing glute during the hold.
safetyNotes: Place a folded mat or cushion under the rear knee for comfort.
contraindications: Acute patellar bursitis on the kneeling knee or acute hip labral pathology.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Quadruped Mobility Flow 90-90 Hip Switch
steps: Sit on the floor with your front right leg bent at ninety degrees.
Position your trailing left leg bent at ninety degrees to your side.
Sit tall with your spine erect, using your hands behind you for support if needed.
Lift your knees and pivot on your heels to sweep your legs across to the left.
Finish in the mirror ninety-ninety position with your left leg leading in front.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your heels anchored into the ground as you transition between sides.
Strive to perform the rotation without placing your hands on the ground as you progress.
commonMistakes: Slouching through the lower back to compensate for limited hip capsule rotation.
Letting knees collapse with uncontrolled momentum.
safetyNotes: Do not force end-range internal rotation if you feel pinching inside the hip joint.
contraindications: Hip labral tear with femoral acetabular impingement (FAI).

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Quadruped Mobility Flow Quadruped Thoracic Rotation
aliases: Quadruped Mobility Flow Quadruped Thoracic Rotation
steps: Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Place your right hand behind your head with elbow wide.
Rotate your right elbow down toward your left forearm on inhale.
Exhale and rotate your chest up toward ceiling, pointing elbow high.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Rotate from your upper thoracic back, keeping hips square.
Move smoothly with breath.
commonMistakes: Shifting hips sideways to cheat through rotation.
Pulling on the neck with the hand.
safetyNotes: Keep movement comfortable within joint range.
contraindications: Thoracic facet joint irritation.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Quadruped Mobility Flow Standing Shoulder CARs
aliases: Quadruped Mobility Flow Standing Shoulder CARs
steps: Stand tall with a rigid braced core and fists clenched.
Raise your right straight arm forward and up past your ear.
At peak overhead height, rotate your bicep outward.
Continue the circle backward, rotating arm internally as it reaches behind.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Do not let your torso twist or arch to assist the arm.
Move slowly through the entire circumference.
commonMistakes: Arching lower back when arm passes overhead.
Shrugging shoulder up into ear.
safetyNotes: Work strictly in pain-free joint range.
contraindications: Rotator cuff impingement.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Quadruped Mobility Flow Resistance Band Shoulder Pass-Through
aliases: Quadruped Mobility Flow Resistance Band Shoulder Pass-Through
steps: Stand tall holding a light resistance band with a wide overhand grip.
Lock your elbows straight and hold the band across your front thighs.
Raise your arms up overhead in a wide smooth arc without bending elbows.
Continue the arc behind your back until the band lightly touches your glutes.
Reverse the arc smoothly to bring the band back overhead to the front.
Repeat for ten continuous fluid repetitions.
tips: Widen your grip on the band if your elbows bend during the pass-through.
Keep your ribs pulled down and glutes squeezed to prevent lower back arching.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows as the band passes overhead.
Over-arching the spine to cheat through shoulder tightness.
safetyNotes: Use a wide enough grip so the band passes smoothly without sharp shoulder pain.
contraindications: Active anterior shoulder dislocation history or acute rotator cuff tear.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Quadruped Mobility Flow Standing Quadriceps Stretch
aliases: Quadruped Mobility Flow Standing Quadriceps Stretch
steps: Stand tall on your left foot using a wall for balance if needed.
Bend your right knee and grasp your right ankle with right hand.
Gently pull your heel toward your glute while keeping knees aligned.
Tuck your pelvis under to increase the stretch along front thigh.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your knees together rather than letting working knee flare out.
Maintain tall posture.
commonMistakes: Arching lower back excessively.
Pulling ankle out to the side.
safetyNotes: Keep knees close together to protect ligaments.
contraindications: Patellofemoral pain syndrome.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Quadruped Mobility Flow Thoracic Spine Foam Rolling
aliases: Quadruped Mobility Flow Thoracic Spine Foam Rolling
steps: Sit on your mat and position a foam roller horizontally across your mid-back.
Interlace your fingers behind your head to support the weight of your neck.
Lift your hips slightly and roll slowly between your mid-back and upper shoulders.
Pause at tight segments, lower your hips, and gently arch back over the roller.
Exhale smoothly as you extend your upper back over the roller.
Continue working your upper thoracic spine for the allotted sixty seconds.
tips: Keep your elbows pointed forward to pull shoulder blades apart and expose tissue.
Never roll down onto your unsupported lumbar spine.
commonMistakes: Rolling onto the lower back or neck vertebrae directly.
Pulling violently on your head and hyper-flexing your cervical spine.
safetyNotes: Keep the roller strictly on the rib-supported thoracic region between shoulder blades.
contraindications: Osteoporosis, vertebral compression fractures, or unhealed rib injury.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Quadruped Mobility Flow World's Greatest Stretch
aliases: Quadruped Mobility Flow World's Greatest Stretch
steps: Step forward into a deep lunge with your right foot outside your right hand.
Place your left hand on the floor and lower your right elbow inside your right ankle.
Rotate your torso to the right and reach your right arm toward the ceiling.
Gaze up toward your right hand while keeping your left hip flexor extended.
Bring your right hand back down, rock back, and straighten your right front leg.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your back knee extended and back glute fired to maximize hip flexor opening.
Rotate from your upper back rather than twisting through your lumbar spine.
commonMistakes: Collapsing your back knee onto the floor during the rotational phase.
Craning your neck to compensate for limited thoracic spine rotation.
safetyNotes: Move smoothly between positions without snapping into end ranges.
contraindications: Acute groin adductor strain or lumbar facet joint irritation.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Quadruped Thoracic Rotation
steps: Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Place your right hand behind your head with elbow wide.
Rotate your right elbow down toward your left forearm on inhale.
Exhale and rotate your chest up toward ceiling, pointing elbow high.
Complete repetitions, then switch sides and repeat with left arm.
tips: Rotate from your upper thoracic back, keeping hips square.
Move smoothly with breath.
commonMistakes: Shifting hips sideways to cheat through rotation.
Pulling on the neck with the hand.
safetyNotes: Keep movement comfortable within joint range.
contraindications: Thoracic facet joint irritation.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: quads
steps: Set up with your feet shoulder-width apart holding the bodyweight securely in position.
Brace your core and inhale deeply to build intra-abdominal pressure.
Hinge your hips back and bend your knees to lower under control.
Descend until your thighs reach parallel to the floor with knees tracking over toes.
Drive firmly through your midfoot and heels to return to standing lockout.
tips: Keep your chest proud and drive your knees outward in line with your toes.
Maintain full midfoot balance throughout the descent and ascent.
commonMistakes: Letting knees cave inward during the upward drive.
Allowing your lower back to round into pelvic wink at bottom depth.
safetyNotes: Always set safety spotter arms just below your target depth before loading heavy weights.
contraindications: Avoid heavy spinal loading during acute lumbar disc flare-ups or acute knee meniscus tears.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: quarter sit-up
steps: Set up in position with the bodyweight and brace your core firmly.
Initiate the movement by contracting your target muscles through a full active range.
Exhale smoothly as you reach peak muscular contraction.
Pause for one second to maximize tension before returning under control.
Reverse the motion smoothly to the starting position.
tips: Draw your belly button toward your spine to engage the transverse abdominis.
Exhale completely at peak contraction to deepen abdominal recruitment.
commonMistakes: Hyperextending the lower back when fatigued during core drills.
Pulling with your neck instead of flexing from your abdominal muscles.
safetyNotes: Do not pull on the back of your neck with your hands during core flexions.
contraindications: Acute lumbar disc herniation aggravated by spinal flexion or twisting.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: quick feet v. 2
steps: Set up with your feet shoulder-width apart holding the bodyweight securely in position.
Brace your core and inhale deeply to build intra-abdominal pressure.
Hinge your hips back and bend your knees to lower under control.
Descend until your thighs reach parallel to the floor with knees tracking over toes.
Drive firmly through your midfoot and heels to return to standing lockout.
tips: Keep your chest proud and drive your knees outward in line with your toes.
Maintain full midfoot balance throughout the descent and ascent.
commonMistakes: Letting knees cave inward during the upward drive.
Allowing your lower back to round into pelvic wink at bottom depth.
safetyNotes: Always set safety spotter arms just below your target depth before loading heavy weights.
contraindications: Avoid heavy spinal loading during acute lumbar disc flare-ups or acute knee meniscus tears.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Rack Delivery
steps: Hold the barbell at shoulder height with your wrists stacked directly over your elbows.
Tighten your glutes and brace your core to create a rigid foundation.
Press the load vertically overhead in a smooth path close to your face.
Lock out overhead with your arms straight and shoulders fully engaged.
Lower the weight under steady control back to the starting shoulder position.
tips: Squeeze your glutes and brace your core tightly to lock your pelvis in place.
Keep your forearms vertical beneath the load at the start of each rep.
commonMistakes: Leaning back excessively, turning the overhead press into an incline press.
Pressing the weight far out in front of your center of mass.
safetyNotes: Avoid excessive lumbar hyperextension under overhead pressing loads.
contraindications: Acute subacromial shoulder impingement or symptomatic cervical disc pathology.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Rack Pull with Bands
steps: Lie back securely on the bench and grasp the barbell with hands slightly wider than shoulders.
Pull your shoulder blades together and plant both feet flat on the floor.
Lower the weight smoothly with elbows angled at roughly forty-five degrees.
Descend until the weight touches or hovers just above your chest.
Press the load back up powerfully until your arms reach full extension.
tips: Retract and depress your shoulder blades into the bench for solid shoulder stability.
Tuck your elbows at roughly forty-five degrees rather than flaring wide.
commonMistakes: Bouncing the weight off your sternum at the bottom.
Flaring your elbows wide at ninety degrees, placing high stress on the rotator cuff.
safetyNotes: Maintain a firm grip and verify bar collars are tightly clamped.
contraindications: Severe active rotator cuff impingement or acute AC joint sprain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Rack Pulls

Lower the weight smoothly with elbows angled at roughly forty-five degrees.

name: raise single arm push-up
steps: Lie back securely on the bench and grasp the bodyweight with hands slightly wider than shoulders.
Pull your shoulder blades together and plant both feet flat on the floor.
Lower the weight smoothly with elbows angled at roughly forty-five degrees.
Descend until the weight touches or hovers just above your chest.
Complete the target reps, then switch sides and repeat the movement.
tips: Retract and depress your shoulder blades into the bench for solid shoulder stability.
Tuck your elbows at roughly forty-five degrees rather than flaring wide.
commonMistakes: Bouncing the weight off your sternum at the bottom.
Flaring your elbows wide at ninety degrees, placing high stress on the rotator cuff.
safetyNotes: Maintain a firm grip and verify bar collars are tightly clamped.
