name: Seated Standing Quadriceps Stretch
steps: Stand tall on your left foot using a wall for balance if needed.
Bend your right knee and grasp your right ankle with right hand.
Gently pull your heel toward your glute while keeping knees aligned.
Tuck your pelvis under to increase the stretch along front thigh.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your knees together rather than letting working knee flare out.
Maintain tall posture.
commonMistakes: Arching lower back excessively.
Pulling ankle out to the side.
safetyNotes: Keep knees close together to protect ligaments.
contraindications: Patellofemoral pain syndrome.

name: Seated Thoracic Spine Foam Rolling
steps: Sit on your mat and position a foam roller horizontally across your mid-back.
Interlace your fingers behind your head to support the weight of your neck.
Lift your hips slightly and roll slowly between your mid-back and upper shoulders.
Pause at tight segments, lower your hips, and gently arch back over the roller.
Exhale smoothly as you extend your upper back over the roller.
Continue working your upper thoracic spine for the allotted sixty seconds.
tips: Keep your elbows pointed forward to pull shoulder blades apart and expose tissue.
Never roll down onto your unsupported lumbar spine.
commonMistakes: Rolling onto the lower back or neck vertebrae directly.
Pulling violently on your head and hyper-flexing your cervical spine.
safetyNotes: Keep the roller strictly on the rib-supported thoracic region between shoulder blades.
contraindications: Osteoporosis, vertebral compression fractures, or unhealed rib injury.

name: Bridge Pose
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on mat, hip-width apart.
Slide your heels close enough so your fingertips can lightly touch them.

Interlace your fingers beneath your back and roll onto the outer tops of shoulders.
Engage your glutes and keep thighs parallel to each other.

name: Shadowboxing Boxer Jump Rope Alternating Step

Shift your weight from foot to foot as if lightly jogging in place.
Tap the ball of your right foot, then left foot on each rope pass.
Keep your torso vertical and shoulders relaxed.
Maintain the alternating boxer skip cadence for the target duration.

Establish a rhythmic two-beat boxer bounce.
commonMistakes: Kicking legs out too far forward or backward.
Tensing shoulders and neck.

name: Shadowboxing Boxer Jump Rope Basic Bounce

steps: Hold jump rope handles with elbows tucked near your waist.
Rotate wrists smoothly to turn the rope around your body.
Jump one to two inches off the floor on the balls of both feet.
Land softly with slightly bent knees on every revolution.
Maintain a light, continuous, rhythmic bouncing cadence for three minutes.
tips: Turn the rope using small wrist rotations, not large arm circles.
Stay on the balls of your feet; heels should not touch the floor.
commonMistakes: Jumping too high and wasting energy.
Flaring elbows wide away from your ribcage.

name: Shadowboxing Backward Retreat Step
steps: Start in orthodox stance with hands held high in guard.
Step backward three to five inches with your rear back foot.
Push off the ball of your lead front foot to propel yourself backward.
Slide your lead foot back the exact same distance to reset stance.
Keep your chin tucked and guard solid as you retreat out of range.
tips: Step first with the back foot when moving backward.
Keep your center of gravity centered between both legs.
commonMistakes: Stepping backward with front foot first, crossing feet.
Leaning torso backward away from feet.

contraindications: Achilles tendon strain.

name: Shadowboxing Bob and Weave
steps: Assume your boxing stance as a horizontal hook is launched.
Drop beneath the punch by bending both knees into a quarter-squat.
Trace a smooth U-shape with your head moving under and across the arc.
Rise up on the opposite side of the hook with hips loaded to counter.
Keep your hands firmly protecting your chin throughout the weave.

Stay in punching range as you come up on the opposite side.
commonMistakes: Bending at the waist and bending neck down into danger.
Standing straight up in the middle of the opponent punch.
safetyNotes: Maintain continuous visual contact with opponent.
contraindications: Meniscus knee strain or lower back pain.

name: Shadowboxing Defensive Check Hook (3)

Pivot sharply on the ball of your lead left foot, swinging your rear leg back.
Turn your body ninety degrees away from the opponent charging line.
Whip punch 3 (lead hook) across as you pivot your hips out of range.
Exit on the safe outside angle with hands returned to guard.
Complete the drill, then repeat on the opposite side.
tips: The check hook uses the opponent forward momentum against them.
Pivot your rear leg like opening a door on a hinge.
commonMistakes: Throwing the hook without pivoting the feet, getting tackled forward.
Dropping the rear defensive hand.
safetyNotes: Maintain stable foot pivot to avoid slipping.
contraindications: Acute ankle sprain or knee torsion.

Snap both hands back to defensive cheek guard.

Keep your chin tucked and non-punching hand in guard.

Over-committing balance forward.

name: Shadowboxing Boxing Combination: Slip Left - Cross - Hook - Cross (slip-2-3-2)
aliases: Shadowboxing Boxing Combination: Slip Left - Cross - Hook - Cross (slip-2-3-2)
steps: Slip outside an incoming jab by shifting weight to rear leg.
Fire counter punch 2 (cross) directly over opponent arm.
Pivot to whip punch 3 (lead hook) to temple.
Finish with powerful punch 2 (cross) down the middle.
Snap both hands back to defensive cheekbones.
tips: Reference the numbered punches 1-6 smoothly without pauses.
Keep your chin tucked and non-punching hand in guard.
commonMistakes: Dropping the rear hand during combinations.
Over-committing balance forward.
safetyNotes: Maintain wrist alignment and wrap hands properly.
contraindications: Wrist fracture or carpal instability.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Shadowboxing Cross - Lead Hook - Cross (2-3-2)
steps: Initiate with a powerful counter punch 2 (rear cross).
Pivot on your lead foot to whip punch 3 (lead hook) to the temple.
Pivot back on your rear foot and drive punch 2 (cross) straight down middle.
Keep your balance centered between both legs throughout.
Recoil back into your tight defensive guard.
tips: This power combo uses alternating hip torque: right-left-right.
Keep your lead shoulder high to protect your jaw.
commonMistakes: Over-committing on punch 2 and falling forward into opponent.
Dropping the non-punching hand.
safetyNotes: Maintain full foot contact with the floor on pivots.
contraindications: Rotator cuff tendonitis.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Shadowboxing Duck Defense
steps: Begin in your boxing stance with your hands held tightly in guard.
Bend at both knees, lowering your body straight down four to six inches.
Allow incoming horizontal hooks to pass safely over your head.
Keep your eyes fixed straight ahead on your opponent torso.
Drive through your heels to return immediately to your tall guard.
tips: Bend at your knees like an athletic squat, not at your lower back.
Keep your chin tucked and elbows tight to your ribs.
commonMistakes: Bending forward at the waist and looking down at the floor.
Duck-walking too deep and getting trapped underneath.
safetyNotes: Never take your eyes off your opponent while ducking.
contraindications: Patellofemoral knee overload.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Shadowboxing 45-Degree Lead Pivot
steps: Stand in orthodox stance with sixty percent weight on lead left foot.
Pivot on the ball of your lead foot while swinging rear leg forty-five degrees to right.
Create a fresh dominant angle outside the opponent front shoulder.
Plant your rear foot firmly to re-establish your balanced base.
Keep your hands in full defensive guard during the entire pivot.
tips: Pivot like a compass with your lead foot acting as the needle.
Turn your hips with the pivot to align punches on the new angle.
commonMistakes: Lifting the lead heel and stumbling off balance.
Dropping hands while pivoting.
safetyNotes: Keep core braced throughout the rotational pivot.
contraindications: Ankle sprain or knee meniscus twist.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Shadowboxing Forward Shuffle Step
steps: Begin in your balanced boxing stance with weight on balls of feet.
Step forward two to four inches with your lead front foot.
Push off the ball of your rear foot to drive the forward movement.
Slide your rear foot forward the exact same distance to restore your stance.
Maintain your standard shoulder-width base without crossing feet.
tips: Always step with the foot closest to the direction you want to travel.
Stay light on the balls of your feet with heels lightly floating.
commonMistakes: Dragging the back foot lazily and narrowing your stance base.
Crossing your feet while stepping forward.
safetyNotes: Maintain athletic knee bend to absorb movement.
contraindications: Acute ankle instability.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Shadowboxing Lead Body Jab (1b)
steps: Begin in your standard boxing stance with elbows tucked in guard.
Change levels by bending your knees and dropping your hips downward.
Step forward with your lead foot and drive punch 1 directly toward opponent solar plexus.
Keep your rear hand glued to your cheek to protect against counter-punches.
Push off your lead foot to snap back into tall guard position.
tips: Bend your knees to change levels rather than bending only at your waist.
Keep your eyes locked on the opponent chest and eyes.
commonMistakes: Bending at the waist and looking down at the floor.
Leaving the rear defensive hand low during the body shot.
safetyNotes: Keep rear guard high to protect against overhand counters.
contraindications: Acute lumbar facet strain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Shadowboxing Lead Jab (1)
steps: Begin in your orthodox boxing stance with your hands held up in guard.
Step forward lightly with your lead left foot as you fire your left fist forward.
Rotate your fist over so your palm faces down at the moment of impact.
Shrug your lead shoulder upward to guard your chin against incoming counters.
Snap your left fist back along the exact same path to your defensive guard position.
tips: The 1 jab is a crisp whip: throw it relaxed and clench your fist on contact.
Keep your rear right hand glued to your cheekbone while throwing the jab.
commonMistakes: Dropping your left hand to your chest before extending the punch.
Over-committing your weight forward and falling off balance.
safetyNotes: Wrap your hands properly and keep your wrist straight to prevent sprains.
contraindications: Acute scaphoid wrist fracture or carpal instability.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Shadowboxing Lead Shovel Hook to Liver (3b)
aliases: Shadowboxing Lead Shovel Hook to Liver (3b)
steps: Assume an orthodox stance within inside fighting distance.
Dip your torso slightly to the left by bending your knees.
Drive upward and inward at a forty-five-degree angle with punch 3.
Target the opponent right floating rib where the liver sits.
Snap the punch back immediately to your protective left cheek guard.
tips: The shovel hook is half-hook, half-uppercut driven by the legs.
Keep your elbow tucked close to your ribs until release.
commonMistakes: Telegraphing the punch by winding your arm backward.
Dropping your rear hand during the inside attack.
safetyNotes: Maintain compact elbow angle to avoid hyperextension.
contraindications: Acute shoulder labral strain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Shadowboxing Orthodox Lead Hook (3)
steps: Begin in your orthodox guard position with hands protecting your jaw.
Shift bodyweight slightly toward your lead left foot.
Pivot sharply on the ball of your lead foot like squashing a bug.
Whip your left arm horizontally into punch 3 with elbow bent ninety degrees.
Align your wrist, elbow, and shoulder in one horizontal plane on impact.
Recoil your left fist immediately back to your cheek in guard.
tips: Power comes from the lead foot pivot and torso rotation, not arm swinging.
Keep your rear right hand glued to your cheek to absorb counters.
commonMistakes: Looping the hook too wide and exposing your chest to counters.
Dropping the rear hand while throwing the lead hook.
safetyNotes: Keep your wrist stiff and forearm horizontal to prevent sprains.
contraindications: Acute rotator cuff tear or wrist TFCC tear.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Shadowboxing Orthodox Lead Uppercut (5)
steps: Begin in your orthodox guard with knees softly flexed.
Dip your left shoulder slightly and drop your left hand three inches.
Drive upward through your legs and rotate your left hip inward.
Thrust punch 5 vertically upward with palm facing your chest.
Target the opponent chin or solar plexus along the centerline.
Retract your left fist back to your defensive cheek guard.
tips: Power comes from leg drive and hip rotation, not lifting with your arm.
Keep the punch compact and close to your body.
commonMistakes: Dropping the hand down to the waist before punching, telegraphing.
Over-extending and exposing your entire face to counters.
safetyNotes: Keep the trajectory compact along the centerline.
contraindications: Acute bicep tendonitis or wrist sprain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Shadowboxing Orthodox Rear Hook (4)
steps: Establish your orthodox stance with your hands in full guard.
Pivot forcefully on the ball of your rear right foot.
Rotate your right hip forward and whip punch 4 in a horizontal arc.
Keep your elbow bent at ninety degrees and locked in line with wrist.
Keep your lead left hand firmly glued to your left cheek.
Retract the punch smoothly along the arc back to your face.
tips: Rotate your entire torso as a single connected unit.
Do not wind up; launch the punch directly from your cheek.
commonMistakes: Over-swinging and missing the target, spinning yourself out of position.
Dropping the opposite lead hand.
safetyNotes: Ensure proper wrist wrapping to cushion hook impacts.
contraindications: Carpal fractures or shoulder impingement.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Shadowboxing Orthodox Rear Uppercut (6)
steps: Start in your orthodox stance with both hands in guard.
Dip your right shoulder slightly and pivot on the ball of your rear foot.
Drive upward through your rear leg and thrust punch 6 vertically.
Keep your palm facing your chest with elbow tucked close to ribcage.
Drive through the target and retract your right hand instantly to your cheek.
tips: The 6 uppercut requires full rear hip extension.
Keep your lead left hand firmly in guard on your left cheek.
commonMistakes: Dropping the rear hand low and loading up visibly.
Leaving your chin exposed at the top of the punch.
safetyNotes: Never drop hand below waist level before launching uppercut.
contraindications: Acromioclavicular shoulder strain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Shadowboxing Overhand Right Punch
steps: Establish an orthodox stance with your weight balanced over your feet.
Slip your head slightly to the left outside the opponent jab line.
Pivot your rear right foot and loop your right fist over the top in an arc.
Turn your thumb downward at impact with elbow elevated high above fist.
Keep your lead left hand pinned to your left jawline.
Recover your balance and snap your right fist back to guard.
tips: Slip your head off the centerline as you throw to evade incoming punches.
Keep your lead hand high throughout the looping arc.
commonMistakes: Throwing without slipping the head, leaving your chin vulnerable.
Over-lunging forward onto your front leg.
safetyNotes: Maintain shoulder engagement to support the descending arc.
contraindications: Rotator cuff impingement.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Shadowboxing Rear Cross (2)
steps: Establish your boxing stance with your rear right fist at your cheekbone.
Pivot on the ball of your rear right foot and turn your right hip forward.
Extend your right arm straight down your centerline toward the target.
Turn your fist over so your palm faces down at full arm extension.
Keep your lead left hand firmly in guard protecting your left jawline.
Retract your right hand immediately back to your cheek along the punch line.
tips: Power in the 2 cross originates from the rear foot pivot and hip rotation.
Do not lean your head past your lead front knee as you punch.
commonMistakes: Leaving the lead hand low while throwing the rear punch.
Failing to pivot the rear foot, resulting in an arm-only punch without power.
safetyNotes: Ensure full wrist alignment on impact to protect metacarpal bones.
contraindications: Acute thumb ulnar collateral ligament tear or wrist sprain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Shadowboxing Rear Hand Parry
steps: Stand in orthodox guard with your rear right hand near your cheek.
As an opponent jab approaches, redirect it by tapping inward with your right palm.
Deflect the punch two inches off its target line across your shoulder.
Move your hand only a few inches from your face; do not reach forward.
Snap your parrying hand right back to your cheek immediately.
tips: A parry is a quick tap like swatting a fly, not a push.
Keep your lead hand high and ready to jab immediately.
commonMistakes: Reaching forward with the parrying hand, creating an opening for fakes.
Slapping wildly across your own face.
safetyNotes: Keep parries compact to avoid opening holes in guard.
contraindications: Wrist sprain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Shadowboxing Straight Rear Body Shot (2b)
steps: Start in a solid boxing stance with hands held high.
Drop your elevation by flexing deeply at both knee joints.
Pivot your rear foot and drive punch 2 straight into opponent midsection.
Keep your lead hand high protecting your jawline against lead hooks.
Drive off your front foot and return smoothly to your tall stance.
tips: Level change before firing the punch to align force with target.
Keep your neck tucked and chin hidden.
commonMistakes: Slumping forward at the waist without bending the knees.
Dropping the lead hand while attacking low.
safetyNotes: Keep lead hand glued to cheek to block counter hooks.
contraindications: Lower back disc pain aggravated by flexion.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Shadowboxing Shoulder Roll (Philly Shell)
steps: Assume a bladed stance with your lead left arm resting low across your belly.
Tuck your chin behind your elevated lead left shoulder.
Keep your rear right hand glued to your right cheekbone.
Rotate your left shoulder inward to deflect incoming straight punches upward.
Absorb the deflected impact through your lead shoulder and spring back.
tips: Keep your chin buried deep behind the shoulder cap.
Use the rotation of the shoulder to deflect, not absorb, force.
commonMistakes: Lifting the chin out from behind the protective shoulder.
Leaving the rear hand low and getting hit with lead hooks.
safetyNotes: Requires advanced timing and shoulder awareness.
contraindications: Rotator cuff impingement or cervical disc injury.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Shadowboxing Inside Slip
steps: Begin in your balanced orthodox boxing stance with guard up.
Bend your knees slightly and rotate your shoulders slightly to the left.
Move your head two to three inches to the inside off the centerline.
Let the opponent jab glide harmlessly over your right shoulder.
Keep your eyes locked on the opponent and return smoothly to center.
tips: Make the slip minimal: move your head just enough to evade the punch.
Keep both hands glued to your cheekbones while slipping.
commonMistakes: Bending at the waist and taking your eyes off the opponent.
Moving your head too far and throwing yourself off balance.
safetyNotes: Keep head movement compact without breaking pelvic balance.
contraindications: Cervical spine strain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Shadowboxing Outside Slip
steps: Start in orthodox stance with hands held high in tight guard.
Flex both knees and rotate your left shoulder slightly inward.
Slip your head two to three inches to the right outside the punch path.
Allow the opponent straight punch to travel past your left ear.
Load your rear right hip to prepare an immediate counter cross.
tips: A small slip of three inches is safer and faster than a large swing.
Keep your hands up protecting your temples.
commonMistakes: Squatting too low or bending at the hips.
Dropping your hands while moving your head.
safetyNotes: Move from the knees and obliques, not the lower back.
contraindications: Lower back muscle strain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Shadowboxing Southpaw Lead Jab (1)
steps: Assume a southpaw boxing stance with your right foot and right hand leading.
Step forward lightly with your lead right foot as you fire your right jab.
Turn your fist over so your palm faces downward at full arm extension.
Shrug your lead right shoulder up to guard your chin against left hands.
Snap your right fist back instantly along the punch line to your cheek.
tips: Keep your rear left hand anchored to your left jawline.
Use the lead jab to establish distance and measure your target.
commonMistakes: Dropping the lead hand before punching, telegraphing the jab.
Leaning forward past your lead front knee.
safetyNotes: Ensure proper hand wraps to cushion metacarpal impact.
contraindications: Acute carpal tunnel or wrist instability.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Shadowboxing Southpaw Rear Straight Left (2)
steps: Set up in southpaw stance with left hand and left foot in rear position.
Pivot dynamically on the ball of your rear left foot, rotating hips.
Drive punch 2 straight down the pipe from your left cheek to target.
Rotate your left wrist over to lock in knuckle alignment at impact.
Keep your lead right hand firmly protecting your right cheekbone.
Retract your left hand instantly to your defensive guard position.
tips: Drive through the ball of the rear foot to engage the entire kinetic chain.
Keep your chin tucked behind your left shoulder at full extension.
commonMistakes: Flaring the rear elbow out wide before extending the punch.
Over-rotating hips and ending up off-balance.
safetyNotes: Keep your wrist straight and braced on contact.
contraindications: Acute wrist injury or elbow hyperextension.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Shadowboxing Heavy Bag Freestyle Rounds
steps: Wrap your hands thoroughly and lace up sixteen-ounce boxing gloves.
Circle the heavy bag at boxing distance in a balanced stance.
Work combinations utilizing punches 1 through 6 while varying cadence and power.
Slip and roll your head after every offensive sequence as if avoiding counters.
Maintain rhythmic footwork and circle smoothly as the bag swings.
Work at high tempo for three minutes, then rest for sixty seconds between rounds.
tips: Hit through the surface of the bag with stiff wrists rather than pushing it.
Never stop moving your feet and head between punch combinations.
commonMistakes: Hitting the heavy bag with unconditioned bare hands or without hand wraps.
Smothering punches by standing too close to the swinging bag.
safetyNotes: Always wrap your hands and wear proper gloves to prevent carpal fractures.
contraindications: Unhealed hand fractures, boxer knuckle, or severe carpal tunnel syndrome.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Shadowboxing Heavy Bag High-Cadence Intervals
steps: Position yourself square to heavy bag with hands up in guard.
Throw continuous straight punches 1 and 2 at high frequency.
Maintain a fast running cadence on the balls of your feet.
Focus on shoulder endurance, hand speed, and continuous output.
Pump straight punches non-stop for sixty-second burnout bursts.
tips: Keep punches eye-level and turn fists over fully on each extension.
Keep your core braced and feet pedaling smoothly.
commonMistakes: Dropping hands to chest level as shoulders fatigue.
Slapping the bag with unaligned wrists.
safetyNotes: Never strike heavy bag without wraps and gloves.
contraindications: Wrist tendonitis.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Shadowboxing One-Two-Lead Hook Combo (1-2-3)
steps: Fire punch 1 (jab) straight out from your lead stance to find distance.
Snap the jab back and immediately pivot hips to drive punch 2 (rear cross).
Transfer your weight smoothly to your front foot and pivot on lead toes.
Whip punch 3 (lead hook) horizontally with elbow bent at ninety degrees.
Recoil your lead arm back instantly into full defensive guard stance.
Perform crisp continuous combination cycles for the duration of the round.
tips: Flow through the sequence 1-2-3 as a single continuous kinetic wave.
Turn your lead foot like squashing a bug on the 3 hook to generate rotational whip.
commonMistakes: Pausing between the 2 and 3 punches instead of chaining the hip weight transfer.
Looping the hook too wide and leaving the entire center open to counterpunches.
safetyNotes: Maintain controlled wrist stiffness on the 3 hook to prevent hyperextension.
contraindications: Rotator cuff tear or acute TFCC wrist tear.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Shadowboxing Orthodox Boxing Stance
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and take one natural stride forward with your left foot.
Angle both feet roughly forty-five degrees to the right of your centerline.
Distribute your bodyweight evenly with fifty-five percent over your back right foot.
Tuck your chin down toward your collarbone behind your raised lead left shoulder.
Bring your right fist to your right cheekbone and your left fist six inches ahead of your chin.
Hold this balanced guard position while keeping your knees softly bent and responsive.
tips: Keep your back right heel slightly off the floor like a loaded spring.
Never stand flat-footed or cross your feet while holding the stance.
commonMistakes: Squaring your hips to your opponent, exposing a broad target area.
Lifting your chin high and dropping your hands below chest height.
safetyNotes: Keep your jaw clamped shut and chin protected by your lead shoulder.
contraindications: Acute ankle instability or severe balance impairment.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Shadowboxing Focus Mitt Speed Combinations
steps: Face trainer holding focus mitts in your orthodox or southpaw stance.
React instantly to mitt cues, firing combinations using punches 1 through 6.
Snap punches crisply against the mitt centers with proper distance.
Duck or slip immediately when trainer flashes counter pad swipes.
Work combinations for three minutes with fifty percent rest intervals.
tips: Keep your eyes locked on trainer chest to read cues quickly.
Snap hands back to your guard faster than you threw them.
commonMistakes: Reaching forward to hit pads rather than letting them meet your range.
Standing flat-footed between combos.
safetyNotes: Communicate with partner on pacing and pad resistance.
contraindications: Partner collision or elbow hyperextension.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Standing Shoulder CARs
steps: Stand tall with a rigid braced core and fists clenched.
Raise your right straight arm forward and up past your ear.
At peak overhead height, rotate your bicep outward.
Continue the circle backward, rotating arm internally as it reaches behind.
Complete repetitions, then switch arms and repeat on left side.
tips: Do not let your torso twist or arch to assist the arm.
Move slowly through the entire circumference.
commonMistakes: Arching lower back when arm passes overhead.
Shrugging shoulder up into ear.
safetyNotes: Work strictly in pain-free joint range.
contraindications: Rotator cuff impingement.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Resistance Band Shoulder Pass-Through
steps: Stand tall holding a light resistance band with a wide overhand grip.
Lock your elbows straight and hold the band across your front thighs.
Raise your arms up overhead in a wide smooth arc without bending elbows.
Continue the arc behind your back until the band lightly touches your glutes.
Reverse the arc smoothly to bring the band back overhead to the front.
Repeat for ten continuous fluid repetitions.
tips: Widen your grip on the band if your elbows bend during the pass-through.
Keep your ribs pulled down and glutes squeezed to prevent lower back arching.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows as the band passes overhead.
Over-arching the spine to cheat through shoulder tightness.
safetyNotes: Use a wide enough grip so the band passes smoothly without sharp shoulder pain.
contraindications: Active anterior shoulder dislocation history or acute rotator cuff tear.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Agility Shuttle Runs
steps: Start in an athletic three-point stance behind the baseline.
Sprint at full speed five yards forward to touch the line.
Pivot sharply and sprint back to the baseline.
Immediately turn and sprint ten yards to the far marker.
Touch down with your hand and sprint hard through the finish.
tips: Lower your center of mass before planting to change direction.
Keep steps quick and responsive.
commonMistakes: Slipping on turn-around points due to high center of mass.
Standing upright before decelerating.
safetyNotes: Ensure surface is dry and free of debris.
contraindications: Groin adductor tear.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Single-Arm Archer Push-Up
steps: Assume a very wide hand placement on the floor.
Lower body toward your right hand while extending left arm completely straight.
Press up powerfully through right arm to return to center.
Complete prescribed repetitions, then switch sides and repeat on left arm.
tips: Keep the extended arm locked straight to isolate the working arm.
Keep core rigid throughout.
commonMistakes: Twisting hips unevenly off horizontal.
Letting straight arm collapse.
safetyNotes: Warm up shoulders and chest thoroughly.
contraindications: Shoulder anterior instability.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Single-Arm Chin-Up
steps: Grip pull-up bar with an underhand grip shoulder-width apart.
Hang with straight arms and engaged shoulders.
Pull elbows down and back, driving chin cleanly over the bar.
Complete the prescribed reps, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Squeeze biceps and lats tightly at top of rep.
Keep legs together and core tight.
commonMistakes: Swinging hips to generate momentum.
Dropping rapidly without controlling the descent.
safetyNotes: Control the descent to protect elbow joints.
contraindications: Medial epicondylitis (golfer elbow).

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Single-Arm Diamond Push-Up
steps: Place hands together directly under chest with thumbs and index fingers touching.
Form a straight plank line from heels to crown.
Lower chest down to touch the back of your hands.
Complete the prescribed reps, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep elbows tucked close to your ribcage.
Maintain an active core brace.
commonMistakes: Flaring elbows wide out to sides.
Sagging at the hips.
safetyNotes: Stop if inner elbow or wrist discomfort occurs.
contraindications: Triceps tendonitis or wrist impingement.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Single-Arm Dragon Flag
steps: Lie on a sturdy bench and grip the bench edges tightly behind your head.
Roll bodyweight onto your upper shoulders and lift your entire torso.
Form a rigid straight line from shoulders to pointed toes.
Complete the prescribed reps, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Pivot purely on your upper back and shoulders.
Do not allow hips to bend or sag.
commonMistakes: Bending at the waist and breaking body alignment.
Resting heavy compressive load on the neck.
safetyNotes: Never bear compressive weight on cervical spine.
contraindications: Acute lower back disc injury.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Single-Arm Full Front Lever Hold
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulders.
Retract and depress your scapulae with locked straight elbows.
Pull down against the bar through your lats to raise your torso and legs.
Lock your entire body into a completely horizontal plane parallel to the floor.
Complete the prescribed reps, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Generate intense straight-arm pulling torque through your latissimus dorsi.
Keep your body straight from shoulders to toes without sagging at the hips.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows to compensate for insufficient straight-arm lat strength.
Piking at the hips rather than maintaining a true horizontal line.
safetyNotes: Warm up your shoulders, elbows, and bicep tendons thoroughly prior to max holds.
contraindications: Distal biceps tendon strain or acute rotator cuff injury.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Single-Arm Wall-Assisted Handstand Push-Up
steps: Place your hands about eight inches away from a sturdy wall.
Kick up into a handstand with heels resting gently against the wall.
Establish an active hollow body position with your glutes and abs tight.
Lower your head forward slightly to touch your crown softly to the mat.
Form a stable tripod shape with your head positioned ahead of your hands.
Complete the prescribed reps, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Avoid flaring your elbows wide; keep them tucked at a forty-five degree angle.
Push the floor away aggressively at the top into an active shoulder shrug.
commonMistakes: Collapsing your neck onto the floor with unbuffered velocity.
Banana-arching your lower back and resting your entire spine against the wall.
safetyNotes: Always place an exercise mat beneath your head to protect the cervical spine.
contraindications: High blood pressure, glaucoma, retinal detachment, or cervical spine disc injury.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Single-Arm Hanging Leg Raise
steps: Hang from an overhead pull-up bar with an overhand shoulder-width grip.
Depress your scapulae to engage your lats and eliminate passive swinging.
Point your toes, squeeze your legs together, and brace your core.
Raise your straight legs upward until your shins are parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top to emphasize lower abdominal contraction.
Complete the prescribed reps, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Posteriorly tilt your pelvis at the top to ensure your abs flex fully.
Do not swing your legs backward past the vertical plane between reps.
commonMistakes: Using pendulum momentum and arching your lower back to fling the legs up.
Bending knees excessively when performing the straight-leg variant.
safetyNotes: Control the lowering phase to avoid sudden lumbar hyperextension.
contraindications: Acute abdominal muscle strain or severe hip flexor tendinitis.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Single-Arm Hollow Body Hold
steps: Lie on your back on an exercise mat with arms and legs fully extended.
Press your lower back firmly into the floor so there is zero gap under your spine.
Lift your shoulder blades and legs two to four inches off the ground.
Reach your arms overhead past your ears while pointing your toes forward.
Complete the prescribed reps, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Your lower back must stay glued to the floor for the entire set.
Breathe shallowly through your diaphragm without releasing abdominal brace.
commonMistakes: Letting your lower back arch and lift off the floor under fatigue.
Craning your neck excessively forward rather than tucking your chin slightly.
safetyNotes: If your lower back begins peeling off the floor, regress by tucking your knees.
contraindications: Acute lumbar disc herniation aggravated by posterior pelvic tilt.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Single-Arm Inverted Row
steps: Lie under a waist-height bar and grasp with an overhand grip.
Extend legs forward with heels grounded and body in a straight plank.
Pull chest up to touch the bar by driving elbows back.
Complete the prescribed reps, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep body completely straight like an iron plank.
Retract shoulder blades fully at peak.
commonMistakes: Sagging hips toward the floor.
Poking chin forward to touch the bar.
safetyNotes: Adjust bar height to scale difficulty.
contraindications: Rotator cuff strain.

safetyNotes: If your lower back begins peeling off the floor, regress by tucking your knees.
contraindications: Acute lumbar disc herniation aggravated by posterior pelvic tilt.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Straddle Inverted Row
steps: Lie under a waist-height bar and grasp with an overhand grip.
Extend legs forward with heels grounded and body in a straight plank.
Pull chest up to touch the bar by driving elbows back.
Lower body smoothly back to full arm extension.
tips: Keep body completely straight like an iron plank.
Retract shoulder blades fully at peak.
commonMistakes: Sagging hips toward the floor.
Poking chin forward to touch the bar.
safetyNotes: Adjust bar height to scale difficulty.
contraindications: Rotator cuff strain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Straddle L-Sit Hold
steps: Mount parallel bars with straight locked arms and depressed shoulders.
Lift straight legs in front of you until parallel to the floor.
Point toes forward and squeeze quadriceps tightly.
Hold the strict L-shape for the target hold duration.
tips: Push the floor or bars away actively through palms.
Keep knees fully locked out straight.
commonMistakes: Bending knees due to weak hip flexors.
Shrugging shoulders into ears.
safetyNotes: Warm up wrists and shoulders thoroughly.
contraindications: Severe hip flexor tendinitis.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Straddle Nordic Hamstring Curl
steps: Kneel on a padded mat with your ankles secured firmly under a support.
Align knees, hips, and shoulders in one rigid vertical line.
Lower torso forward toward the floor as slowly as possible using hamstrings.
Catch yourself on hands, push lightly, and pull back up with hamstrings.
tips: Resist gravity for as long as possible on the way down.
Keep hips extended without breaking at the waist.
commonMistakes: Bending at the hips to avoid hamstring loading.
Falling forward without muscular control.
safetyNotes: Cushion knees with thick padding.
contraindications: Acute hamstring strain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Straddle Parallel Bar Dip
steps: Mount the parallel bars and lock out your arms with shoulders depressed.
Lean your torso forward roughly fifteen degrees to engage your chest.
Bend your elbows to lower your body downward smoothly.
Descend until your shoulders are level with or slightly below your elbows.
Press through your palms to extend your arms back to the top support position.
tips: Keep your elbows tucked at roughly forty-five degrees rather than flared.
Maintain an active hollow body position with crossed or straight ankles.
commonMistakes: Dipping too shallow and cutting the range of motion in half.
Allowing your shoulders to shrug upward toward your ears under load.
safetyNotes: Avoid excessive downward depth if you experience anterior shoulder pain.
contraindications: Acute sternoclavicular joint injury or anterior glenohumeral instability.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Straddle Pistol Squat
steps: Stand balanced on your right leg and extend your left leg straight in front of you.
Reach your arms forward to counterbalance your center of mass.
Hinge your hips slightly and bend your right knee to descend smoothly.
Lower down fully until your right hamstring rests against your calf.
Keep your left heel elevated completely off the ground throughout.
Drive firmly through your right foot to stand back up to tall extension.
Switch and perform the same number of reps on your opposite left leg.
tips: Maintain deep ankle dorsiflexion and keep your heel planted firmly.
Round your upper back slightly to maintain forward counterbalance.
commonMistakes: Allowing your standing heel to lift off the floor during the descent.
Letting the elevated non-working leg touch the ground.
safetyNotes: Requires substantial ankle and knee integrity; progress using box support first.
contraindications: Severe patellofemoral osteoarthritis or recovering meniscus repair.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Straddle Standard Pull-Up
steps: Grip the overhead pull-up bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than your shoulders.
Hang at full arm extension in an active dead hang with engaged shoulder blades.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes into a hollow body shape.
Pull your elbows down toward your hips while driving your chest toward the bar.
Continue pulling smoothly until your chin clears the top edge of the bar.
Lower yourself under steady control back to the complete active hang.
tips: Initiate the pull by depressing your scapulae before bending your arms.
Keep your legs glued together to avoid leaking core tension.
commonMistakes: Kicking your legs or kipping with momentum to reach the top.
Shortening repetitions by failing to reach full arm lockout at the bottom.
safetyNotes: Do not relax into an inactive joint hang with limp shoulders at the bottom.
contraindications: Acute shoulder labrum tear or severe golfer elbow flare-up.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Straddle Push-Up
steps: Set hands slightly wider than shoulders on the floor.
Keep feet together and form a rigid straight plank line.
Lower body smoothly until chest hovers just off the floor.
Press the ground away forcefully to complete arm lockout.
tips: Keep elbows angled at forty-five degrees like an arrow.
Squeeze glutes to protect lower spine.
commonMistakes: Sagging hips toward the mat during descent.
Flaring elbows wide at ninety degrees.
safetyNotes: Keep wrists stacked comfortably.
contraindications: Acute wrist sprain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Straddle Standard Push-Up
steps: Place your hands on the ground slightly wider than your shoulders.
Extend your legs behind you with feet together and form a straight body line.
Squeeze your glutes and draw your belly button toward your spine.
Lower your entire body until your chest hovers an inch above the floor.
Push the ground away forcefully until your arms lock out smoothly at the top.
tips: Position your elbows in an arrow shape relative to your torso.
Keep your neck neutral by gazing at a spot slightly ahead of your hands.
commonMistakes: Sagging your hips toward the floor and hyperextending your lumbar spine.
Poking your chin down to make it feel like you reached full depth.
safetyNotes: Keep your wrists stacked comfortably or use push-up handles if wrists ache.
contraindications: Acute wrist sprain or unhealed scaphoid fracture.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Easy Pose
steps: Sit on mat and cross legs at shins, sliding feet beneath opposite knees.
Rest hands on knees with palms facing down or up in mudra.
Lengthen spine tall and align ears over shoulders and shoulders over hips.
Soften facial muscles, drop shoulders away from ears, and close eyes.
Breathe naturally through nose, focusing on breath awareness.
Hold for sixty seconds, then switch cross of legs.
tips: Sit on folded blanket to elevate hips if knees rise higher than pelvis.
Keep spine erect without leaning forward or backward.
commonMistakes: Slouching into lower back and hunching shoulders.
Tensing knees upward.
safetyNotes: Use elevation beneath pelvis for comfortable hip opening.
contraindications: Severe knee arthritis or recent hip surgery.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Supine Cat-Cow Dynamic Stretch
steps: Set up on hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
Inhale into cow pose by dropping your belly and lifting your chest and tailbone.
Exhale into cat pose by tucking your tailbone and rounding your spine up.
Press firmly through your palms to spread your shoulder blades apart.
Flow continuously between extension and flexion in rhythm with your breath.
tips: Articulate the movement vertebra by vertebra starting from your pelvis.
Keep your elbows unlocked throughout the transition.
commonMistakes: Cramming into cervical hyperextension by jerking the chin up too far.
Moving with rapid uncontrolled pace rather than smooth segmental articulation.
safetyNotes: Stay within a comfortable pain-free range of motion without forcing end ranges.
contraindications: Severe acute disc prolapse aggravated by flexion.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Supine Doorway Pectoral Stretch
steps: Stand in an open doorway and place forearms flat against doorframe.
Position elbows at ninety degrees at shoulder height.
Step forward with one foot until you feel a gentle chest stretch.
Keep your neck relaxed and chest broad.
Hold the stretch for thirty seconds with steady breathing.
tips: Step gently forward to regulate stretch intensity.
Keep ribs pulled down.
commonMistakes: Pressing forward with aggressive sudden force.
Shrugging shoulders into ears.
safetyNotes: Do not over-stretch anterior shoulder capsule.
contraindications: Anterior shoulder instability.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Supine Latissimus Dorsi Foam Rolling
steps: Lie on your right side with a foam roller beneath your armpit.
Extend your right arm straight along the floor overhead.
Roll slowly along the outer ribcage and latissimus dorsi.
Pause on tight spots and take slow deep breaths.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Roll only along muscular tissue, avoiding lower ribs.
Regulate pressure using your feet.
commonMistakes: Rolling directly onto floating lower ribs.
Tensing up and holding breath.
safetyNotes: Keep roller on muscular lat belly.
contraindications: Osteoporosis or rib fracture.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Supine Quadriceps Foam Rolling
steps: Lie prone on your mat with a foam roller under your thighs.
Support your upper body on your forearms in a low plank.
Roll slowly from the top of your hips down to just above knees.
Pause and breathe on tender trigger points for twenty seconds.
Continue rolling along the muscle belly for sixty seconds.
tips: Keep your core gently braced to prevent lower back sagging.
Relax quadricep tissue.
commonMistakes: Rolling directly over the kneecap bone.
Holding your breath while rolling tender areas.
safetyNotes: Never roll directly onto bone or joint capsules.
contraindications: Acute thigh hematoma.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Supine Standing Hamstring Stretch
steps: Stand tall and place your right heel on a low bench or step.
Flex your right foot with toes pointing upward.
Hinge forward from your hips with a flat back.
Feel a gentle stretch through the back of your right thigh.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Hinge from the hips rather than rounding the lower back.
Keep your standing leg stable.
commonMistakes: Rounding the spine to force head toward knee.
Locking knee into painful hyperextension.
safetyNotes: Avoid aggressive stretching into sharp pain.
contraindications: Acute hamstring tear.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Supine Quadruped Hip CARs
steps: Assume a quadruped tabletop position on your hands and knees.
Brace your core and lift your right knee toward your chest.
Open your right knee out to the side in abduction.
Rotate hip internally and drive heel toward ceiling.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Isolate the hip capsule without moving lower back.
Imagine tracing the biggest circle possible.
commonMistakes: Arching or twisting your spine to compensate.
Rushing through sticky ranges.
safetyNotes: Move slowly with total joint control.
contraindications: Hip labral tear or severe impingement.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Supine Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
steps: Kneel on your left knee and step your right foot forward in a half-kneeling stance.
Maintain ninety-degree angles at both front and back knee joints.
Posteriorly tilt your pelvis by tucking your tailbone and squeezing your left glute.
Shift your hips forward slightly until you feel a deep stretch in front of your left hip.
Keep your torso completely vertical and hold the position for thirty seconds.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: The posterior pelvic tilt is what isolates the psoas; do not arch your lower back.
Raise your left arm overhead to intensify the stretch through the entire fascial line.
commonMistakes: Hyperextending the lumbar spine and dumping all forward travel into the lower back.
Failing to contract the trailing glute during the hold.
safetyNotes: Place a folded mat or cushion under the rear knee for comfort.
contraindications: Acute patellar bursitis on the kneeling knee or acute hip labral pathology.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Supine 90-90 Hip Switch
steps: Sit on the floor with your front right leg bent at ninety degrees.
Position your trailing left leg bent at ninety degrees to your side.
Sit tall with your spine erect, using your hands behind you for support if needed.
Lift your knees and pivot on your heels to sweep your legs across to the left.
Finish in the mirror ninety-ninety position with your left leg leading in front.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your heels anchored into the ground as you transition between sides.
Strive to perform the rotation without placing your hands on the ground as you progress.
commonMistakes: Slouching through the lower back to compensate for limited hip capsule rotation.
Letting knees collapse with uncontrolled momentum.
safetyNotes: Do not force end-range internal rotation if you feel pinching inside the hip joint.
contraindications: Hip labral tear with femoral acetabular impingement (FAI).

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Supine Quadruped Thoracic Rotation
steps: Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Place your right hand behind your head with elbow wide.
Rotate your right elbow down toward your left forearm on inhale.
Exhale and rotate your chest up toward ceiling, pointing elbow high.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Rotate from your upper thoracic back, keeping hips square.
Move smoothly with breath.
commonMistakes: Shifting hips sideways to cheat through rotation.
Pulling on the neck with the hand.
safetyNotes: Keep movement comfortable within joint range.
contraindications: Thoracic facet joint irritation.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Supine Standing Shoulder CARs
steps: Stand tall with a rigid braced core and fists clenched.
Raise your right straight arm forward and up past your ear.
At peak overhead height, rotate your bicep outward.
Continue the circle backward, rotating arm internally as it reaches behind.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Do not let your torso twist or arch to assist the arm.
Move slowly through the entire circumference.
commonMistakes: Arching lower back when arm passes overhead.
Shrugging shoulder up into ear.
safetyNotes: Work strictly in pain-free joint range.
contraindications: Rotator cuff impingement.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Supine Resistance Band Shoulder Pass-Through
steps: Stand tall holding a light resistance band with a wide overhand grip.
Lock your elbows straight and hold the band across your front thighs.
Raise your arms up overhead in a wide smooth arc without bending elbows.
Continue the arc behind your back until the band lightly touches your glutes.
Reverse the arc smoothly to bring the band back overhead to the front.
Repeat for ten continuous fluid repetitions.
tips: Widen your grip on the band if your elbows bend during the pass-through.
Keep your ribs pulled down and glutes squeezed to prevent lower back arching.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows as the band passes overhead.
Over-arching the spine to cheat through shoulder tightness.
safetyNotes: Use a wide enough grip so the band passes smoothly without sharp shoulder pain.
contraindications: Active anterior shoulder dislocation history or acute rotator cuff tear.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Supine Standing Quadriceps Stretch
steps: Stand tall on your left foot using a wall for balance if needed.
Bend your right knee and grasp your right ankle with right hand.
Gently pull your heel toward your glute while keeping knees aligned.
Tuck your pelvis under to increase the stretch along front thigh.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your knees together rather than letting working knee flare out.
Maintain tall posture.
commonMistakes: Arching lower back excessively.
Pulling ankle out to the side.
safetyNotes: Keep knees close together to protect ligaments.
contraindications: Patellofemoral pain syndrome.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Supine Thoracic Spine Foam Rolling
steps: Sit on your mat and position a foam roller horizontally across your mid-back.
Interlace your fingers behind your head to support the weight of your neck.
Lift your hips slightly and roll slowly between your mid-back and upper shoulders.
Pause at tight segments, lower your hips, and gently arch back over the roller.
Exhale smoothly as you extend your upper back over the roller.
Continue working your upper thoracic spine for the allotted sixty seconds.
tips: Keep your elbows pointed forward to pull shoulder blades apart and expose tissue.
Never roll down onto your unsupported lumbar spine.
commonMistakes: Rolling onto the lower back or neck vertebrae directly.
Pulling violently on your head and hyper-flexing your cervical spine.
safetyNotes: Keep the roller strictly on the rib-supported thoracic region between shoulder blades.
contraindications: Osteoporosis, vertebral compression fractures, or unhealed rib injury.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Supine World's Greatest Stretch
steps: Step forward into a deep lunge with your right foot outside your right hand.
Place your left hand on the floor and lower your right elbow inside your right ankle.
Rotate your torso to the right and reach your right arm toward the ceiling.
Gaze up toward your right hand while keeping your left hip flexor extended.
Bring your right hand back down, rock back, and straighten your right front leg.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your back knee extended and back glute fired to maximize hip flexor opening.
Rotate from your upper back rather than twisting through your lumbar spine.
commonMistakes: Collapsing your back knee onto the floor during the rotational phase.
Craning your neck to compensate for limited thoracic spine rotation.
safetyNotes: Move smoothly between positions without snapping into end ranges.
contraindications: Acute groin adductor strain or lumbar facet joint irritation.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Supported Headstand
steps: Kneel on your mat and interlace your fingers to create a sturdy triangular base.
Place your forearms on the floor with elbows kept shoulder-width apart.
Nestle the crown of your head softly into the cradle of your clasped hands.
Straighten your legs, lift your hips, and walk your feet in toward your face.
Engage your shoulders and core to float both legs up vertically into the inversion.
Press strongly down through your forearms to alleviate compression on your cervical spine.
Hold with steady breath, then lower down smoothly into child pose.
tips: Eighty percent of bodyweight should be held by your forearms, not your head.
Keep your shoulder blades pulled actively away from your ears.
commonMistakes: Allowing your elbows to splay wide, collapsing forearm support.
Kicking up with wild uncontrolled momentum and arching the spine.
safetyNotes: Never compress your cervical vertebrae; bail immediately if you experience neck pain.
contraindications: Cervical spine injury, glaucoma, detached retina, severe high blood pressure, or migraine.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Reclining Fire Log Pose (Double Pigeon)
steps: Sit on your mat and bend your left knee, placing shin parallel to front of mat.
Stack your right shin directly on top of your left shin with right ankle over left knee.
Flex both feet intensely to protect your knee joints.
Sit tall with an erect spine and place fingertips on the floor beside hips.
Hinge forward gently from hips if extra stretch is desired in outer glutes.
Hold for forty-five seconds, then unwind legs and repeat with left shin on top.
tips: Flex both feet firmly to keep knee ligaments stable.
Place a yoga block under the top knee if it hovers high off the bottom foot.
commonMistakes: Sickling the ankles and twisting knee joints.
Rounding lower back to force torso down.
safetyNotes: Do not force top knee down; support with a block.
contraindications: Acute meniscus tear or knee osteoarthritis.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Reclining Happy Baby Pose
steps: Lie on your back on your mat and draw both knees toward your armpits.
Flex your feet and grip the outside edges of your feet with your hands.
Open your knees slightly wider than your torso and stack ankles over knees.
Gently pull downward with hands to draw knees toward the floor.
Keep your tailbone and entire spine grounded flat against the mat.
Hold the restorative hip opener for forty-five seconds with slow breaths.
tips: Keep the back of your neck long by tucking your chin slightly.
Gently rock side to side if comfortable for lower back massage.
commonMistakes: Peeling the tailbone and lower back high off the mat.
Tensing shoulders and neck up toward ears.
safetyNotes: Hold shins or back of thighs if feet are out of reach.
contraindications: Late-term pregnancy or acute neck injury.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Reclining Half Moon Pose
steps: Begin in Triangle pose with your right leg forward.
Bend your right knee slightly and place right fingertips on the floor six inches ahead of toes.
Shift your weight into your right foot and float your left leg up parallel to the floor.
Straighten your standing right leg without locking the knee joint.
Stack your left hip and shoulder directly over your right side.
Extend your left arm toward the ceiling and gaze up if balance allows.
Hold for thirty seconds, then lower down and repeat on your left side.
tips: Flex your lifted foot intensely and push out through the heel.
Place a yoga block beneath your lower hand to keep torso elongated.
commonMistakes: Letting the lifted leg drop below hip level.
Collapsing the chest toward the mat.
safetyNotes: Use wall support behind your back to build hip stacking confidence.
contraindications: Severe vertigo or inner ear infection.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Reclining Half Lord of the Fishes Pose
aliases: Reclining Half Lord of the Fishes Pose
steps: Sit with legs extended, bend right knee, and place right foot outside left thigh.
Bend left knee and fold left foot close to right outer hip.
Place right hand on floor behind your sacrum like a kickstand.
Inhale, raise left arm tall, then exhale and hook left elbow outside right knee.
Rotate torso to the right with each exhale, gazing over right shoulder.
Hold for forty-five seconds, untwist, and repeat on opposite side.
tips: Lengthen spine tall on every inhale before deepening twist on exhale.
Keep both sitting bones grounded flat on mat.
commonMistakes: Slouching back onto the rear hand and rounding spine.
Craning the neck aggressively instead of twisting from thoracic spine.
safetyNotes: Twist from the upper back, not the lower back.
contraindications: Acute spinal disc prolapse or severe sacroiliac irritation.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Reclining Eight-Angle Pose
steps: Sit on mat, bend right knee, and hook right leg high over right shoulder.
Place palms flat on floor beside hips with fingers spread wide.
Cross left ankle over right ankle and squeeze thighs against right arm.
Press through hands to lift hips and legs off the mat.
Bend elbows to ninety degrees, extend legs out to right, and lower chest parallel to floor.
Hold for thirty seconds, release, and repeat on opposite side.
tips: Squeeze thighs firmly together like a vise around your arm.
Keep shoulders level and gaze forward.
commonMistakes: Failing to clamp legs, causing them to slide down arm.
Collapsing chest onto the floor.
safetyNotes: Warm up wrists and hips thoroughly before practicing.
contraindications: Acute wrist injury or shoulder impingement.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Reclining Bound Angle Pose (Cobbler)
steps: Sit upright on your mat and bend both knees.
Bring the soles of your feet together and draw heels toward your pelvis.
Clasp your hands around your feet or ankles and sit tall with shoulders back.
Let your knees drop naturally outward toward the floor without forcing them.
Inhale to lengthen your spine, then hinge forward gently from your hips.
Hold the posture for sixty seconds with calm, steady breathing.
tips: Open the soles of your feet toward the ceiling like pages of a book.
Never push down forcefully on your knees with your hands.
commonMistakes: Pushing knees down aggressively with arm force.
Hunching shoulders forward into ears.
safetyNotes: Support knees with blocks if groin feels strained.
contraindications: Acute knee ligament tears or severe groin pull.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Reclining Crow Pose
steps: Squat down on your mat with feet together and hands shoulder-width on floor.
Spread fingers wide and press firmly through knuckle pads.
Lift hips, bend elbows slightly, and rest knees on backs of upper triceps.
Shift bodyweight forward until feet become light.
Lift one foot, then the other, balancing entirely on your hands.
Hold for thirty seconds while drawing navel toward spine, then lower feet.
tips: Look slightly forward rather than down to keep momentum balanced.
Round your upper back and push floor away.
commonMistakes: Looking down at your feet, causing you to tip forward.
Letting elbows flare wide out to the sides.
safetyNotes: Place a cushion in front of your head while learning balance.
contraindications: Carpal tunnel syndrome or acute wrist sprains.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Reclining Child's Pose
steps: Kneel on mat with big toes touching and knees wide apart.
Lower hips to rest back on heels and fold torso forward over thighs.
Extend arms forward along mat or rest them alongside body, palms up.
Rest forehead softly on yoga mat.
Release all muscular tension and breathe into back ribcage.
Hold for sixty seconds in calm surrender.
tips: Rest forehead on a block if head does not reach floor.
Place a rolled blanket behind knees if hips do not meet heels.
commonMistakes: Holding tension in shoulders or neck.
Holding breath during resting posture.
safetyNotes: Restorative pose; adjust knee width for comfort.
contraindications: Recent knee surgery or acute diarrhea.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Reclining Wild Thing
steps: From Downward-Facing Dog, lift your right leg high into Three-Legged Dog.
Bend your right knee and flip your dog by stepping right foot to floor behind you.
Ground through your left hand and left outer foot.
Inhale, lift your hips high, and extend your right arm overhead toward front of mat.
Curl your upper back into an expressive, joyful backbend.
Hold for thirty seconds, flip back to downward dog, and repeat on opposite side.
tips: Press down through your supporting left hand and engage the left lat.
Keep hips elevated through glute contraction.
commonMistakes: Collapsing into the supporting shoulder joint.
Letting hips sag toward the ground.
safetyNotes: Maintain active shoulder blade engagement on base arm.
contraindications: Rotator cuff tears or carpal tunnel syndrome.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Reclining Cobra Pose
steps: Lie prone on your stomach with the tops of your feet flat on the mat.
Place your hands beneath your shoulders with fingers pointing forward.
Hug your elbows lightly against your ribcage.
Press your pubic bone into the mat and inhale as you peel your chest upward.
Engage your back extensors to lift your sternum without pressing heavily through hands.
Hold the gentle backbend while breathing evenly through your nose.
tips: Keep the back of your neck long by directing your gaze forward and slightly down.
Press the tops of your feet into the mat to stabilize your pelvis.
commonMistakes: Pushing with full arm force into a crunching compression of the lumbar spine.
Shrugging your shoulders tightly up around your ears.
safetyNotes: Distribute spinal extension evenly across the thoracic spine rather than hinging only in lower back.
contraindications: Pregnancy, carpal tunnel syndrome, or acute spinal disc herniation.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Reclining Corpse Pose
steps: Lie completely flat on your back along the center of your yoga mat.
Allow your feet to fall open naturally wider than hip-width apart.
Rest your arms comfortably alongside your body with palms turned upward.
Close your eyes softly and release all intentional muscular control.
Allow your breathing to settle into a natural, quiet rhythm.
Remain completely still and present for the entire allotted relaxation period.
tips: Place a rolled blanket under your knees if your lower back feels strained.
Scan your body from crown to toes to systematically soften residual tension.
commonMistakes: Holding physical tension in the jaw, brow, or shoulders.
Leaving the session abruptly without gentle preliminary movements.
safetyNotes: Keep warm with a blanket if your body temperature drops during stillness.
contraindications: Third-trimester pregnancy (modify by lying on the left side with bolster).

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Reclining Bow Pose
steps: Lie flat on your stomach and bend both knees, bringing heels toward buttocks.
Reach back with both hands and clasp your outer ankles.
Keep knees hip-width apart throughout the movement.
Inhale and kick your shins and feet strongly backward away from your body.
Allow the kick of your legs to lift your chest and thighs off the floor.
Balance on your abdomen and hold for thirty seconds with rhythmic breath.
tips: The lift comes from kicking your legs backward into your hands.
Do not let knees splay out wider than your hips.
commonMistakes: Letting knees splay very wide, jamming sacroiliac joints.
Holding breath while balancing on the belly.
safetyNotes: Kick legs back smoothly without sudden jerking.
contraindications: High blood pressure, hernia, or pregnancy.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Reclining Downward-Facing Dog
steps: Begin on your hands and knees in a tabletop position on your mat.
Spread your fingers wide and press firmly through all ten knuckles.
Tuck your toes under and lift your knees away from the floor.
Send your sitting bones up and back toward the ceiling to lengthen your spine.
Ground your heels gently toward the mat while keeping your ears between your upper arms.
Hold the posture steady while taking slow, measured nasal breaths.
tips: Bend your knees slightly if tight hamstrings cause your lower back to round.
Externally rotate your upper arms to broaden your upper back.
commonMistakes: Dumping bodyweight into the wrists instead of pressing through finger knuckles.
Rounding the spine and pushing the chest forward rather than back.
safetyNotes: Distribute weight evenly across the entire surface of both hands to avoid wrist strain.
contraindications: Severe carpal tunnel syndrome, late-term pregnancy, or uncontrolled hypertension.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Reclining Eagle Pose
steps: Stand in mountain pose, bend both knees slightly, and shift weight to your right foot.
Cross your left thigh over your right thigh and hook left toes behind right calf if able.
Cross your right elbow over your left elbow, bending arms and pressing palms together.
Lift your elbows to shoulder height while pulling your hands away from your face.
Sink your hips deeper into the squat while keeping your spine erect.
Hold for thirty seconds, then unwind arms and legs and repeat on the opposite side.
tips: Squeeze your inner thighs tightly together to maintain balance on your standing leg.
Draw your navel in and lengthen your tailbone toward the ground.
commonMistakes: Hunching forward and collapsing your chest over your thighs.
Letting your knees splay unevenly.
safetyNotes: Unwrap toes from calf if knee twist or ankle torque occurs.
contraindications: Acute knee ligament tears or shoulder impingement.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Reclining Cow Face Pose
steps: Sit with knees bent, sliding left foot under right hip and right knee over left knee.
Stack your knees directly on top of each other in the centerline.
Reach your right arm overhead, bend elbow, and place palm between shoulder blades.
Reach your left arm behind your back, bend elbow, and reach fingers up toward right hand.
Clasp fingers together or hold a yoga strap between both hands.
Hold with tall spine for forty-five seconds, then switch legs and arms and repeat.
tips: Keep both sit bones grounded evenly on the floor.
Use a strap between hands if shoulders are tight.
commonMistakes: Arching lower back into hyper-lordosis to connect hands.
Sitting unevenly on one hip.
safetyNotes: Use a strap to prevent shoulder joint strain.
contraindications: Rotator cuff impingement or acute knee meniscus tear.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Reclining Plow Pose
steps: Lie on back, engage core, and lift legs up and overhead.
Lower toes to the floor behind your head with legs straight.
Support lower back with hands or interlace fingers on mat.
Press through toes to lift sit bones toward ceiling.
Keep neck stationary and breathe into back of ribcage.
Hold for forty-five seconds, then roll down vertebra by vertebra.
tips: Rest toes on a chair or block behind head if feet do not reach floor.
Keep neck long and gaze upward toward belly.
commonMistakes: Turning head while neck is loaded under flexion.
Forcing feet down while rounding and compressing spine.
safetyNotes: Do not turn head while in plow pose.
contraindications: Cervical disc herniation or severe hypertension.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Reclining Head-to-Knee Forward Bend
steps: Sit with your right leg extended straight and left knee bent.
Place the sole of your left foot against your right inner thigh.
Turn your torso slightly to align your sternum over your right extended leg.
Inhale to lengthen your spine, then exhale and fold forward over right thigh.
Hold your right shin, ankle, or foot with both hands.
Hold for forty-five seconds, then sit up, switch legs, and repeat on left side.
tips: Keep your extended foot flexed and kneecap pointing straight up.
Rotate your torso from the navel to square over the extended leg.
commonMistakes: Rounding the upper back aggressively and yanking with the neck.
Letting the extended leg roll outward.
safetyNotes: Use a strap to maintain spinal length.
contraindications: Acute groin strain or lumbar disc herniation.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Reclining Garland Pose (Yogi Squat)
steps: Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width with toes angled forty-five degrees outward.
Bend your knees deeply and lower your hips down into a deep squat.
Bring your palms together at your heart center in prayer position.
Press your elbows outward against your inner knees to gently open your hips.
Lengthen your spine upward from your tailbone through the crown of your head.
Hold the deep squat while breathing into your pelvic floor.
tips: Place a rolled blanket or block under your heels if they lift off the mat.
Broaden across your chest and keep your spine tall.
commonMistakes: Rounding the spine into a hunched turtle posture.
Letting knees collapse inward over arches.
safetyNotes: Use block beneath hips if deep knee flexion causes discomfort.
contraindications: Severe meniscus tears or advanced knee osteoarthritis.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Reclining Frog Pose
steps: Begin on all fours on a padded mat or blanket.
Widen your knees as far apart as comfortably possible while keeping them in line with hips.
Bend your ankles at ninety degrees with inside edges of feet resting on the floor.
Lower down onto your forearms and keep your spine flat and neutral.
Gently shift your hips back toward your heels to deepen the inner groin stretch.
Hold the posture for forty-five seconds while breathing steadily into your pelvis.
tips: Double-pad your knees with folded blankets for joint comfort.
Keep your belly gently braced to support your lower back.
commonMistakes: Arching lower back into severe swayback collapse.
Pushing hips back aggressively into sharp groin pain.
safetyNotes: Stop immediately if sharp pinching occurs in hip capsule.
contraindications: Groin adductor tear or severe hip impingement.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Reclining Sage Marichi Pose C
steps: Sit with both legs straight; bend right knee and place foot flat near sit bone.
Leave one hand-width space between right foot and left inner thigh.
Place right fingertips on floor behind your spine.
Inhale, extend left arm high, then exhale and hook left elbow outside right thigh.
Press arm against thigh to deepen thoracic twist to the right.
Hold for forty-five seconds, then release and repeat on opposite side.
tips: Keep left extended leg active and foot flexed throughout.
Sit tall and avoid slouching back.
commonMistakes: Collapsing into the rear hand with a curved spine.
Letting extended leg go limp and roll outward.
safetyNotes: Maintain upright spine throughout rotation.
contraindications: Acute spinal disc injuries or pregnancy.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Reclining Fish Pose
steps: Lie on your back with legs extended together.
Slide your hands under your buttocks, palms down, with elbows tucked close to sides.
Press firmly down through your forearms and elbows to arch your chest upward.
Lift your sternum high and gently release the crown of your head to the mat.
Keep ninety percent of your bodyweight on your forearms, not your head.
Hold for thirty seconds while breathing deeply into your chest.
tips: Keep weight anchored on your forearms to avoid compressing cervical spine.
Expand your ribcage fully with every deep inhale.
commonMistakes: Resting full head weight onto the neck vertebrae.
Spreading elbows wide and collapsing forearm base.
safetyNotes: Do not bear heavy weight on crown of head.
contraindications: Severe cervical spine injury or migraine.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Supine Spinal Twist
steps: Lie flat on back and hug right knee into chest.
Extend right arm out to right side in a T-shape, palm facing up.
Guide right knee across body toward floor on left with left hand.
Turn head gently to gaze over right shoulder toward right hand.
Keep right shoulder blade pinned flat against mat.
Hold for forty-five seconds, bring knee to center, and repeat on left side.
tips: Keep both shoulder blades grounded flat against mat.
Place a block under the descending knee if it hovers in air.
commonMistakes: Lifting the right shoulder blade off mat to force knee to floor.
Holding tension in belly.
safetyNotes: Keep shoulders relaxed on the mat.
contraindications: Acute sacroiliac joint flare-up or disc herniation.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Reclining Peacock Pose
steps: Kneel on mat, place palms flat with fingers pointing backward toward knees.
Press elbows together and bury them into your upper abdomen near navel.
Extend legs back one at a time into a plank shape.
Shift bodyweight forward and elevate legs horizontally off the mat.
Balance entirely on your hands with body horizontal like a peacock.
Hold for twenty seconds, then lower feet softly to the mat.
