Hinge your hips back and place both hands flat on the floor.
Kick your feet back simultaneously into a high plank position.
Lower your chest and thighs completely onto the floor in one smooth wave.
Push the floor away and jump your feet forward just outside your hands.
Jump explosively into the air, clapping your hands overhead with body extended.
tips: Land with soft knees and transition immediately into your next descent.
Breathe rhythmically on every single repetition.
commonMistakes: Landing on stiff locked knees during the overhead jump landing.
Letting your lower back sag into a painful hyper-extended arch.
safetyNotes: Absorb landing impact through soft knees and ankles to protect joint cartilage.
contraindications: Severe patellofemoral osteoarthritis or severe vertigo.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tempo Standard Push-Up
steps: Place your hands on the ground slightly wider than your shoulders.
Extend your legs behind you with feet together and form a straight body line.
Squeeze your glutes and draw your belly button toward your spine.
Lower your entire body until your chest hovers an inch above the floor.
Push the ground away forcefully until your arms lock out smoothly at the top.
tips: Position your elbows in an arrow shape relative to your torso.
Keep your neck neutral by gazing at a spot slightly ahead of your hands.
commonMistakes: Sagging your hips toward the floor and hyperextending your lumbar spine.
Poking your chin down to make it feel like you reached full depth.
safetyNotes: Keep your wrists stacked comfortably or use push-up handles if wrists ache.
contraindications: Acute wrist sprain or unhealed scaphoid fracture.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: High-Tempo Plyometric Tuck Jump
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and knees soft.
Drop into a shallow quarter-squat and explode vertically.
Tuck your knees up aggressively toward your chest in mid-air.
Slap your knees lightly with hands at peak height.
Extend legs quickly to land softly on balls of feet.
tips: Explode straight up and tuck knees high.
Land softly and rebound immediately if trained.
commonMistakes: Landing with straight locked knees.
Kicking heels back to buttocks instead of tucking knees to chest.
safetyNotes: High-impact plyometric; verify joint readiness.
contraindications: Severe joint degeneration.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Thoracic Spine Foam Rolling
steps: Sit on your mat and position a foam roller horizontally across your mid-back.
Interlace your fingers behind your head to support the weight of your neck.
Lift your hips slightly and roll slowly between your mid-back and upper shoulders.
Pause at tight segments, lower your hips, and gently arch back over the roller.
Exhale smoothly as you extend your upper back over the roller.
Continue working your upper thoracic spine for the allotted sixty seconds.
tips: Keep your elbows pointed forward to pull shoulder blades apart and expose tissue.
Never roll down onto your unsupported lumbar spine.
commonMistakes: Rolling onto the lower back or neck vertebrae directly.
Pulling violently on your head and hyper-flexing your cervical spine.
safetyNotes: Keep the roller strictly on the rib-supported thoracic region between shoulder blades.
contraindications: Osteoporosis, vertebral compression fractures, or unhealed rib injury.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tower Spring The Roll Over
steps: Lie on back with arms by sides and legs extended together.
Inhale and lift legs to ninety degrees perpendicular to floor.
Exhale and peel spine off mat to carry legs overhead parallel to floor.
Open legs shoulder-width, flex feet, and articulate down vertebra by vertebra.
Bring legs together at forty-five degrees and repeat.
tips: Roll through spine with deep abdominal scooping.
Never turn your head sideways during the roll-over.
commonMistakes: Throwing legs back with violent momentum.
Turning head sideways while neck is bearing weight.
safetyNotes: Do not turn head while inverted on upper back.
contraindications: Cervical spine disc injury.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tower Spring The Roll Up
steps: Lie supine with arms reaching overhead and legs glued together.
Inhale and lift arms toward ceiling, tucking chin to chest.
Exhale and roll up smoothly off mat vertebra by vertebra.
Reach forward over toes in a continuous C-curve spine.
Roll down vertebra by vertebra back to the mat.
tips: Articulate through each spinal segment without momentum.
Keep feet flexed and thighs squeezed together.
commonMistakes: Flinging arms forward to heave body up.
Collapsing lower back onto mat abruptly.
safetyNotes: Control the descent to protect lumbar vertebrae.
contraindications: Acute lumbar disc herniation.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tower Spring The Saw
steps: Sit tall with legs opened slightly wider than your shoulders.
Extend arms out to sides at shoulder height with palms down.
Inhale and rotate torso to right with tall erect spine.
Exhale and reach left pinky finger past right pinky toe.
Complete the target reps, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Anchor both sit bones firmly to the mat throughout the reach.
Rotate from the waist, not just the arms.
commonMistakes: Lifting opposite hip off the floor while reaching.
Slumping into rounded lower back.
safetyNotes: Maintain spinal elongation during rotation.
contraindications: Acute sciatica.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tower Spring The Seal
steps: Sit on mat, bend knees, and thread arms through inner thighs to grip outer ankles.
Lift feet off mat and balance on sitting bones.
Clap feet together three times like a seal.
Roll back onto shoulder blades, clap feet three times, and roll up to balance.
Repeat the rolling sequence smoothly for target repetitions.
tips: Roll only onto upper shoulder blades; never roll onto neck.
Use deep core scoop to control balance at top.
commonMistakes: Rolling back onto cervical vertebrae.
Unclasping ankles and losing body shape.
safetyNotes: Never roll onto the neck.
contraindications: Cervical disc injury.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tower Spring Single Leg Stretch
steps: Lie on your back on your mat and bring both knees into your chest.
Curl your head and shoulder blades off the mat into an abdominal curl.
Extend your left leg forward at a forty-five-degree angle while drawing right knee in.
Place your left hand on your right knee and right hand on your right ankle.
Switch legs smoothly, extending your right leg and pulling left knee into chest.
Complete the target reps, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your torso completely stable and quiet as your legs alternate.
Keep your outside hand near your ankle and inside hand near your knee.
commonMistakes: Rocking your hips and torso side to side as your legs switch.
Dropping your shoulder blades down onto the mat between repetitions.
safetyNotes: Rest your head on the mat if your neck extensors become fatigued.
contraindications: Acute cervical strain or unhealed abdominal surgery.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tower Spring Swan Dive
steps: Lie prone with palms flat beside shoulders and legs together.
Inhale and press through hands, lifting chest into long extension.
Rock forward onto ribs, lifting legs up behind you as arms reach forward.
Rock back onto thighs, catching yourself lightly on hands.
Maintain continuous rocking arc for prescribed repetitions.
tips: Keep abdominal wall scooped to protect lumbar spine.
Maintain a uniform arc from crown to toes.
commonMistakes: Collapsing into lumbar hyperextension.
Throwing head back aggressively.
safetyNotes: Do not force extension if lower back pinches.
contraindications: Spondylolysis or acute spinal stenosis.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tower Spring The Hundred
steps: Lie on your back on a mat and bring both knees into your chest.
Curl your head, neck, and shoulder blades smoothly off the mat.
Extend your legs forward to a forty-five-degree angle in Pilates stance.
Reach your arms long by your sides hovering two inches off the floor.
Pump your arms briskly up and down from the shoulders in a six-inch range.
Inhale deeply for five arm pumps, then exhale completely for five arm pumps.
Complete ten breath cycles for a total of one hundred arm pumps.
tips: Pump your arms from the back of your shoulders with firm straight elbows.
Anchor your lower back into the mat by drawing your navel deeply to your spine.
commonMistakes: Pumping from the wrists or elbows instead of moving from the shoulder joint.
Letting your lower back peel up off the mat as legs extend.
safetyNotes: If your neck strains or lower back arches, bend your knees into tabletop.
contraindications: Acute cervical spine disc herniation or active diastasis recti.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tower Spring The Teaser
steps: Lie flat on your mat with arms reaching overhead and legs extended together.
Inhale and lift your arms and head to begin rolling forward off the mat.
Simultaneously lift your legs straight to a forty-five-degree angle.
Roll up into a balanced V-sit position on your sacrum with arms parallel to legs.
Pause for two seconds at the apex, lifting through your chest with open collarbones.
Articulate your spine smoothly back down onto the mat vertebra by vertebra.
tips: Roll through the spine with articulation rather than snapping up with momentum.
Keep your inner thighs firmly squeezed together throughout the movement.
commonMistakes: Flinging arms forward and using sudden jerking momentum to sit up.
Collapsing chest and slouching at the top of the V-position.
safetyNotes: Control the descent vertebra by vertebra to protect lumbar spine integrity.
contraindications: Severe osteoporosis or acute lumbar spinal disc herniation.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tower Spring Reformer Elephant
steps: Stand on reformer carriage with heels flat against shoulder blocks.
Place hands flat on footbar and round spine into a deep C-curve.
Press carriage away by pushing through heels using glutes and hamstrings.
Draw carriage home by scooping abdominals deeply without moving shoulders.
Maintain rounded back and head hanging heavy between arms.
tips: Keep heels anchored into carriage throughout.
Draw carriage in using deep lower abdominals.
commonMistakes: Lifting heels off carriage during movement.
Flattening lower back and looking up.
safetyNotes: Maintain secure grip on footbar.
contraindications: Acute hamstring tendonitis.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tower Spring Reformer Footwork - Toes
steps: Lie supine on the reformer carriage with shoulders resting lightly against the blocks.
Place the balls of both feet onto the footbar with heels together in Pilates V.
Maintain a neutral pelvis with your spine resting long and flat on the carriage.
Inhale and press the carriage away by extending your knees smoothly.
Reach full leg extension without hyperextending or locking out your knee joints.
Exhale and resist the springs as you bend your knees to return the carriage home.
tips: Keep your heels glued together and elevated at a steady height throughout.
Resist the carriage springs with control on the return stroke.
commonMistakes: Letting heels drop underneath the footbar during the press.
Allowing the carriage to crash loudly into the stoppers on the return.
safetyNotes: Confirm that reformer spring tension is properly configured before lying down.
contraindications: Acute Achilles tendonitis or recent foot stress fracture.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tower Spring Reformer Long Stretch
steps: Place hands on footbar and balls of feet against headrest in high plank.
Establish a long, rigid, continuous plank line.
Inhale and push carriage away by opening shoulder angle.
Exhale and pull carriage home by closing shoulders over footbar.
Maintain rigid core without sagging hips throughout.
tips: Keep shoulders depressed and long line from heels to crown.
Push and pull carriage purely from shoulder joints.
commonMistakes: Sagging hips toward springs.
Piking hips up into the air.
safetyNotes: Verify reformer springs are securely attached.
contraindications: Shoulder impingement.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tower Spring Reformer Short Box Round
aliases: Tower Spring Reformer Short Box Round
steps: Place the short box crosswise over the reformer carriage and secure the safety foot strap.
Sit on the box facing the footbar and slip both feet securely under the safety strap.
Flex your ankles firmly against the strap and round your spine into a deep C-curve.
Wrap your arms around your midsection and draw your navel toward your spine.
Roll back over your sit bones, maintaining the rounded C-curve until arms reach horizontal.
Use your deep abdominals to curl back up over your pelvis without releasing the curve.
tips: Anchor into the foot strap with flexed feet for firm pelvic stability.
Keep the C-curve uniform from crown to tailbone rather than hinging in lower back.
commonMistakes: Flattening your back and turning the roll into a straight-back hinge.
Forgetting to verify the safety foot strap is securely fastened.
safetyNotes: Always inspect and secure the foot safety strap before sitting on the short box.
contraindications: Acute spinal stenosis or lumbar facet syndrome aggravated by deep flexion.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tree Pose
steps: Stand tall in mountain pose with your feet rooted firmly beneath your hips.
Shift your weight into your left foot and lift your right knee.
Place the sole of your right foot against your left inner calf or inner thigh.
Never place your foot directly against the side of your standing knee joint.
Bring your palms together in front of your chest at prayer position.
Fix your gaze on a stable unmoving point ahead to sustain balance.
Hold for thirty seconds, then release and repeat with equal duration on your left foot.
tips: Press your standing thigh and foot sole firmly into each other.
Engage your standing glute to keep your pelvis level.
commonMistakes: Resting the foot sole directly against the inner knee joint.
Letting the standing hip jut out sideways.
safetyNotes: Position hands near a wall if balance feels unsteady.
contraindications: Acute ankle sprain or inner ear balance pathology.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tuck Archer Push-Up
steps: Assume a very wide hand placement on the floor.
Lower body toward your right hand while extending left arm completely straight.
Press up powerfully through right arm to return to center.
Complete prescribed repetitions, then switch sides and repeat on left arm.
tips: Keep the extended arm locked straight to isolate the working arm.
Keep core rigid throughout.
commonMistakes: Twisting hips unevenly off horizontal.
Letting straight arm collapse.
safetyNotes: Warm up shoulders and chest thoroughly.
contraindications: Shoulder anterior instability.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tuck Chin-Up
steps: Grip pull-up bar with an underhand grip shoulder-width apart.
Hang with straight arms and engaged shoulders.
Pull elbows down and back, driving chin cleanly over the bar.
Lower body under steady control to full arm extension.
tips: Squeeze biceps and lats tightly at top of rep.
Keep legs together and core tight.
commonMistakes: Swinging hips to generate momentum.
Dropping rapidly without controlling the descent.
safetyNotes: Control the descent to protect elbow joints.
contraindications: Medial epicondylitis (golfer elbow).

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tuck Diamond Push-Up
steps: Place hands together directly under chest with thumbs and index fingers touching.
Form a straight plank line from heels to crown.
Lower chest down to touch the back of your hands.
Press up forcefully through triceps to full arm extension.
tips: Keep elbows tucked close to your ribcage.
Maintain an active core brace.
commonMistakes: Flaring elbows wide out to sides.
Sagging at the hips.
safetyNotes: Stop if inner elbow or wrist discomfort occurs.
contraindications: Triceps tendonitis or wrist impingement.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tuck Dragon Flag
steps: Lie on a sturdy bench and grip the bench edges tightly behind your head.
Roll bodyweight onto your upper shoulders and lift your entire torso.
Form a rigid straight line from shoulders to pointed toes.
Lower your straight body slowly toward the bench, then lift back up.
tips: Pivot purely on your upper back and shoulders.
Do not allow hips to bend or sag.
commonMistakes: Bending at the waist and breaking body alignment.
Resting heavy compressive load on the neck.
safetyNotes: Never bear compressive weight on cervical spine.
contraindications: Acute lower back disc injury.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tuck Full Front Lever Hold
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulders.
Retract and depress your scapulae with locked straight elbows.
Pull down against the bar through your lats to raise your torso and legs.
Lock your entire body into a completely horizontal plane parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your glutes and quads tightly while holding the horizontal position steady.
tips: Generate intense straight-arm pulling torque through your latissimus dorsi.
Keep your body straight from shoulders to toes without sagging at the hips.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows to compensate for insufficient straight-arm lat strength.
Piking at the hips rather than maintaining a true horizontal line.
safetyNotes: Warm up your shoulders, elbows, and bicep tendons thoroughly prior to max holds.
contraindications: Distal biceps tendon strain or acute rotator cuff injury.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tuck Wall-Assisted Handstand Push-Up
steps: Place your hands about eight inches away from a sturdy wall.
Kick up into a handstand with heels resting gently against the wall.
Establish an active hollow body position with your glutes and abs tight.
Lower your head forward slightly to touch your crown softly to the mat.
Form a stable tripod shape with your head positioned ahead of your hands.
Press hard through your palms and extend your arms to return to the full handstand.
tips: Avoid flaring your elbows wide; keep them tucked at a forty-five degree angle.
Push the floor away aggressively at the top into an active shoulder shrug.
commonMistakes: Collapsing your neck onto the floor with unbuffered velocity.
Banana-arching your lower back and resting your entire spine against the wall.
safetyNotes: Always place an exercise mat beneath your head to protect the cervical spine.
contraindications: High blood pressure, glaucoma, retinal detachment, or cervical spine disc injury.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tuck Hanging Leg Raise
steps: Hang from an overhead pull-up bar with an overhand shoulder-width grip.
Depress your scapulae to engage your lats and eliminate passive swinging.
Point your toes, squeeze your legs together, and brace your core.
Raise your straight legs upward until your shins are parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top to emphasize lower abdominal contraction.
Lower your legs back down under strict muscular control to the dead hang.
tips: Posteriorly tilt your pelvis at the top to ensure your abs flex fully.
Do not swing your legs backward past the vertical plane between reps.
commonMistakes: Using pendulum momentum and arching your lower back to fling the legs up.
Bending knees excessively when performing the straight-leg variant.
safetyNotes: Control the lowering phase to avoid sudden lumbar hyperextension.
contraindications: Acute abdominal muscle strain or severe hip flexor tendinitis.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tuck Hollow Body Hold
steps: Lie on your back on an exercise mat with arms and legs fully extended.
Press your lower back firmly into the floor so there is zero gap under your spine.
Lift your shoulder blades and legs two to four inches off the ground.
Reach your arms overhead past your ears while pointing your toes forward.
Maintain this continuous banana-shaped hollow body arc for the target hold duration.
tips: Your lower back must stay glued to the floor for the entire set.
Breathe shallowly through your diaphragm without releasing abdominal brace.
commonMistakes: Letting your lower back arch and lift off the floor under fatigue.
Craning your neck excessively forward rather than tucking your chin slightly.
safetyNotes: If your lower back begins peeling off the floor, regress by tucking your knees.
contraindications: Acute lumbar disc herniation aggravated by posterior pelvic tilt.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tuck Inverted Row
steps: Lie under a waist-height bar and grasp with an overhand grip.
Extend legs forward with heels grounded and body in a straight plank.
Pull chest up to touch the bar by driving elbows back.
Lower body smoothly back to full arm extension.
tips: Keep body completely straight like an iron plank.
Retract shoulder blades fully at peak.
commonMistakes: Sagging hips toward the floor.
Poking chin forward to touch the bar.
safetyNotes: Adjust bar height to scale difficulty.
contraindications: Rotator cuff strain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Plyometric Tuck Jump
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and knees soft.
Drop into a shallow quarter-squat and explode vertically.
Tuck your knees up aggressively toward your chest in mid-air.
Slap your knees lightly with hands at peak height.
Extend legs quickly to land softly on balls of feet.
tips: Explode straight up and tuck knees high.
Land softly and rebound immediately if trained.
commonMistakes: Landing with straight locked knees.
Kicking heels back to buttocks instead of tucking knees to chest.
safetyNotes: High-impact plyometric; verify joint readiness.
contraindications: Severe joint degeneration.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tuck L-Sit Hold
steps: Mount parallel bars with straight locked arms and depressed shoulders.
Lift straight legs in front of you until parallel to the floor.
Point toes forward and squeeze quadriceps tightly.
Hold the strict L-shape for the target hold duration.
tips: Push the floor or bars away actively through palms.
Keep knees fully locked out straight.
commonMistakes: Bending knees due to weak hip flexors.
Shrugging shoulders into ears.
safetyNotes: Warm up wrists and shoulders thoroughly.
contraindications: Severe hip flexor tendinitis.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tuck Nordic Hamstring Curl
steps: Kneel on a padded mat with your ankles secured firmly under a support.
Align knees, hips, and shoulders in one rigid vertical line.
Lower torso forward toward the floor as slowly as possible using hamstrings.
Catch yourself on hands, push lightly, and pull back up with hamstrings.
tips: Resist gravity for as long as possible on the way down.
Keep hips extended without breaking at the waist.
commonMistakes: Bending at the hips to avoid hamstring loading.
Falling forward without muscular control.
safetyNotes: Cushion knees with thick padding.
contraindications: Acute hamstring strain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tuck Parallel Bar Dip
steps: Mount the parallel bars and lock out your arms with shoulders depressed.
Lean your torso forward roughly fifteen degrees to engage your chest.
Bend your elbows to lower your body downward smoothly.
Descend until your shoulders are level with or slightly below your elbows.
Press through your palms to extend your arms back to the top support position.
tips: Keep your elbows tucked at roughly forty-five degrees rather than flared.
Maintain an active hollow body position with crossed or straight ankles.
commonMistakes: Dipping too shallow and cutting the range of motion in half.
Allowing your shoulders to shrug upward toward your ears under load.
safetyNotes: Avoid excessive downward depth if you experience anterior shoulder pain.
contraindications: Acute sternoclavicular joint injury or anterior glenohumeral instability.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tuck Pistol Squat
steps: Stand balanced on your right leg and extend your left leg straight in front of you.
Reach your arms forward to counterbalance your center of mass.
Hinge your hips slightly and bend your right knee to descend smoothly.
Lower down fully until your right hamstring rests against your calf.
Keep your left heel elevated completely off the ground throughout.
Drive firmly through your right foot to stand back up to tall extension.
Switch and perform the same number of reps on your opposite left leg.
tips: Maintain deep ankle dorsiflexion and keep your heel planted firmly.
Round your upper back slightly to maintain forward counterbalance.
commonMistakes: Allowing your standing heel to lift off the floor during the descent.
Letting the elevated non-working leg touch the ground.
safetyNotes: Requires substantial ankle and knee integrity; progress using box support first.
contraindications: Severe patellofemoral osteoarthritis or recovering meniscus repair.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tuck Standard Pull-Up
steps: Grip the overhead pull-up bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than your shoulders.
Hang at full arm extension in an active dead hang with engaged shoulder blades.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes into a hollow body shape.
Pull your elbows down toward your hips while driving your chest toward the bar.
Continue pulling smoothly until your chin clears the top edge of the bar.
Lower yourself under steady control back to the complete active hang.
tips: Initiate the pull by depressing your scapulae before bending your arms.
Keep your legs glued together to avoid leaking core tension.
commonMistakes: Kicking your legs or kipping with momentum to reach the top.
Shortening repetitions by failing to reach full arm lockout at the bottom.
safetyNotes: Do not relax into an inactive joint hang with limp shoulders at the bottom.
contraindications: Acute shoulder labrum tear or severe golfer elbow flare-up.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tuck Push-Up
steps: Set hands slightly wider than shoulders on the floor.
Keep feet together and form a rigid straight plank line.
Lower body smoothly until chest hovers just off the floor.
Press the ground away forcefully to complete arm lockout.
tips: Keep elbows angled at forty-five degrees like an arrow.
Squeeze glutes to protect lower spine.
commonMistakes: Sagging hips toward the mat during descent.
Flaring elbows wide at ninety degrees.
safetyNotes: Keep wrists stacked comfortably.
contraindications: Acute wrist sprain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Tuck Standard Push-Up
steps: Place your hands on the ground slightly wider than your shoulders.
Extend your legs behind you with feet together and form a straight body line.
Squeeze your glutes and draw your belly button toward your spine.
Lower your entire body until your chest hovers an inch above the floor.
Push the ground away forcefully until your arms lock out smoothly at the top.
tips: Position your elbows in an arrow shape relative to your torso.
Keep your neck neutral by gazing at a spot slightly ahead of your hands.
commonMistakes: Sagging your hips toward the floor and hyperextending your lumbar spine.
Poking your chin down to make it feel like you reached full depth.
safetyNotes: Keep your wrists stacked comfortably or use push-up handles if wrists ache.
contraindications: Acute wrist sprain or unhealed scaphoid fracture.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Victorious Breath
steps: Sit comfortably or practice during gentle asana transitions.
Inhale and exhale exclusively through your nose.
Constrict the back of your throat slightly as if whispering with mouth closed.
Create a soft, soothing ocean-wave sound on both inhale and exhale.
Keep inhalations and exhalations of equal length and depth.
Maintain continuous Ujjayi breath for five to ten minutes.
tips: The throat constriction is gentle, like fogging a mirror with mouth closed.
Use sound as a rhythm anchor for the mind.
commonMistakes: Constricting throat too tightly and straining vocal cords.
Breathing through mouth.
safetyNotes: Keep sound gentle and effortless.
contraindications: Severe throat infection or acute laryngitis.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Wide-Angle Seated Forward Bend
steps: Sit on your mat and open your legs wide apart into a comfortable V-shape.
Flex both feet with toes pointing straight up toward the ceiling.
Place hands on the floor in front of you and sit tall on your sit bones.
Inhale, then exhale and walk your hands forward along the floor.
Lower your chest toward the floor while maintaining a flat, long spine.
Hold for forty-five seconds while breathing into your inner thighs.
tips: Sit on a folded blanket to tilt your pelvis forward if lower back rounds.
Keep kneecaps and toes pointing upward throughout.
commonMistakes: Allowing thighs and feet to roll inward as you fold.
Slouching through the lower back instead of hinging.
safetyNotes: Stop folding if sharp pain occurs in inner groin.
contraindications: Groin adductor tear or hamstring avulsion.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Wheel Pose (Upward Bow)
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet planted flat hip-width apart.
Place your palms flat on the floor beside your ears with fingers pointing toward shoulders.
Press through feet and hands simultaneously to lift your hips and chest off the mat.
Pause on the crown of your head to adjust elbows in, then push arms straight.
Open your chest toward the wall behind you while pressing firmly through big toes.
Hold the full backbend for thirty seconds, then tuck chin and lower slowly.
tips: Distribute the arc evenly through shoulders and upper back.
Keep thighs parallel and avoid letting feet turn outward.
commonMistakes: Letting feet splay out wide, compressing lumbar spine.
Pushing purely from lower back without opening shoulders.
safetyNotes: Tuck chin to chest before lowering down to protect neck.
contraindications: Carpal tunnel, high blood pressure, detached retina, or pregnancy.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Upward Salute
steps: Begin standing tall in mountain pose with your core gently engaged.
Inhale and sweep both arms out and overhead in a wide circular arc.
Turn your palms to face each other or press them gently together overhead.
Keep your shoulders drawn down away from your ears as you reach up.
Gaze toward your thumbs without compressing the back of your cervical spine.
Hold for thirty seconds while lengthening through both sides of your ribcage.
tips: Anchor firmly through your feet as you reach vertically through your fingertips.
Keep your ribs drawn downward rather than flaring your ribcage out.
commonMistakes: Shrugging shoulders up toward the ears, pinching the neck.
Leaning backward and compressing the lumbar vertebrae.
safetyNotes: Avoid severe neck hyperextension if cervical pain occurs.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Upward-Facing Dog
steps: Lie prone and place hands beside lower ribs with elbows stacked over wrists.
Press tops of feet and palms firmly into the yoga mat.
Inhale, straighten arms fully, and lift torso and thighs completely off the floor.
Roll shoulders back and draw chest forward through the window of your arms.
Keep thighs engaged and off the mat with knees lifted.
Hold for thirty seconds, then lower down or transition to downward dog.
tips: Keep thighs and knees elevated off the mat throughout.
Broaden across your collarbones and draw shoulder blades down.
commonMistakes: Sagging hips onto the mat and jamming into lower back.
Locking shoulders up into the ears.
safetyNotes: Ensure wrist joints are stacked comfortably under shoulders.
contraindications: Carpal tunnel syndrome or late-term pregnancy.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Camel Pose
steps: Kneel upright with your knees hip-width apart and thighs vertical.
Place your hands on your lower back with fingers pointing down for support.
Press your hips gently forward and lift your sternum toward the ceiling.
Reach back one hand at a time to grasp your heels or keep hands on lower back.
Open your chest fully while keeping thighs perpendicular to the floor.
Hold with steady breath for thirty seconds, then carefully sit back onto heels.
tips: Keep hips pressed forward over your knees rather than sagging backward.
Lift upward through the sternum to avoid crunching lower back.
commonMistakes: Dropping hips backward over heels.
Dropping the head backward violently and pinching cervical vertebrae.
safetyNotes: Keep hands on sacrum if reaching heels strains lower back.
contraindications: Severe lower back disc disease or cervical injury.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Goddess Pose
steps: Step feet wide apart on your mat with toes turned outward at forty-five degrees.
Bend your knees deeply, lowering hips until thighs are parallel to the floor.
Ensure your knees track directly over your middle toes.
Bring arms into cactus shape with elbows at shoulder height and palms facing forward.
Tuck your tailbone slightly and keep your torso completely vertical.
Hold the wide squat steadily while taking slow, deep diaphragmatic breaths.
tips: Press knees outward away from centerline to activate outer hips and glutes.
Stack your shoulders directly over your hips.
commonMistakes: Leaning forward and collapsing chest toward thighs.
Allowing knees to cave inward past ankles.
safetyNotes: Align knees over second toes to avoid joint torque.
contraindications: Recent groin pull or knee ligament strain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Chair Pose
steps: Stand with feet together or hip-width apart with arms by your sides.
Inhale and sweep your arms overhead with palms facing inward.
Exhale and bend your knees deeply, shifting your hips back as if sitting in a low chair.
Keep your weight centered over your heels and midfoot so toes can wiggle.
Lift your chest high and draw your belly button toward your spine.
Hold the squat with steady breath for the prescribed duration.
tips: Shift your knees back so you can see your toes in front of your kneecaps.
Keep your lower back long without excessive lumbar sway.
commonMistakes: Letting knees travel far forward over the toes, overloading patella.
Arching lower back into a deep swayback curve.
safetyNotes: Keep weight back into heels to protect kneecaps.
contraindications: Acute patellofemoral pain syndrome or severe arthritis.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Standing Forward Fold
steps: Stand in mountain pose with feet hip-width apart and hands on hips.
Inhale deeply to lengthen your spine toward the ceiling.
Exhale and hinge forward from your hip creases with an extended flat back.
Place your fingertips on the floor or rest hands on your shins or blocks.
Release your neck and let the crown of your head hang heavy toward the floor.
Hold for forty-five seconds while lifting your sitting bones toward the ceiling.
tips: Bend your knees softly if tight hamstrings cause your lower back to round.
Shift your weight forward slightly over the balls of your feet.
commonMistakes: Rounding aggressively through the lumbar spine to reach the floor.
Locking the knees into backward hyperextension.
safetyNotes: Hinge strictly from hips to avoid lumbar strain.
contraindications: Acute lumbar disc herniation or hamstring tear.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Extended Side Angle Pose
steps: Set up in Warrior II with your right knee bent directly over your ankle.
Rest your right forearm gently on your right thigh just above the knee.
Reach your left arm up and overhead creating a straight diagonal line from foot to fingers.
Spiral your chest upward toward the ceiling and gaze toward your left palm.
Press firmly into the outer blade of your back left foot.
Hold for thirty seconds, then rise, switch sides, and repeat with left leg forward.
tips: Keep your front thigh parallel to the mat and maintain deep hip flexion.
Avoid dumping your torso weight passively onto the resting forearm.
commonMistakes: Letting your top shoulder roll downward toward the floor.
Collapsing the arch of your rear foot.
safetyNotes: Maintain active core lift to protect resting shoulder joint.
contraindications: Recent knee injury or severe cervical disc issue.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Extended Triangle Pose
steps: Step feet wide apart with right foot pointing forward and left foot angled slightly inward.
Extend your arms out to shoulder height with palms facing down.
Inhale and reach your right arm forward directly over your right thigh.
Hinge at the right hip and bring your right hand to your shin, ankle, or a yoga block.
Extend your left arm straight up toward the ceiling and gaze toward your top thumb.
Hold with open chest, then reverse feet and repeat the posture on your left side.
tips: Prioritize lengthening both sides of your waist over touching the floor.
Imagine leaning the back of your body flat against an invisible wall.
commonMistakes: Resting heavy bodyweight onto the front shin or knee joint.
Collapsing your chest forward toward the ground.
safetyNotes: Use a yoga block under the lower hand to keep spine long.
contraindications: Severe hamstring strain or acute neck pain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Thunderbolt Pose
steps: Kneel on mat with knees and big toes touching.
Lower buttocks to rest comfortably on tops of heels.
Place palms flat on thighs with fingers pointing forward.
Sit tall with crown of head lifting toward ceiling.
Relax shoulders and breathe calmly into abdomen.
Hold for sixty seconds for post-meal digestive benefit.
tips: Place a blanket between calves and thighs if knees feel tight.
Keep spine vertically stacked.
commonMistakes: Slouching forward over thighs.
Letting ankles roll outward.
safetyNotes: Place cushion under ankles if tops of feet ache.
contraindications: Recent knee surgery or severe ankle sprains.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Legs-Up-the-Wall Pose
steps: Sit sideways with one hip against a sturdy wall.
Pivot on buttocks and swing legs up the wall as you lie back.
Rest back and head flat on mat with legs resting vertically.
Open arms out to sides with palms facing upward.
Close eyes and let gravitational drainage soothe legs.
Hold for sixty seconds while breathing naturally.
tips: Place a bolster under hips for elevated pelvic relaxation.
Allow all leg musculature to soften completely.
commonMistakes: Scooting too far from the wall so legs slide down.
Straining neck or shoulders.
safetyNotes: Maintain comfortable position for passive restorative blood flow.
contraindications: Glaucoma or late-term pregnancy.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Warrior I
steps: From standing, step your left foot back roughly four feet along your mat.
Angle your back left foot forty-five degrees outward with your heel grounded firmly.
Square your hips forward toward the front edge of your yoga mat.
Bend your front right knee until it stacks directly over your front ankle.
Inhale and raise both arms overhead with palms facing inward toward each other.
Hold with a tall spine, then switch sides and repeat with left leg leading.
tips: Press deeply into the outer heel of your back foot to stabilize your pelvis.
Sink hips lower while keeping your front knee tracking over middle toes.
commonMistakes: Letting the back heel peel off the mat during the posture.
Twisting through the lower back to force hips forward.
safetyNotes: Keep the back heel anchored to maintain knee alignment.
contraindications: Severe high blood pressure or acute knee injury.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Warrior III
steps: Stand balanced on your right foot with hands on your hips.
Hinge forward at your right hip as you extend your left leg straight behind you.
Bring your torso and left leg into a single horizontal line parallel to the ground.
Reach your arms forward past your ears or extend them back alongside your hips.
Flex your left foot and point all five toes straight down toward the mat.
Hold for thirty seconds with level hips, then switch and repeat on left leg.
tips: Keep both hip bones pointing evenly toward the floor like headlights.
Micro-bend your standing knee to avoid hyperextension.
commonMistakes: Opening the lifted hip upward and twisting the pelvis out of alignment.
Rounding the upper back and dropping the chest toward the floor.
safetyNotes: Engage core firmly to support lumbar spine during horizontal hold.
contraindications: Severe vertigo or uncontrolled balance disorders.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Hero Pose
steps: Kneel on mat with knees together and feet separated wider than hips.
Tops of feet rest flat on mat with toes pointing straight back.
Lower buttocks to sit on floor or block between heels.
Rest hands on thighs and lengthen spine tall.
Hold for sixty seconds with steady, measured breaths.
tips: Sit on a block between feet to eliminate knee strain.
Do not allow feet to roll inward.
commonMistakes: Sitting between feet when knees feel pinching pain.
Slumping lower back.
safetyNotes: Use block under sitting bones if knees feel torque.
contraindications: Knee ligament tear or meniscus pathology.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Walking Dumbbell Lunge
steps: Stand upright holding a pair of dumbbells securely at your sides.
Step forward with your right leg into an elongated stride position.
Lower your hips until your right thigh is parallel to the ground.
Ensure your back left knee gently hovers one inch above the floor.
Drive through your right front heel to rise and step forward with the left leg.
Repeat the movement alternating sides evenly for all prescribed repetitions.
tips: Keep your torso tall and vertical without tilting forward at your hips.
Track your front knee directly over your middle toes.
commonMistakes: Collapsing your front knee inward during the deceleration phase.
Slamming your rear kneecap violently against hard flooring.
safetyNotes: Maintain balance and step with adequate width to prevent knee torque.
contraindications: Acute patellofemoral pain syndrome or severe balance disorders.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Wall-Assisted Cat-Cow Dynamic Stretch
steps: Set up on hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
Inhale into cow pose by dropping your belly and lifting your chest and tailbone.
Exhale into cat pose by tucking your tailbone and rounding your spine up.
Press firmly through your palms to spread your shoulder blades apart.
Flow continuously between extension and flexion in rhythm with your breath.
tips: Articulate the movement vertebra by vertebra starting from your pelvis.
Keep your elbows unlocked throughout the transition.
commonMistakes: Cramming into cervical hyperextension by jerking the chin up too far.
Moving with rapid uncontrolled pace rather than smooth segmental articulation.
safetyNotes: Stay within a comfortable pain-free range of motion without forcing end ranges.
contraindications: Severe acute disc prolapse aggravated by flexion.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Wall-Assisted Doorway Pectoral Stretch
steps: Stand in an open doorway and place forearms flat against doorframe.
Position elbows at ninety degrees at shoulder height.
Step forward with one foot until you feel a gentle chest stretch.
Keep your neck relaxed and chest broad.
Hold the stretch for thirty seconds with steady breathing.
tips: Step gently forward to regulate stretch intensity.
Keep ribs pulled down.
commonMistakes: Pressing forward with aggressive sudden force.
Shrugging shoulders into ears.
safetyNotes: Do not over-stretch anterior shoulder capsule.
contraindications: Anterior shoulder instability.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Wall-Assisted Latissimus Dorsi Foam Rolling
steps: Lie on your right side with a foam roller beneath your armpit.
Extend your right arm straight along the floor overhead.
Roll slowly along the outer ribcage and latissimus dorsi.
Pause on tight spots and take slow deep breaths.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Roll only along muscular tissue, avoiding lower ribs.
Regulate pressure using your feet.
commonMistakes: Rolling directly onto floating lower ribs.
Tensing up and holding breath.
safetyNotes: Keep roller on muscular lat belly.
contraindications: Osteoporosis or rib fracture.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Wall-Assisted Quadriceps Foam Rolling
steps: Lie prone on your mat with a foam roller under your thighs.
Support your upper body on your forearms in a low plank.
Roll slowly from the top of your hips down to just above knees.
Pause and breathe on tender trigger points for twenty seconds.
Continue rolling along the muscle belly for sixty seconds.
tips: Keep your core gently braced to prevent lower back sagging.
Relax quadricep tissue.
commonMistakes: Rolling directly over the kneecap bone.
Holding your breath while rolling tender areas.
safetyNotes: Never roll directly onto bone or joint capsules.
contraindications: Acute thigh hematoma.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Wall-Assisted Standing Hamstring Stretch
steps: Stand tall and place your right heel on a low bench or step.
Flex your right foot with toes pointing upward.
Hinge forward from your hips with a flat back.
Feel a gentle stretch through the back of your right thigh.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Hinge from the hips rather than rounding the lower back.
Keep your standing leg stable.
commonMistakes: Rounding the spine to force head toward knee.
Locking knee into painful hyperextension.
safetyNotes: Avoid aggressive stretching into sharp pain.
contraindications: Acute hamstring tear.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Wall-Assisted Quadruped Hip CARs
steps: Assume a quadruped tabletop position on your hands and knees.
Brace your core and lift your right knee toward your chest.
Open your right knee out to the side in abduction.
Rotate hip internally and drive heel toward ceiling.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Isolate the hip capsule without moving lower back.
Imagine tracing the biggest circle possible.
commonMistakes: Arching or twisting your spine to compensate.
Rushing through sticky ranges.
safetyNotes: Move slowly with total joint control.
contraindications: Hip labral tear or severe impingement.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Wall-Assisted Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
steps: Kneel on your left knee and step your right foot forward in a half-kneeling stance.
Maintain ninety-degree angles at both front and back knee joints.
Posteriorly tilt your pelvis by tucking your tailbone and squeezing your left glute.
Shift your hips forward slightly until you feel a deep stretch in front of your left hip.
Keep your torso completely vertical and hold the position for thirty seconds.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: The posterior pelvic tilt is what isolates the psoas; do not arch your lower back.
Raise your left arm overhead to intensify the stretch through the entire fascial line.
commonMistakes: Hyperextending the lumbar spine and dumping all forward travel into the lower back.
Failing to contract the trailing glute during the hold.
safetyNotes: Place a folded mat or cushion under the rear knee for comfort.
contraindications: Acute patellar bursitis on the kneeling knee or acute hip labral pathology.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Wall-Assisted 90-90 Hip Switch
steps: Sit on the floor with your front right leg bent at ninety degrees.
Position your trailing left leg bent at ninety degrees to your side.
Sit tall with your spine erect, using your hands behind you for support if needed.
Lift your knees and pivot on your heels to sweep your legs across to the left.
Finish in the mirror ninety-ninety position with your left leg leading in front.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your heels anchored into the ground as you transition between sides.
Strive to perform the rotation without placing your hands on the ground as you progress.
commonMistakes: Slouching through the lower back to compensate for limited hip capsule rotation.
Letting knees collapse with uncontrolled momentum.
safetyNotes: Do not force end-range internal rotation if you feel pinching inside the hip joint.
contraindications: Hip labral tear with femoral acetabular impingement (FAI).

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Wall-Assisted Quadruped Thoracic Rotation
steps: Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Place your right hand behind your head with elbow wide.
Rotate your right elbow down toward your left forearm on inhale.
Exhale and rotate your chest up toward ceiling, pointing elbow high.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Rotate from your upper thoracic back, keeping hips square.
Move smoothly with breath.
commonMistakes: Shifting hips sideways to cheat through rotation.
Pulling on the neck with the hand.
safetyNotes: Keep movement comfortable within joint range.
contraindications: Thoracic facet joint irritation.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Wall-Assisted Standing Shoulder CARs
steps: Stand tall with a rigid braced core and fists clenched.
Raise your right straight arm forward and up past your ear.
At peak overhead height, rotate your bicep outward.
Continue the circle backward, rotating arm internally as it reaches behind.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Do not let your torso twist or arch to assist the arm.
Move slowly through the entire circumference.
commonMistakes: Arching lower back when arm passes overhead.
Shrugging shoulder up into ear.
safetyNotes: Work strictly in pain-free joint range.
contraindications: Rotator cuff impingement.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Wall-Assisted Resistance Band Shoulder Pass-Through
steps: Stand tall holding a light resistance band with a wide overhand grip.
Lock your elbows straight and hold the band across your front thighs.
Raise your arms up overhead in a wide smooth arc without bending elbows.
Continue the arc behind your back until the band lightly touches your glutes.
Reverse the arc smoothly to bring the band back overhead to the front.
Repeat for ten continuous fluid repetitions.
tips: Widen your grip on the band if your elbows bend during the pass-through.
Keep your ribs pulled down and glutes squeezed to prevent lower back arching.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows as the band passes overhead.
Over-arching the spine to cheat through shoulder tightness.
safetyNotes: Use a wide enough grip so the band passes smoothly without sharp shoulder pain.
contraindications: Active anterior shoulder dislocation history or acute rotator cuff tear.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Wall-Assisted Standing Quadriceps Stretch
steps: Stand tall on your left foot using a wall for balance if needed.
Bend your right knee and grasp your right ankle with right hand.
Gently pull your heel toward your glute while keeping knees aligned.
Tuck your pelvis under to increase the stretch along front thigh.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your knees together rather than letting working knee flare out.
Maintain tall posture.
commonMistakes: Arching lower back excessively.
Pulling ankle out to the side.
safetyNotes: Keep knees close together to protect ligaments.
contraindications: Patellofemoral pain syndrome.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Wall-Assisted Thoracic Spine Foam Rolling
steps: Sit on your mat and position a foam roller horizontally across your mid-back.
Interlace your fingers behind your head to support the weight of your neck.
Lift your hips slightly and roll slowly between your mid-back and upper shoulders.
Pause at tight segments, lower your hips, and gently arch back over the roller.
Exhale smoothly as you extend your upper back over the roller.
Continue working your upper thoracic spine for the allotted sixty seconds.
tips: Keep your elbows pointed forward to pull shoulder blades apart and expose tissue.
Never roll down onto your unsupported lumbar spine.
commonMistakes: Rolling onto the lower back or neck vertebrae directly.
Pulling violently on your head and hyper-flexing your cervical spine.
safetyNotes: Keep the roller strictly on the rib-supported thoracic region between shoulder blades.
contraindications: Osteoporosis, vertebral compression fractures, or unhealed rib injury.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Wall-Assisted World's Greatest Stretch
steps: Step forward into a deep lunge with your right foot outside your right hand.
Place your left hand on the floor and lower your right elbow inside your right ankle.
Rotate your torso to the right and reach your right arm toward the ceiling.
Gaze up toward your right hand while keeping your left hip flexor extended.
Bring your right hand back down, rock back, and straighten your right front leg.
Complete the prescribed movement, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your back knee extended and back glute fired to maximize hip flexor opening.
Rotate from your upper back rather than twisting through your lumbar spine.
commonMistakes: Collapsing your back knee onto the floor during the rotational phase.
Craning your neck to compensate for limited thoracic spine rotation.
safetyNotes: Move smoothly between positions without snapping into end ranges.
contraindications: Acute groin adductor strain or lumbar facet joint irritation.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Warrior II
steps: Step your feet four feet apart along the length of your yoga mat.
Turn your right foot out ninety degrees and angle your left foot slightly inward.
Inhale and raise both arms parallel to the floor with palms facing down.
Exhale and bend your right knee until it stacks directly over your right ankle.
Gaze steadily over your right front middle finger and hold the pose.
Straighten your leg, reverse your foot positions, and repeat on your left side.
tips: Press firmly into the outer blade of your back foot to stabilize your pelvis.
Stack your shoulders directly above your hips rather than leaning forward.
commonMistakes: Allowing the front knee to collapse inward past the big toe.
Lifting the back arm lazily lower than shoulder height.
safetyNotes: Ensure the front knee stays aligned with the second toe to prevent knee torque.
contraindications: Recent knee ligament tear or severe hip bursitis.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Weighted Archer Push-Up
steps: Assume a very wide hand placement on the floor.
Lower body toward your right hand while extending left arm completely straight.
Press up powerfully through right arm to return to center.
Complete prescribed repetitions, then switch sides and repeat on left arm.
tips: Keep the extended arm locked straight to isolate the working arm.
Keep core rigid throughout.
commonMistakes: Twisting hips unevenly off horizontal.
Letting straight arm collapse.
safetyNotes: Warm up shoulders and chest thoroughly.
contraindications: Shoulder anterior instability.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Weighted Alternating Battle Rope Waves
steps: Stand facing the anchor holding one rope end firmly in each hand.
Assume a solid athletic stance with knees bent and chest lifted.
Whip your right arm upward and drive it back down forcefully.
Immediately alternate by whipping your left arm upward as the right descends.
Maintain a fast, continuous reciprocating rhythm to send fluid waves to the anchor.
Keep your torso anchored and core braced for the entire thirty-second interval.
tips: Generate waves through quick shoulder and arm cycling, not torso swaying.
Keep your weight centered over your midfoot in a stable athletic base.
commonMistakes: Standing straight-legged and letting rope recoil pull you off balance.
Holding your breath during high-frequency wave intervals.
safetyNotes: Ensure the rope anchor is structurally secure before beginning high-intensity intervals.
contraindications: Acute bicep tendonitis or active acromioclavicular shoulder pain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Weighted Plyometric Box Jump
steps: Stand facing a sturdy plyometric box half a step away with feet hip-width.
Swing your arms back and hinge your hips into an athletic quarter-squat.
Explode upward through your hips and swing arms forward aggressively.
Tuck your knees up and land softly on top of the box in an athletic squat.
Stand up completely on top of the box to verify full hip extension.
Step down carefully one foot at a time to reset for the next rep.
tips: Focus on landing quietly like a cat to absorb impact through your musculature.
Always step down rather than jumping backward off the box to spare your Achilles tendons.
commonMistakes: Rebounding backward off the box, creating high risk for Achilles rupture.
Landing with a loud thud and stiff knees on the box surface.
safetyNotes: Always step down one foot at a time; never jump backward off the box.
contraindications: Achilles tendinopathy, recent ACL reconstruction, or severe balance disorders.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Weighted Standing Broad Jump
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and swing arms backward.
Hinge hips into a loaded quarter-squat.
Explode forward and upward driving through hips and swinging arms.
Tuck knees slightly and land softly in a balanced athletic squat.
Reset your feet and repeat for prescribed repetitions.
tips: Focus on maximal horizontal hip displacement.
Absorb the landing softly with knees tracking over toes.
commonMistakes: Stiff-legged landing jarring lower back.
Allowing knees to cave inward on landing.
safetyNotes: Perform on shock-absorbing rubber or grass surfaces.
contraindications: Achilles tendinopathy.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Weighted Chin-Up
steps: Grip pull-up bar with an underhand grip shoulder-width apart.
Hang with straight arms and engaged shoulders.
Pull elbows down and back, driving chin cleanly over the bar.
Lower body under steady control to full arm extension.
tips: Squeeze biceps and lats tightly at top of rep.
Keep legs together and core tight.
commonMistakes: Swinging hips to generate momentum.
Dropping rapidly without controlling the descent.
safetyNotes: Control the descent to protect elbow joints.
contraindications: Medial epicondylitis (golfer elbow).

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Weighted Diamond Push-Up
steps: Place hands together directly under chest with thumbs and index fingers touching.
Form a straight plank line from heels to crown.
Lower chest down to touch the back of your hands.
Press up forcefully through triceps to full arm extension.
tips: Keep elbows tucked close to your ribcage.
Maintain an active core brace.
commonMistakes: Flaring elbows wide out to sides.
Sagging at the hips.
safetyNotes: Stop if inner elbow or wrist discomfort occurs.
contraindications: Triceps tendonitis or wrist impingement.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Weighted Dragon Flag
steps: Lie on a sturdy bench and grip the bench edges tightly behind your head.
Roll bodyweight onto your upper shoulders and lift your entire torso.
Form a rigid straight line from shoulders to pointed toes.
Lower your straight body slowly toward the bench, then lift back up.
tips: Pivot purely on your upper back and shoulders.
Do not allow hips to bend or sag.
commonMistakes: Bending at the waist and breaking body alignment.
Resting heavy compressive load on the neck.
safetyNotes: Never bear compressive weight on cervical spine.
contraindications: Acute lower back disc injury.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Weighted Full Front Lever Hold
steps: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulders.
Retract and depress your scapulae with locked straight elbows.
Pull down against the bar through your lats to raise your torso and legs.
Lock your entire body into a completely horizontal plane parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your glutes and quads tightly while holding the horizontal position steady.
tips: Generate intense straight-arm pulling torque through your latissimus dorsi.
Keep your body straight from shoulders to toes without sagging at the hips.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows to compensate for insufficient straight-arm lat strength.
Piking at the hips rather than maintaining a true horizontal line.
safetyNotes: Warm up your shoulders, elbows, and bicep tendons thoroughly prior to max holds.
contraindications: Distal biceps tendon strain or acute rotator cuff injury.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Weighted Wall-Assisted Handstand Push-Up
steps: Place your hands about eight inches away from a sturdy wall.
Kick up into a handstand with heels resting gently against the wall.
Establish an active hollow body position with your glutes and abs tight.
Lower your head forward slightly to touch your crown softly to the mat.
Form a stable tripod shape with your head positioned ahead of your hands.
Press hard through your palms and extend your arms to return to the full handstand.
tips: Avoid flaring your elbows wide; keep them tucked at a forty-five degree angle.
Push the floor away aggressively at the top into an active shoulder shrug.
commonMistakes: Collapsing your neck onto the floor with unbuffered velocity.
Banana-arching your lower back and resting your entire spine against the wall.
safetyNotes: Always place an exercise mat beneath your head to protect the cervical spine.
contraindications: High blood pressure, glaucoma, retinal detachment, or cervical spine disc injury.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Weighted Hanging Leg Raise
steps: Hang from an overhead pull-up bar with an overhand shoulder-width grip.
Depress your scapulae to engage your lats and eliminate passive swinging.
Point your toes, squeeze your legs together, and brace your core.
Raise your straight legs upward until your shins are parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top to emphasize lower abdominal contraction.
Lower your legs back down under strict muscular control to the dead hang.
tips: Posteriorly tilt your pelvis at the top to ensure your abs flex fully.
Do not swing your legs backward past the vertical plane between reps.
commonMistakes: Using pendulum momentum and arching your lower back to fling the legs up.
Bending knees excessively when performing the straight-leg variant.
safetyNotes: Control the lowering phase to avoid sudden lumbar hyperextension.
contraindications: Acute abdominal muscle strain or severe hip flexor tendinitis.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Weighted Hollow Body Hold
steps: Lie on your back on an exercise mat with arms and legs fully extended.
Press your lower back firmly into the floor so there is zero gap under your spine.
Lift your shoulder blades and legs two to four inches off the ground.
Reach your arms overhead past your ears while pointing your toes forward.
Maintain this continuous banana-shaped hollow body arc for the target hold duration.
tips: Your lower back must stay glued to the floor for the entire set.
Breathe shallowly through your diaphragm without releasing abdominal brace.
commonMistakes: Letting your lower back arch and lift off the floor under fatigue.
Craning your neck excessively forward rather than tucking your chin slightly.
safetyNotes: If your lower back begins peeling off the floor, regress by tucking your knees.
contraindications: Acute lumbar disc herniation aggravated by posterior pelvic tilt.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Weighted Inverted Row
steps: Lie under a waist-height bar and grasp with an overhand grip.
Extend legs forward with heels grounded and body in a straight plank.
Pull chest up to touch the bar by driving elbows back.
Lower body smoothly back to full arm extension.
tips: Keep body completely straight like an iron plank.
Retract shoulder blades fully at peak.
commonMistakes: Sagging hips toward the floor.
Poking chin forward to touch the bar.
safetyNotes: Adjust bar height to scale difficulty.
contraindications: Rotator cuff strain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Weighted Plyometric Jumping Lunge
steps: Begin in a lunge position with your right leg forward and knees bent ninety degrees.
Drop down quickly and explode vertically into the air off both feet.
Switch your leg positions in mid-air, bringing your left leg forward.
Land softly in a lunge with your left foot forward and absorb the impact smoothly.
Immediately drive up into the next repetition without pausing.
Continue alternating sides continuously for all prescribed repetitions.
tips: Use your arms to assist momentum by driving them opposite to your legs.
Keep your torso tall and center of gravity balanced between both legs.
commonMistakes: Letting the front knee collapse inward upon impact.
Banging the rear knee violently into the ground during descent.
safetyNotes: High impact plyometric: land softly toe-to-heel and never slam rear knee.
contraindications: Patellar tendinopathy, knee ligament reconstruction, or severe joint degeneration.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Weighted L-Sit Hold
steps: Mount parallel bars with straight locked arms and depressed shoulders.
Lift straight legs in front of you until parallel to the floor.
Point toes forward and squeeze quadriceps tightly.
Hold the strict L-shape for the target hold duration.
tips: Push the floor or bars away actively through palms.
Keep knees fully locked out straight.
commonMistakes: Bending knees due to weak hip flexors.
Shrugging shoulders into ears.
safetyNotes: Warm up wrists and shoulders thoroughly.
contraindications: Severe hip flexor tendinitis.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Weighted Lateral Skater Hops
steps: Stand balanced on your right foot with knees softly bent.
Bound laterally to the left off your right foot.
Land softly on your left foot, sweeping right leg behind you.
Absorb the impact and bound back immediately to the right.
Continue alternating sides continuously for the prescribed repetitions.
tips: Stay low in an athletic stance throughout the bounds.
Drive off the outside foot with power.
commonMistakes: Landing with a stiff knee or locked ankle.
Letting chest collapse downward.
safetyNotes: Land softly and check footing to prevent slips.
contraindications: Lateral ankle ligament sprain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Weighted Mountain Climber
steps: Start in a high plank position with hands beneath shoulders and body straight.
Drive your right knee up toward your chest while keeping hips low.
Quickly tap the ball of your right foot and jump it back to plank.
Simultaneously drive your left knee forward toward your chest.
Alternate your legs rapidly in a smooth running cadence.
Maintain a steady level pelvis without bouncing your hips up and down.
tips: Keep your shoulders pushed away from your ears to maintain upper back stability.
Land lightly on the balls of your feet during the foot transitions.
commonMistakes: Piking hips high up into the air to take tension off the core.
Letting hands drift forward ahead of the shoulders.
safetyNotes: Maintain core brace to prevent lower back sagging during rapid cadence.
contraindications: Acute toe joint sprain or symptomatic abdominal wall hernia.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Weighted Nordic Hamstring Curl
steps: Kneel on a padded mat with your ankles secured firmly under a support.
Align knees, hips, and shoulders in one rigid vertical line.
Lower torso forward toward the floor as slowly as possible using hamstrings.
Catch yourself on hands, push lightly, and pull back up with hamstrings.
tips: Resist gravity for as long as possible on the way down.
Keep hips extended without breaking at the waist.
commonMistakes: Bending at the hips to avoid hamstring loading.
Falling forward without muscular control.
safetyNotes: Cushion knees with thick padding.
contraindications: Acute hamstring strain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Weighted Parallel Bar Dip
steps: Mount the parallel bars and lock out your arms with shoulders depressed.
Lean your torso forward roughly fifteen degrees to engage your chest.
Bend your elbows to lower your body downward smoothly.
Descend until your shoulders are level with or slightly below your elbows.
Press through your palms to extend your arms back to the top support position.
tips: Keep your elbows tucked at roughly forty-five degrees rather than flared.
Maintain an active hollow body position with crossed or straight ankles.
commonMistakes: Dipping too shallow and cutting the range of motion in half.
Allowing your shoulders to shrug upward toward your ears under load.
safetyNotes: Avoid excessive downward depth if you experience anterior shoulder pain.
contraindications: Acute sternoclavicular joint injury or anterior glenohumeral instability.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Weighted Pistol Squat
steps: Stand balanced on your right leg and extend your left leg straight in front of you.
Reach your arms forward to counterbalance your center of mass.
Hinge your hips slightly and bend your right knee to descend smoothly.
Lower down fully until your right hamstring rests against your calf.
Keep your left heel elevated completely off the ground throughout.
Drive firmly through your right foot to stand back up to tall extension.
Switch and perform the same number of reps on your opposite left leg.
tips: Maintain deep ankle dorsiflexion and keep your heel planted firmly.
Round your upper back slightly to maintain forward counterbalance.
commonMistakes: Allowing your standing heel to lift off the floor during the descent.
Letting the elevated non-working leg touch the ground.
safetyNotes: Requires substantial ankle and knee integrity; progress using box support first.
contraindications: Severe patellofemoral osteoarthritis or recovering meniscus repair.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Weighted Plyometric Jump Squat
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and chest upright.
Hinge hips back and descend into a quarter-squat.
Explode vertically off the floor pushing through your midfoot.
Reach full triple extension in mid-air.
Land softly like a cat and absorb into the next squat repetition.
tips: Land softly toe-to-heel with bent knees to absorb impact.
Swing arms upward to add vertical momentum.
commonMistakes: Landing on stiff locked knees.
Collapsing knees inward upon landing.
safetyNotes: Land softly to absorb shock through musculature.
contraindications: Severe patellofemoral arthritis.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Weighted Standard Pull-Up
steps: Grip the overhead pull-up bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than your shoulders.
Hang at full arm extension in an active dead hang with engaged shoulder blades.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes into a hollow body shape.
Pull your elbows down toward your hips while driving your chest toward the bar.
Continue pulling smoothly until your chin clears the top edge of the bar.
Lower yourself under steady control back to the complete active hang.
tips: Initiate the pull by depressing your scapulae before bending your arms.
Keep your legs glued together to avoid leaking core tension.
commonMistakes: Kicking your legs or kipping with momentum to reach the top.
Shortening repetitions by failing to reach full arm lockout at the bottom.
safetyNotes: Do not relax into an inactive joint hang with limp shoulders at the bottom.
contraindications: Acute shoulder labrum tear or severe golfer elbow flare-up.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Weighted Push-Up
steps: Set hands slightly wider than shoulders on the floor.
Keep feet together and form a rigid straight plank line.
Lower body smoothly until chest hovers just off the floor.
Press the ground away forcefully to complete arm lockout.
tips: Keep elbows angled at forty-five degrees like an arrow.
Squeeze glutes to protect lower spine.
commonMistakes: Sagging hips toward the mat during descent.
Flaring elbows wide at ninety degrees.
safetyNotes: Keep wrists stacked comfortably.
contraindications: Acute wrist sprain.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Weighted Agility Shuttle Runs
steps: Start in an athletic three-point stance behind the baseline.
Sprint at full speed five yards forward to touch the line.
Pivot sharply and sprint back to the baseline.
Immediately turn and sprint ten yards to the far marker.
Touch down with your hand and sprint hard through the finish.
tips: Lower your center of mass before planting to change direction.
Keep steps quick and responsive.
commonMistakes: Slipping on turn-around points due to high center of mass.
Standing upright before decelerating.
safetyNotes: Ensure surface is dry and free of debris.
contraindications: Groin adductor tear.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Weighted Six-Count Military Burpee
steps: Stand tall; drop into a squat and place palms flat on the floor.
Kick both feet back into a rigid plank position.
Lower chest smoothly to touch the floor in a push-up.
Push back up to full plank extension.
Jump feet forward outside hands and jump explosively overhead.
tips: Keep each movement distinct and crisp like military drill.
Breathe out forcefully on the push-up drive.
commonMistakes: Sagging hips during the plank and push-up.
Landing on stiff straight legs.
safetyNotes: Maintain core brace to protect lumbar spine.
contraindications: Severe shoulder instability.

verification.notes: Verified by independent factual rules and Compendium mapping.

name: Weighted High-Intensity Sprint Intervals
steps: Accelerate aggressively out of an athletic split stance.
Drive knees high and pump elbows back and forth in rhythm.
Maintain a forward torso lean originating from the ankles.
Strike the ground with the balls of your feet directly under hips.
Sprint at maximal effort for the prescribed interval duration.
tips: Keep shoulders and face relaxed as you sprint.
Drive arms forcefully to power leg turnover.
commonMistakes: Overstriding with heavy braking heel strikes.
Tightening jaw and hunching shoulders.
safetyNotes: Warm up thoroughly before full-speed sprints.
contraindications: Acute hamstring strain.

name: Weighted Chest-to-Floor Burpee
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and arms hanging naturally.
Hinge your hips back and place both hands flat on the floor.
Kick your feet back simultaneously into a high plank position.
Lower your chest and thighs completely onto the floor in one smooth wave.
Push the floor away and jump your feet forward just outside your hands.
Jump explosively into the air, clapping your hands overhead with body extended.
tips: Land with soft knees and transition immediately into your next descent.
Breathe rhythmically on every single repetition.
commonMistakes: Landing on stiff locked knees during the overhead jump landing.
Letting your lower back sag into a painful hyper-extended arch.
safetyNotes: Absorb landing impact through soft knees and ankles to protect joint cartilage.
contraindications: Severe patellofemoral osteoarthritis or severe vertigo.
